  • Nobody uses the engine's kinds. The reef has Topic and Queue, both reconciled by nats; the cluster holds none of either.
  • Triton does not use the reef. It opens its own JetStream streams (rooms.<room>, controllers/triton/rooms.py) and two KV buckets (orders, agents) in a NATS account of its own, AGENTS.
  • The engine knows its client by name. A Mandate's agents=true makes the nats Nereid write the account AGENTS and the user triton.
  • Triton declares no required reef in its image, though it needs the NATS the nats Nereid runs.
  • Triton reconciles no kind, so nereus nereid list shows it NotConformant: a Nereid reconciles every kind of each reef it looks after (#2065), and a Room kind in messaging would make nats not conformant instead.
  • A session's presence is a key in the bucket agents, one revision per change of state; its heartbeats stay in memory.

So the engine's swap kept nothing: the rooms were NATS streams by another name. What an agent on another machine lives through is the same whatever the shape: the CLI's bridge, the Nereus API, Triton, over HTTPS; no machine reaches NATS (#1599).

ADR 0018 makes the Nereus API the one door, and ADR 0029 has the API serve /mcp with the tools the reefs declare in their contract.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The measure of the feature (owner, 2026-11-22): a Nereus user creates a room, and their agent joins it beside a teammate's agent. No extra configuration, no paperwork, no request to an admin, no change to Nereus's settings. Every step below is checked against it, and an end-to-end scene with two ordinary users, neither of them an admin, is its acceptance test.

The flow, as a person lives it:

  1. Ana creates the room: nereus rooms create ops. Without a name, the room takes the repository's name; without --owner, her own team (the token's nereus_owner). The API checks that she may create it, as it checks a Topic.
  2. Triton sees the Room and asks the messaging reef for a Topic room-ops; the nats Nereid makes the stream and a NATS user of the owner, and gives the credential back in a binding beside the Topic; Triton opens the room with it. The Room is Ready, with no agent in it.
  3. Ana and Bruno each run nereus rooms list, see ops, and run nereus rooms join ops. The join registers their Peer with ops in spec.rooms.
  4. When a room goes from no agent to one, a new room session starts; it ends when the last agent leaves, and its data is kept for analysis afterwards (below).
  5. Their agents post and read through the CLI's MCP server, the API and Triton; a hook brings each new message into the session's context.

Who may create a Room is the authorization reef's answer on the Room's spec.owner, and the profile installs what lets a member of a team create Rooms owned by that team (owner, 2026-11-22): a grant of the authorization reef, either a Role and its Binding seeded with the reef or a rule the openfga Nereid computes, as it does for a Session's staff (#1727); #1491 settles which. It is a setting of the installation, made once, not a request to an admin: without it only nereus-admins could create a Room, and the measure of the feature would fail. Policies will refine it later (owner, 2026-11-22), outside the journey #2067, as the hard and soft gates of Thinking in Platforms: a hard gate refuses, a soft gate lets an ordinary user ask and waits for an admin's approval, the Room standing in a pending phase (its name to be decided) until then; which part is the authorization engine's (OpenFGA) and which is a policy's is to be worked out.

nereus rooms join is one command, wherever it runs (owner, 2026-11-22). It takes the room as its argument, the repository's name without one, and nereus rooms session create and its --room go:

  • Outside Claude Code, it does what session create did: it draws the agent's name, registers the Peer and opens Claude Code with the Nereus MCP server's rooms tools on.
  • Inside Claude Code (the variable CLAUDECODE, which Claude Code sets in the processes it starts), it draws the agent's name when the session has none, registers the Peer, and turns the rooms tools on in that session, with no restart.
$ nereus rooms join ops          # outside Claude Code
starting doto with claude-code: in the room ops on Triton

$ nereus rooms join              # inside, in the repository nereus
doto joined the room nereus

$ nereus rooms leave ops
doto left the room ops

An agent leaves a room two ways (owner, 2026-11-22): nereus rooms leave <room> takes the room off its Peer at once, inside or outside Claude Code as join does, so an agent changes rooms with its session open; and its session ending takes it out of every room (the heartbeats stop, the Peer goes Away).

A room session is a RoomSession in the cluster (owner, 2026-11-22, narrowed 2026-11-23 in #2100). Beside its Room and written by Triton, it says who came and went, when, and how many messages were posted. Its messages stay on the Topic while the Topic's own retention (maxAge, short) keeps them: no file, no Drive and no automatic delete. Keeping the history goes with #1269 (history out of etcd) and #2099 (the observability reef, VictoriaLogs first, Drive as an export).

The CLI is the agent's MCP server, with groups of tools (owner, 2026-11-22: "the Nereus MCP server with different tools that can be turned on or not by calling the CLI"). Today session create passes the bridge (--mcp-config) and the pull hooks (--settings) to each Claude Code it opens, so a session already open cannot join. Instead:

  • nereus mcp local add registers, once and in the user's scope, one MCP server, nereus mcp local serve, and the hooks, as claude mcp add does for any server; nereus rooms join runs it when it is missing.
  • The server's tools come in groups, rooms the first; nereus mcp local list shows them, nereus mcp local enable and disable turn one on or off, and join turns rooms on for its session. When a group changes, the server tells Claude Code (notifications/tools/list_changed, of the MCP protocol), so tools appear and go with the session open.
  • The hooks call the CLI and print nothing while the session is in no room.
  • The rooms group is today's bridge: it holds the person's token (refreshed, never in the session's argv or environment), names the agent in Nereus-Agent, lets through the peer tools only, and sends the heartbeat that makes the Peer Ready; with the session in no room it sends none.

This server is local and serves an agent on its machine; the API's /mcp below is a remote one, for a person in claude.ai. The word local keeps the two apart in the CLI (owner, 2026-11-22): nereus mcp tool and nereus mcp client stay the remote /mcp's.

Two small reefs, composed (owner, 2026-11-21). messaging is the engine's reef: Topic and Queue, looked after by nats. rooms is the conversation's reef: Room and Peer, looked after by triton. Each Nereid reconciles every kind of its reef, with no exemption. Triton looks after rooms only: messaging leaves its spec.reefs and stays as the reef it requires, so it never answers for Topic or Queue.

Triton knows the contract, not the engine (owner, 2026-11-21: "it only needs to understand the contract and depend on the reef"). Its image declares requires=messaging, as keycloak's declares secrets, so a profile installs the engine first and refuses to leave it out. There are two planes:

  • The control plane is the reef's contract. For each Room, Triton applies a Topic named room-<room>, owned by the Room, with the Room's spec.owner, and reads the binding the reef gives back. It opens no stream of its own.
  • A Room has an owner, an Organization or a Project of the tenancy tree (ADR 0015), as a Topic has, and it cannot change (owner, 2026-11-21, #2073): its Topic takes it, so each team's room lives in that owner's NATS account, and the API checks a Room as it checks a Topic, on its spec.owner.
  • Rooms live in the namespace nereus-rooms (owner, 2026-11-21, #2073: "create a room and join it with your teammates", so a new Room works at once, with no list to change): a Room's Topic sits beside it, the reef writes a Topic's binding in the Topic's own namespace, and Triton reads Secrets there only, never in nereus-system.
  • The Mandate stays the only routing key (#2065). Triton names no engine and no Nereid in a Topic (a Topic's spec.engine is optional, #2073): the messaging reef's Mandate picks who reconciles it, and the binding's provider only reports who did.
  • One writer per field (ADR 0005). A Room's Topic is Triton's to ask for: Triton alone writes its spec, as keycloak writes the Release it requires, and nats writes its status and its binding.
  • The data plane is an adapter chosen by the binding's provider. A room needs four operations of an engine: open, read the last sequence, append only if the last sequence is still the expected one, and read after a cursor. One adapter exists, for NATS. A second engine asks for a second adapter, and that is the whole of "swapping the engine keeps the rooms".

What a room asks of a Topic. Its messages are kept, in order, each with a sequence, and a reader starts after a sequence; the Topic carries its own retention (spec.maxAge, spec.maxBytes). Its binding carries a credential of its owner, and the Topic is closed to every other client (spec.access: owner): in a room, the sender of a message is the agent Triton checked, so Triton stays the only writer.

A Peer is an agent's session in the rooms (owner, 2026-11-21). Its name is <owner>.<agent>. One writer per field (ADR 0005): the session writes spec through the API (owner, a {kind: User, name} as ADR 0015 and ADR 0027 name a person; agent; tool; rooms, a list from the start, so an agent in several rooms changes no schema). Triton writes status (phase: Arriving, Ready or Away; since), and only when the phase changes: a heartbeat never writes the object. An Away Peer is deleted after 24 hours. A person who posts from the CLI or from claude.ai is not a Peer: a person has no presence.

The orders' code leaves Triton (owner, 2026-11-21). Orders have been off since #1440. Their code is what else keeps Triton on NATS directly; the idea stays in #2068.

Everything reaches Triton through the Nereus API. Triton keeps no public /mcp and no OAuth of its own: the bridge's calls (the heartbeat, whoami, a post and a read as an agent) and the person's (the peers and a read as a person) all go through the API. Triton stays an internal service.

The internal door. Triton serves HTTP only in the cluster (a ClusterIP Service and a NetworkPolicy). The API calls it with its own ServiceAccount token, which Triton checks by TokenReview and admits only for the API's ServiceAccount. The API passes the person (sub, groups, nereus_owner) and the agent the bridge names (Nereus-Agent) in headers, and Triton keeps its peer_call check: the agent is a Peer of the person's.

The API's Principal gains agent, read from Nereus-Agent, so the audit log says "person X, agent Y, via mcp" or "via cli". No token goes on to Triton (no passthrough) and none is exchanged: the API checked the person, and Triton trusts the API.

The bridge talks REST. The CLI's MCP server (its rooms group, the bridge) turns its local tools and its heartbeat into calls on /v1/rooms/... with the nereus login token (aud: nereus-api, #1320), so the separate login of the triton client goes.

/mcp lists only what serves a person in claude.ai: rooms_peers and rooms_read (GET, on by default) and rooms_post (POST, off until an admin turns it on, ADR 0029).

The names:

What Name The reef of the conversation rooms, API group rooms.<domain>/v1alpha1 Its kinds Room (the reef's default kind), Peer, RoomSession, all namespaced, as Topic is; Rooms in nereus-rooms Its Nereid triton, whose image declares requires=messaging The engine's reef messaging: Topic, Queue, Nereid nats A Room's Topic room-<room>, owned by its Room A Room's fields spec.owner, spec.description, spec.maxAge, spec.maxBytes, spec.deletionPolicy; status.topic A Peer's name <owner>.<agent> A Peer's fields spec.owner, spec.agent, spec.tool, spec.rooms; status.phase, status.since A Topic's new fields spec.maxAge, spec.maxBytes, spec.access (shared, the default, or owner) CLI nereus rooms create, apply, list, get, delete, join, leave; nereus rooms peer list, get; nereus rooms follow, pull, post; nereus rooms session list, get; nereus mcp local add, serve, list, enable, disable The agent's MCP server nereus mcp local serve, its groups of tools, rooms the first A room's activity a room session, from the first agent in to the last one out: kind RoomSession, written by Triton; its messages on the Topic while its retention keeps them (#1269, #2099 keep the history) Routes /v1/rooms/... MCP tools rooms_peers, rooms_read, rooms_post 
$ nereus rooms create ops --description "Operations peers"
✓ rooms/rooms/ops created

$ nereus messaging topic list
NAME      OWNER  READY  AGE
room-ops  ops    True   5s

$ nereus rooms list
NAME  OWNER  AGENTS  READY
ops   ops    0       True

$ nereus rooms join ops
starting doto with claude-code: in the room ops on Triton

$ nereus rooms peer list
NAME      ROOMS  PHASE  SINCE
ana.doto  ops    Ready  10:02:11

The options weighed:

Option What it is Against One Nereid for one reef nats and triton merged, reconciling Topic, Queue and Room Two code bases merged; a second engine's Nereid would have to do rooms too The conversation alone One reef with Room only, Topic and Queue removed, NATS inside Triton Drops the nats Nereid already built and the queue a Workload will ask for No engine Rooms kept in the Kubernetes API or in SQLite The rooms' storage and the asks rewritten, with nothing an agent would notice Triton on NATS directly, said so Today's code, the ADR saying "rooms on NATS" The engine keeps a parameter for one client, and Triton depends on a Nereid, not on a reef The messaging name for the conversation messaging holds Room, the engine moves to a new reef Moves the kinds ADR 0017 named; the owner is the only user of the session commands, so renaming those is the cheaper side Two reefs, Triton on the reef's contract Above A Room costs a Topic and a binding, and the Topic's contract grows by retention and a credential

On the door, weighed on 2026-11-18 and unchanged:

Option What it is Against Token passthrough to Triton The API forwards the person's token MCP forbids it; Triton would check a token issued for another audience Token exchange (RFC 8693) The API trades the person's token for one of Triton's audience A second issuer path and client in the realm for a call that never leaves the cluster The API on the engine, no Triton The API reads and writes the rooms itself Presence, peer_call and the asks move into the API, which then depends on the engine The bridge over /mcp The CLI calls the API's MCP tools /mcp is the person's door (ADR 0029, aud: nereus-mcp); the CLI already holds a nereus-api token for REST Internal door, bridge on REST Above A second hop inside the cluster, and Triton must trust the API's headers

docs.title: Prior art
docs.text:
• Service Binding Specification for Kubernetes (servicebinding.io): a binding is a Secret whose type entry "identifies the abstract classification of the binding" and whose provider entry "identifies the provider of the binding", beside well-known entries such as host, port, uri, username and password. Triton picks its adapter by provider, and reads the rest.
  • Kubernetes Leases (kubernetes.io): a kubelet's heartbeats are updates of a small Lease object. A Peer goes one step further for the same reason: the heartbeat is kept in memory, and only a change of phase is written.
  • Kubernetes API aggregation, request header authentication (kubernetes.io): the API server authenticates the person and proxies to an extension API server with the user and groups in headers, which that server trusts only from the front proxy's identity; the same split as Triton trusting the API.
  • Kubernetes TokenReview (kubernetes.io): a service checks a ServiceAccount token with the cluster, with no secret of its own.
  • MCP Security Best Practices (modelcontextprotocol.io): no token passthrough to the services behind an MCP server.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
The journey #2067 carries the change, all at once, in steps that each fit one agent's context:

Under #1812, with the names above: #1895 (the internal door, the API's /v1/rooms routes and Principal.agent), #1896 (the bridge on REST), #1897 (Triton's contract declares the three tools) and #1898 (Triton's public /mcp, its OAuth, the triton and triton-door clients, the claude.ai Triton connector and the NATS auth callout all go; the cloudflared tunnel stays).

  • Triton is NotConformant from #2072 until #2073 and #2074 are both merged: the contract saying what is missing, not a defect.
  • The old streams rooms.<room> of the account AGENTS are not migrated: a room's messages are short-lived coordination.
  • The audience nereus-mcp stays: it names the token /mcp accepts.
  • Until v1.0.0 this ADR is rewritten in place when the decision changes (ADR 0001).

docs.title: 2070: a Topic keeps its messages by its own spec, maxAge and maxBytes.
2071: a Topic's binding carries its owner's credential, so only the owner publishes.
2072: the rooms reef and its two kinds; triton looks after it and requires messaging; no kind of either reef joins the list of exempt kinds, which #2066 freezes.
2073: Triton reconciles Room: the Topic, the binding, the adapter.
1491: the Room's verbs in the CLI and the bound on rooms per installation.
2074: Triton reconciles Peer, and the bucket agents goes.
2075: a Peer's rooms: nereus rooms join, outside and inside Claude Code, and the bridge and the pull hook over several rooms (rewritten 2026-11-22: no --room, no .nereus/room file).
2101: nereus mcp local, the CLI as the agent's MCP server, its tools in groups, rooms the first.
2100: the room sessions, RoomSession, read with nereus rooms session list and get (narrowed on 2026-11-23: no file on Drive).
1491 also carries who may create a Room (a team member, their team's Rooms); the hard and soft gates are #2102, outside the journey.
2076: the CLI's surface moves to nereus rooms; #1889: a person posts with nereus rooms post.
2078: the nats Nereid loses agents=true, the account AGENTS and the user triton.
2079: the docs and the peers protocol say rooms.
Origin
docs.text: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-18, refining #1812 (Triton's tools served by the Nereus API's /mcp) one question at a time: the door, the bridge, the tools. Decided again on 2026-11-21, evaluating the messaging reef one question at a time: the two reefs, the name rooms, Triton on the reef's contract, the Peer kind, the orders' code, and one journey for all of it (#2067). Decided again on 2026-11-22, the flow as a person lives it, one question at a time: the measure of the feature, who may create a Room, nereus rooms join and leave, the room sessions and what they keep, and the CLI's MCP server. Narrowed on 2026-11-23 (#2100, #2079, the owner's word): a room session keeps no file on Drive.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• A RoomSession's retention in the cluster, and where a room's history is kept: #1269 (history out of etcd).
  • Later, most likely, a room session's logs and metrics go to the observability reef, VictoriaLogs first and Drive as an export (owner, 2026-11-22): #2099, outside this journey.
  • Whether Claude Code applies notifications/tools/list_changed in an open session: checked before the CLI's MCP server is built.

  • The hard and soft gates on creating a Room: the pending phase's name, and what is OpenFGA's and what a policy's (#2102).

  • How orders arrive if they come back: #2068.

  • Who may join a room: any member of the team group for now; a room's own members wait for the teams reef (#1307).
  • How NATS learns a Topic's new user without a restart (#2071, #600).
  • The rooms reef's Mandate carries the bound on rooms per installation (maxRooms, 20 by default): its value on the kept cluster is the owner's (#1491).

Extended 2026-11-22 with the flow as a person lives it (#2067); raw data in #pontos/raw/2026-11-22/. Rewritten 2026-11-21 from the owner's evaluation of the messaging reef (#2067, #2069); raw data in #pontos/raw/2026-11-21/. First written 2026-11-18 (#1893); raw data in #pontos/raw/2026-11-18/.

docs.title: 0031. Gates and approvals native to Nereus: a hard gate refuses, a soft gate holds the object Pending until an approver decides
docs.text:
In short

Any resource created through the Nereus API can be refused (a hard gate, 403 as today) or held: under a soft gate, a person with the right to ask creates the object, which stands visibly Pending until an approver approves or rejects it through the API; with no list of approvers, whoever may create that kind there approves. Two kinds in the authorization reef, Gate and Approval, one hold annotation, one admission policy, and no flow written per kind. Status: Accepted (2026-11-24).

Status: Accepted (2026-11-24, by the owner)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The platform's controls are all or nothing: the Nereus API asks the authorization reef before every write (ADR 0027, #1649), and the answer is yes, or a 403. Teams need a middle path, "you may ask, someone decides", and two issues asked for it from two sides: #2102 (hard and soft gates on creating a Room) and #2044 (change classes by blast radius).

If each reef wrote its own approval flow, every kind would grow a different one: its own pending state, its own notification, its own idea of who decides. The owner's requirement (2026-11-22) rules that out: "the Environment was only an example; it should hold for practically any resource created through Nereus, so we do not implement different, custom flows for each resource; this control becomes a native feature of Nereus."

Two more requirements come from the same decision:

  • The object exists while it waits. The custom resource is created at once and stays Pending, "so whoever asked sees that it is pending, can follow it and tell the approvers"; no hold at the door that keeps the object out of the cluster.
  • The requester is told. When a resource they asked for is approved or rejected, and then when it is provisioned or fails.

What makes it possible without touching each reef: every route of api/server.py already declares its Asks (reef, kinds, verb, the node it writes under) for the Authorizer of api/authorization.py, so the API knows, before any write, which reef, kind and verb a request is about.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Hard and soft, in the owner's sense of #2102. A hard gate refuses: the person has no right to the verb, and the API answers 403, as spec 0011 does today. A soft gate lets a person ask: the person has the right to request the verb, the API writes the object held, and an approver decides.

Three answers for one write. When a write reaches the API, after the Authorizer:

person ── nereus <reef> <kind> create ──▶ Nereus API (the route wrappers of api/server.py)
  ├─ may create?                                  yes ─▶ written as today
  ├─ may request, and a Gate matches reef/kind/verb?
  │    no ─▶ 403, as today (a hard gate)
  │    yes ─▶ the object is written WITH the hold, and an Approval beside it
  │         ├─ the gate Nereid writes the object's status: Pending, Ready=False WaitingApproval
  │         ├─ the notifications reef tells the approvers and the requester
  │         └─ approver ── nereus authorization approval approve|reject ──▶ the API records the decision
  │              ├─ approved: the API lifts the hold ─▶ the kind's own Nereid reconciles as usual
  │              │     └─ the gate Nereid follows Ready until it is provisioned or fails ─▶ notified
  │              └─ rejected: the gate Nereid marks the object Rejected; nothing is provisioned ─▶ notified
  └─ admission (one ValidatingAdmissionPolicy for every reef kind): only the API sets or lifts the hold and
     writes an Approval's spec; while the hold is on, only the gate Nereid writes the object's status or finalizers

A person who may create is not held: the bindings decide who goes straight through (create), who may ask (request) and who is refused (neither). A request with no Gate to match is refused, since nobody would decide it.

docs.title: The API group: two kinds in the authorization reef
docs.text:
Both live in authorization.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, beside Role and Binding (ADR 0027), and, like them, are objects the Nereus API keeps.

Gate: which requests wait, and for whom. Owned by a node of the tenancy tree, as a Binding is, and holding for that node and the nodes under it.

apiVersion: authorization.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Gate
metadata:
  name: payments-environments
spec:
  owner: {kind: Project, name: payments}
  reef: environment
  kinds: [environments]
  verbs: [create]                       # create only, for now
  approvers:                            # optional: the subjects a Binding takes (ADR 0027)
    - team/payments/tech-lead
  expires: 7d                           # optional; default from the authorization Mandate's approvalExpires

Who approves (owner, 2026-11-24). Whoever may create the held kind at the target's node, or at a node above it (every right of ADR 0027 is inherited), may approve, always: they could have created the object themselves. spec.approvers is optional: it adds subjects who may approve without holding create (a FinOps or a security team) and names who is told, so no request waits on an empty position. A Gate with no list is approved by the holders of create alone, the administrators included. Nobody approves their own request by default, since whoever holds create is never held. Creating or changing a Gate whose list names approvers requires create on its kinds at its node, so nobody grants through a Gate what they could not do themselves; nereus authorization gate create warns when the instance's root is the only possible approver.

Approval: one per held request. Its spec is written only by the Nereus API, its status only by the gate Nereid (ADR 0005). It carries an ownerReference to the held object, so it goes away with it.

apiVersion: authorization.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Approval
metadata:
  name: staging-create-7f3a             # <target>-<verb>-<4 hex>
spec:
  gate: payments-environments
  target: {reef: environment, kind: environments, name: staging}
  verb: create
  requestedBy: <User id>                # never an e-mail
  decisions:                            # a list, so a quorum fits later
    - {by: <User id>, decision: approved, at: "2026-11-24T14:02:00Z", reason: "sprint demo"}
status:
  phase: Approved                       # Pending | Approved | Rejected | Expired
  conditions:
    - {type: Provisioned, status: "True", reason: Ready}   # the target's Ready, once approved

The hold is one annotation on the held object, authorization.getnereus.dev/approval: <Approval name>, set by the API when it writes the object and lifted only by the API when the Approval is approved. A rejected or expired object keeps it.

docs.title: Who writes what (ADR 0005, one writer per field)
docs.text:
Field Writer the held object's spec, the hold annotation the Nereus API an Approval's spec, its decisions[] included the Nereus API the held object's status and finalizers, while the hold is on the gate Nereid the held object's status, once the hold is lifted the kind's own Nereid, as usual an Approval's status the gate Nereid

The gate Nereid is the Nereid of the authorization reef's default Mandate (the openfga Nereid in an install, the reference Nereid in make scene-core). While the hold is on it writes the held object's status.phase: Pending and the condition Ready=False, reason WaitingApproval, with a message that names the Approval and who may approve (with no list: whoever may create environment/environments at project/payments). After a rejection it writes phase: Rejected, Ready=False, reason Rejected; at expiry phase: Expired, reason Expired. Once the hold is lifted it stops writing the object and follows its Ready into the Approval's Provisioned condition, which the notifications read.

A Nereid never acts on a held object. The Nereid SDK skips any object that carries the hold, every Nereid adopts it, and a conformance test proves it (step 3 of #2117).

While held, the object does not change. The API refuses an apply on a held object (409, naming its Approval); a delete by the requester withdraws the request, and the Approval goes with the object.

Rejection and expiry keep the history in ADR 0026's shape: the phase stays until delete, and nothing is provisioned. An Approval expires at the Gate's expires (the authorization Mandate's parameter approvalExpires, 7d by default).

docs.title: The seam in the API
docs.text: The route wrappers of api/server.py, right after the Authorizer of api/authorization.py. Every route already declares its Asks; the wrapper finds the Gates that match the route's reef, kinds and verb at its node, asks request when create was refused, and writes the hold and the Approval. No reef's route changes, so a new kind gets approvals by configuration only: a Gate naming it.

docs.title: The verbs (an amendment to ADR 0013)
docs.text:
• request is a right, not a command. It appears in a Role's rules (environment:environments:request) and in can-i (nereus authorization can-i request environment/environments). A person who may request but not create runs the ordinary create and gets a held object.
  • approve and reject are commands of the approval kind: nereus authorization approval approve <name> --reason <text> and reject, each recording one decision. The API asks, for the approver, the same check as for a creation: create on the target's reef and kind at the target's node; a Gate's listed approvers are answered by the openfga Nereid's model (step 7 of #2117).
  • can-i says when a person may ask: no, but may ask: authorization/gates/<name> holds create for <approvers>'s approval, with exit code 1, since the answer to create is still no.

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
$ nereus environment create staging --owner project/payments
✓ environment/environments/staging created, waiting for approval (authorization/approvals/staging-create-7f3a; approvers: team/payments/tech-lead)

Next steps:

  nereus environment get staging --watch

$ nereus environment get staging
NAME      PHASE     READY   REASON            AGE
staging   Pending   False   WaitingApproval   2m

$ nereus authorization approval list
NAME                  TARGET                             VERB     REQUESTED BY   PHASE     AGE
staging-create-7f3a   environment/environments/staging   create   bruno          Pending   2m

$ nereus authorization approval approve staging-create-7f3a --reason "sprint demo"
✓ authorization/approvals/staging-create-7f3a approved; environment/environments/staging released

$ nereus authorization approval reject staging-create-7f3a --reason "use the shared staging"
✓ authorization/approvals/staging-create-7f3a rejected; environment/environments/staging will not be provisioned

$ nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments --owner project/payments --user bruno
no, but may ask: authorization/gates/payments-environments holds create for team/payments/tech-lead's approval

$ nereus authorization gate create payments-environments \
    --reef environment \
    --kinds environments \
    --verbs create \
    --approvers team/payments/tech-lead \
    --owner project/payments
✓ authorization/gates/payments-environments created

docs.title: Admission
docs.text: One ValidatingAdmissionPolicy for every reef kind (the groups *.getnereus.dev), built as the existing policies of cli/src/nereus/cluster.py are (step 2 of #2117): only the Nereus API's ServiceAccount sets, changes or removes the hold annotation and writes an Approval's spec; while the hold is on, only the gate Nereid's ServiceAccount writes the object's status or finalizers.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
The lists come first, read from the API: the portal's Approvals screen (#2126) shows a requester all of their requests with their phase until the outcome, and an approver the pending requests they may decide, with a count, refreshed while the screen is open; no push is needed to see them.

The pushes come from the conditions, through the notifications reef (#2147: a Notification for a person, a Subscription per device): the gate Nereid writes one Notification per transition of an Approval: "waiting for approval" to the approvers and the requester, "approved", "rejected" or "expired" on the decision, "provisioned" or "failed" from the Provisioned condition. The webpush Nereid delivers them (#2148) to the portal's PWA (#2149), whose service worker has no push yet; Android first, the permission asked in context after the first request, the payload only the name and the phase, opening the decision. --watch on the CLI reads the object's status. Voice and phone come later, with #278; the messaging reef (ADR 0019, #254) may carry the same events later.

docs.title: Prior art
docs.text:
• Kubernetes Pod scheduling readiness (Pod Scheduling Readiness): a Pod created with schedulingGates exists and is visible, but is not scheduled until every gate is removed; the hold annotation takes the same shape, an object that exists and waits, released by removing a mark.
  • Kubernetes certificate signing requests (Certificates and Certificate Signing Requests): a request object that an approver approves or denies with kubectl certificate approve and kubectl certificate deny, recorded as conditions; Approval and the approve and reject commands follow it.
  • GitHub deployment environments with required reviewers (Managing environments for deployment): a job that targets a protected environment waits until a required reviewer approves or rejects it, and the reviewers are people or teams; the Gate's approvers take teams the same way.
  • Kubernetes ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (Validating Admission Policy): CEL rules evaluated in the API server; one policy guards the hold for every reef kind.
  • Kaspar von Grünberg and Luca Galante, Thinking in Platforms (2026, docs/thinking-in-platforms.md): the owner's proposal that started this ADR, Hard Gates, Soft Gates and protected approval in Nereus, was written while reading it; the words hard and soft are used here in the owner's sense of #2102, and the book's own wording on gates is not yet in the notes.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The authorization reef gains Gate and Approval, and its Nereid gains a second job: the gate Nereid, the first Nereid that writes the status of objects of other reefs, and only while they are held.
  • ADR 0005 holds with one handover: while the hold is on, the gate Nereid is the one writer of the held object's status; the kind's own Nereid writes it from the moment the hold is lifted.
  • ADR 0013 gains the right request and the commands approve and reject of the approval kind.
  • Every Nereid moves to an SDK that skips held objects (step 3 of #2117); a Nereid outside the SDK that ignores the hold could still act outside the cluster before trying to write. The admission refuses any trace of it in the cluster, step 3's conformance test catches it before install, and #894 and #86 narrow it further.
  • The API becomes the one writer of decisions, which raises the weight of #1500 (the API never writes the admission policies that guard it).
  • A new kind gets approvals by a Gate alone; Room is the proof (#2102, step 10 of #2117).
  • The steps of #2117 build it: the walking skeleton on an Environment (#2119), the admission policy (#2120), the SDK filter (#2121), rejection and expiry (#2122), notifications (#2123), can-i and --dry-run (#2124), the openfga rights (#2125), the portal and MCP (#2126), the metrics (#2127) and Room (#2102).

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: A quorum of several approvers (later: decisions[] already fits it), change classes by blast radius or cost (#2044, a later extension of Gate), the policy reef with kyverno (#898), segregation of duties and an audit log nobody can rewrite (#241), cloud access approvals (#259), contextual conditions by IP or time of day, e-mail or chat pushes, gates on apply and delete, a count in the portal's navigation before the Approvals screen opens (an amendment to ADR 0022).

docs.title: Origin
docs.text: The owner's proposal of 2026-11-22 (Hard Gates, Soft Gates and protected approval in Nereus), analysed by a Fable agent and reshaped into journey #2117 the same day; the design was closed by the owner on 2026-11-22 its verbs approved on 2026-11-24, and this ADR accepted by the owner the same day (#2118, PR #2202). Raw data in #pontos/raw/2026-11-22/ and #pontos/raw/2026-11-24/.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• A requester among a Gate's listed approvers: may they approve their own request? Nothing refuses it today; segregation of duties belongs to #241. The default approvers never include the requester.
  • A hold whose Approval is missing (the API wrote the object and failed before the Approval): the gate Nereid's reason for it, and whether the API retries or removes the object; step 1 decides.

Rewritten 2026-11-24 from the owner's decisions after a second opinion (#2117): with no list, whoever may create the kind at the target's node approves; listed approvers add to them; a Gate's list needs create on its kinds; the lists come before the pushes, which go through the notifications reef (#2147). Raw data in #pontos/raw/2026-11-24/.

docs.title: Agent guides
docs.text:
One page per topic, read on demand. CLAUDE.md stays small and points here, so a session loads only the guide it needs.

  • The CLI design: reef, Nereid, Mandate, the commands, legacy commands mapped.
  • How the owner works: voice, pt-BR, spoken summaries, the visual companion, the terminal format.
  • Rules: the durable rules and the pillars.
  • The queue: the board and how issues are registered.
  • Layout: where things live in the repository.
  • Worktrees: one git worktree per agent run, its name and its cleanup.
  • How we work: good enough first, open source first, the languages.
  • Issues: GitHub Issues are the backlog.
  • Raw data: where the recordings and dumps of the sessions live.
  • ADRs: how to write a decision.
  • API groups: every new idea starts as an API group (proposed rule).
  • Decks: the rules for a deck or an HTML page, from the deck engine, and for screens used from a phone.
  • Beach: Glaucus, the messenger between the voice session and the local agent.
  • Peers: the other sessions on this repository, and the resources they share (the protocol and the room skill live in the owner's linux repository).
  • Saving tokens: the token practices, their hooks and how to tell whether they worked.
  • AI and teams: the AI accelerates, people set the direction and decide (Paulo Caroli).
  • The session prompt: rewritten with /next save before every /clear, loaded after it, STALE when not rewritten.
  • The status bar: each piece of the bar under the prompt, and what the forecast asks of the session.
  • Publishing on ghcr.io: make promote, and the click that makes a new package public.

docs.title: ADRs
docs.text:
ADR 0001 (record architecture decisions) is the rule; this page is the checklist.

  • One file per decision: docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md, the next free number on main, and its line in the Decisions section of mkdocs.yml.
  • A number is valid only once the ADR is merged (ADR 0001): a draft in a branch, a PR or a work order is named by its title, never by a number. Right before the merge, check the next free number on main again, and rename the file and its links if another ADR took it.
  • Nygard format: Title, Status, Context, Decision, ## Prior art (credits, #332), Consequences.
  • Origin: when and by whom the decision was taken, and the path of the raw file it came from (see Raw data), without personal names.
  • Status starts Proposed; only the owner moves it to Accepted.
  • Until v1.0.0, a changed decision rewrites its ADR in place: keep the number, rename the file to the new words when they changed, fix every link, and end it with *Rewritten <date> from <source>; raw data in <path>.*. From v1.0.0 on, an accepted ADR is immutable: a changed decision is a new ADR that supersedes it.
  • Open questions are listed as such, never presented as decided.

docs.title: AI and teams
docs.text:
How an agent helps the owner and the team: the AI accelerates, people set the direction and decide. The owner agrees with these lessons and adopts them as working rules (2026-10-27).

  • Source: Paulo Caroli, Times importam mais do que nunca: direção humana, aceleração com IA e o futuro do trabalho de produto, https://caroli.org/livro/times-importam-mais-do-que-nunca/. The quotes below come from the owner's reading highlights, translated into English; they were not checked against the printed edition.

docs.title: The lessons
docs.text:
• Learn faster, never fake certainty. "AI should help teams learn faster. Not create the illusion of certainty." An answer states what is known, what is assumed and what is still open; a guess is never dressed as a fact.
  • Help think, do not decide. The daily question: "should AI make this decision, or should it help us think better about it? Most of the time, the second option is healthier." The agent lays out the options, the trade-offs and a recommendation; the owner decides (the open questions of a beach order go into the reply, beach.md).
  • Output is not progress. "Quantity is not the same as progress", and speed without direction "creates a dangerous illusion of efficacy": "the problem is no longer a lack of productivity, it is producing in the right direction". Before widening a slice, check that it still points at the goal of its issue; a long run of output with no feedback is a signal to stop and ask.
  • Progress motivates, so show the real kind. Teresa Amabile and Steven Kramer's research, published in The Progress Principle and cited by Paulo Caroli in Team OKR em Ação, showed that nothing motivates more at work than the feeling of moving forward. Small slices and a visible board give that feeling; a vanity number gives it falsely, so a report says what changed for a person, not how much was produced.
  • Accelerate the operational, free the human. AI accelerates synthesis, drafts, organisation, exploration and summaries, brainstorming, documentation, pattern recognition, preparation and finding information. That frees the team for what does not happen by itself: strategic conversations, understanding the customer, experimentation, prioritisation, collaboration, learning and the quality of decisions.
  • Clarity comes from learning together. AI produces a sense of clarity, "but real clarity emerges from joint learning". A synthesis by the agent is a draft for the conversation, not its conclusion.
  • In a strategic conversation, the agent challenges. Explore alternative approaches, point out inconsistencies, question assumptions, organise market information, synthesise large volumes of data, compare strategic options, list the possible risks, prepare conversations with leadership, refine objectives and name the missing perspectives (the panel skill does this at the end of a wave).
  • Do not fall in love with the first reasonable idea. "AI can also help teams avoid a common problem: falling in love with the first reasonable idea", because it makes exploration cheaper. Before recommending a design, the agent asks, and answers in the open: what are the alternative approaches? What assumptions are we making? What are the unintended consequences? What would a competitor do differently? What signals are we ignoring? What would make this strategy fail? Better visibility often leads to better decisions.
  • The edge is the combination. Teams win "not because they automate more, but because they combine fast exploration, strong collaboration, clear direction and well-defined criteria": short cycles and the walking skeleton for exploration, the issue and the spec for direction, the tests and the fitness functions for criteria (rules.md).
  • AI amplifies what is there. "If the way an organization produces products is unstructured or suboptimal now, it'll only get worse with AI" (Kaspar von Grünberg and Luca Galante, Thinking in Platforms, p. 10; Thinking in platforms). Agents work on top of clear interfaces, written rules and deterministic checks; where those are missing, the first job is to write them, not to add more agents.
  • Learn faster together. "The future won't belong to the teams that simply use more AI. The future will belong to the teams that learn faster together." Measure learning, not volume: what an attempt teaches is kept (rules.md, "What an attempt teaches is kept").

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • Paulo Caroli, Times importam mais do que nunca: AI in strategy, discovery, delivery, Team OKRs and Lean Inception.

docs.title: API groups
docs.text:
Status: proposed, to be written as an ADR and reviewed with the owner. Until that ADR is accepted, this page records the intent, not a rule.

An API group is a reef (The CLI design): <reef>.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, for example secrets.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1.

  1. Every new idea is first modelled as an API group (a reef), before any Nereid.
  2. Then we design how the API and the CLI interact with it, as CLI examples first.
  3. Every API group is born with the standard verbs of ADR 0013 (command conventions), kubectl's: create fails when the thing exists and lists the apply commands to run; apply creates or updates (it is the update verb); plus list, get and delete. Any other verb is an API extension.
  4. Every API group has a reference Nereid: once installed, the CLI answers every command and the resources are really created in Kubernetes. It is one Nereid for every reef (controllers/reference, #486), the subject of each reef's TCK: a reef is a module of its reefs/, the Nereid reference-<reef>, and every real Nereid of the reef must behave as it does. A port adds the reef's module there ("A port adds its reef" in its README). Not to be confused with a fake, an imitation of an outside tool's API that tests a real Nereid without the tool (test/fake-github).

Open points for the ADR:

  • The CRDs follow ADR 0009 (#20): a reef's own kinds in <reef>.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (clouds.cloud.getnereus.dev), the platform's in core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, which also prefixes the keys of the platform's labels and annotations. The platform's kinds are Reef, Nereid and Mandate (renamed by #402).

docs.title: Beach
docs.text: Glaucus (Glauco in Portuguese) is the messenger between the owner's voice session and the local agent (Claude Code): in the myth, the fisherman who became a sea god, next to Nereus and the Nereids. The channel is temporary: it ends when the first Nereid (the interlocutor, exposed as a remote MCP connector) runs on a Nereus instance. Conceptually, an order is a message of a future messaging reef; the Drive folder is its first, rudimentary implementation.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Everything lives under #pontos/beach/ on Google Drive:

Path What it holds beach/ the open orders, YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<slug>.md, plus 00-local-agent-prompt.md (the standing prompt, not an order). "Open" means not archived yet: a finished order stays here, next to its .done.md, until the session is closed beach/replies/<order-name>/ everything the agent writes for that order: <order-name>.ack.md, <order-name>.done.md and every output file beach/archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ finished orders, each with its replies/<order-name>/ folder

docs.title: The order header
docs.text:
Every order opens with a YAML front matter of five fields, in this order. The watcher reads only assigned_to (or, when an order has none, agent); the others say where the order comes from.

Field What it holds order the order's file name without .md: YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<slug> assigned_to the agent that does the work, the agent of its machine's .nereus-agent (for example m15); agent: is read the same way when an order has no assigned_to: (the owner, 2026-10-26); never assignee: initiator who asked for it: human:<first-name> or agent:<name> requested_via the channel it came through, for example voice conversation (claude.ai), coordinator Claude created_at when it was written, ISO 8601 with the offset: 2026-10-26T19:24-03:00

A complete order:

---
order: 20261026-1924-watcher-flags-unassigned-orders
assigned_to: m15
initiator: human:maria
requested_via: voice conversation (claude.ai), coordinator Claude
created_at: 2026-10-26T19:24-03:00
---

# Order 20261026-1924 - The beach watcher flags orders it cannot assign

Context: one paragraph on why.

## What to build
- ...

## Rules
- ...

## Reply
- Done file in replies/ with issue/PR links and the merge commit.

While the watcher knows only its own agent (no other in agents=, as long as m15 is the only one), an order whose assigned_to is missing or empty, with no likely typo of it in the header, is that agent's by default (the owner, 2026-10-28): claim.json and the ack say assigned_by: default, and explicit when assigned_to names the agent.

Otherwise an order whose assigned_to is missing, empty or names an agent the watcher does not know is never claimed: the watcher writes replies/<order-name>/unassigned.md once, saying what is wrong, which agents it knows, and asking "did you mean assigned_to:?" for a likely typo (agent:, assignee:, assigned-to:). Fix the header and the watcher picks the order up on its next poll.

docs.title: The protocol
docs.text:
• When the owner says "manda jangada" ("send it by raft"), the voice session writes one self-contained work order, in English, to beach/: a jangada (raft) is one order, the boat Glaucus sails.
  • The local agent lists the folder with rclone lsf and reads with rclone cat, or copies it with rclone copy (the FUSE mount is slow). A pending order is a *.md in beach/ without replies/<order-name>/<order-name>.ack.md.
  • On pickup, write replies/<order-name>/<order-name>.ack.md: a timestamp and a one-line understanding. Then do the work in this repository.
  • When finished, write replies/<order-name>/<order-name>.done.md: a summary, commit hashes, links to PRs and issues, open questions. Never edit the original order.
  • A cancelled order gets replies/<order-name>/<order-name>.cancelled.md, naming the order that superseded it.
  • Open questions go into the reply; the agent does not decide them.
  • An ambiguous or risky order (destroying resources, secrets, pushing to main) stops at the ack, with the questions written in it.
  • An order may say to wait for the owner's go; then it waits, even when it is the next one in the folder.
  • Only when the owner says "close the session" ("fecha a sessão"), move each finished order and its replies/<order-name>/ folder to beach/archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>/.

docs.title: The watcher
docs.text:
scripts/beach/watch picks up the orders for the agent of its machine. It reads its settings from .nereus-agent (git-ignored): the agent's name (for example m15), the Drive owner whose orders it trusts, and the intervals.

It polls the beach with rclone every 15 seconds, or every 60 while a run is active. It skips any file another owner wrote, writes claim.json first, and starts claude -p with bypass permissions on each new order whose assigned_to: names it; an order it cannot assign gets unassigned.md instead (The order header). Addenda go to the agent holding the claim.

How to set it up and run it: scripts/beach/README.md. It is a stand-in for an event bus on Nereus.

docs.title: The evaluation of an order
docs.text:
Every reply to an order ends with these two blocks, filled by the agent, and the agent records the row with scripts/metrics/order record (#803), in getnereus/internal, metrics/orders/<year>-W<week>.csv.

Never ask the owner for a rating: it did not help (owner, 2026-11-03). The row keeps its rating empty, unless the owner gives one unasked, which goes in with scripts/metrics/order rate. Asking for a rating where a command is used is a separate idea, #885.

## Evaluation
- Performance: start -> PR opened (time), PR -> merge (time), review rounds, smoke test / nereus doctor passed (yes/no)
- Cost: tokens and estimated cost, per agent (source/tool used)
## Session metrics
- Duration (start -> end), active vs idle
- Orders sent / done / blocked
- Tokens and estimated cost (tool/source)
- Interruptions / rework (times the plan changed or a detail had to be repeated)

docs.title: The CLI design
docs.text:
The target CLI, from the owner's voice session of 2026-10-25 (raw data in Drive #pontos/raw/2026-10-25, files 38 to 47; the flow in last-terminal.html). It wins over any legacy command: the commands of today's code (platform ...) are reference only, mapped below.

Every command lives in a deck, one per reef (#477): docs/specs/cli/reefs/<reef>.yaml, with a section per kind and the index in docs/specs/cli/index.yaml. The YAML is the source of truth, an outline of the deck engine (docs/presentations/render-outline, Decks); each command slide has a status (built, planned with its issue, or idea), shown as a tag after its label.

A new command, or a change to one, goes into its reef's deck first, and the issue that builds it points to the slide (reefs/edge.html#domain-get). The get-started, release and edge decks in docs/walkthrough/decks/ link each step to its command's slide; the engine refuses a link to a slide that does not exist.

make decks renders them all; make deck-test checks them and fails when an HTML is stale. The reefs not ported yet keep their commands in this page and in the walkthroughs.

docs.title: The words
docs.text:
Word What it is Legacy word reef A capability of the platform, an API group <reef>.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (for example secrets.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1). A reef can exist with no Nereid; then it waits. core is built in. Interface Nereid A controller installed in the platform, top-level, with a name global to the platform. One Nereid may look after many reefs (--reef repeats), and one reef may have many Nereids. It owns its authentication (for example workload-identity) and its default target parameters (for example a default vaultUrl). Its image is <reef>-<tool>-controller. Implementation Mandate Binds one reef to one Nereid, top-level. It may override the Nereid's target parameters with --param (a Nereid may serve several vaults); --default makes it the reef's default; --match <key>=<value> picks it for the requests whose keys equal the values, the most specific match winning (ADR 0017, #1598). Class tenancy The reef that holds whose a thing is (ADR 0015): tenancy.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, its kinds from each instance's reefs/tenancy/ (here Organization, the boundary, and Project), every kind a node with spec.parent: {kind, name}. Its commands are ideas in its deck (#569) until #573 builds them. none catalog The reef that says what Nereus has (ADR 0016): catalog.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, its kinds Workload (what runs, the default kind, so nereus catalog list is nereus catalog workload list), Package (what is published), the configurable WorkloadType and PackageType, and Template (its render is the delivery deck's). Every entry names its owner and a Workload its audience; source.ref is structured as Flux's (--ref <field>=<value>, repeatable, never one string); --audience none is audience: []. Its commands are ideas in its deck (#570) until #574 builds them. none delivery The reef that takes a Workload to an Environment (ADR 0020): delivery.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, its kind Delivery (the default kind), one per pair. nereus workload deploy writes it, and the Nereid kubernetes resolves the image's digest and writes a Release. Its commands are planned in its deck until #845 builds them. none database The first resource reef (ADR 0017, #653): database.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, its kind Database (the default kind, so nereus database create) with owner: {kind, name} in the tenancy tree, which must exist, and engine (postgres), in the nereus namespace only; the Nereid cloudnative-pg of its default Mandate cloudnative-pg (applied by the internal-developer-platform profile) writes in status.binding.secret the Secret of the connection. none messaging A resource reef (ADR 0017, #1597, the first cut of #576): messaging.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, its kinds Topic and Queue (no default kind, so nereus messaging topic create and nereus messaging queue create; the agents' sessions moved to the rooms reef, #2076) with owner: {kind, name} in the tenancy tree, engine (nats) and deletionPolicy (retain, the default, or delete), in the nereus namespace only; the Nereid nats of the admin's default Mandate (--param jetstream=true) runs NATS next to it and writes in status.binding.secret the Secret <name>-topic or <name>-queue. none rooms The reef of the conversation between agents (ADR 0030, #2067): rooms.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, its kinds Room (the default kind, so nereus rooms create, apply, list, get and delete) and Peer (an agent's session in the rooms, nereus rooms peer list and get), with nereus rooms join and leave (#2075), nereus rooms follow and pull (#2076) and post (#1889). The Nereid triton requires the messaging reef and asks it for a Topic room-<room> per Room. create, apply, list, get and delete of a Room go through the Nereus API, asked on the Room's owner: a team's members create rooms owned by the team's owner, admins delete them (#1491), and a new room past the default Mandate's maxRooms (20) fails. Triton writes a RoomSession per room's activity, read with nereus rooms session list and get (#2100). Every command is in its deck; the old names are mapped in Legacy commands. none registry The reef that runs a registry of images in the cluster (ADR 0021): registry.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, its kinds Registry (the default kind) and Repository (#1013, its own push credential). The Nereid writes status.pullAddress for a node and status.internalAddress for a Pod. Not the Nereid registry (#22). See its deck. none scm The reef that holds what a source host is to Nereus (ADR "The scm reef", #927): scm.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, its kind Connection (one organisation of a host, reached through the GitHub App that its scm Mandate's param identity names; the default kind). Who the platform is towards the host (the App, a short-lived Token) is the authentication reef's (ADR 0006). The github Nereid serves both reefs, opt-in. See its deck. none owner Whatever points to the tenancy tree names owner: {kind, name}, a kind of the tenancy group, never an apiVersion or a namespace: the catalog's Workloads and Packages, an Environment, a resource Instance, a Mandate's match. On the command line --owner <kind>/<name>, optional once nereus config set owner names the current one; the flag wins and the output line names the owner used. spec.project target What nereus init --target <provider> prepares (for azure: Key Vault, Storage, DNS zone, Managed Identity), with the person's own login, since no Nereid exists yet. --target of platform init

"Mandate" is the working term, and "Instance" keeps its name (ADR 0002). The CLI binary is nereus (formerly platform, #396); its commands are the ones below since #409, and the legacy ones are deprecated aliases (see Legacy commands).

docs.title: The commands
docs.text:
# Prepare a cluster: core, then a profile (ADR 0014). core, the default: core only;
# internal-developer-platform: authentication with keycloak, after the secrets reef it
# requires (OpenBao on k3d, its default vault Mandate and RSA key)
nereus init
nereus init --profile internal-developer-platform
nereus init --target azure

# Profiles (ADR 0014): one YAML file each, charts/nereus/profiles/<name>.yaml, rendered by the chart
# into the Profile's spec, which thetis reads alone (spec.reefs required, #1370); apply layers one on core, idempotent, and
# `init --profile <name>` is init, then this. `profile create` is parked
nereus profile list
nereus profile describe <profile>
nereus profile apply <profile> [--without <nereid>]... [--dry-run]   # on a Profile (the charts), --without leaves a Nereid out (#1231); the Nereids install side by side, NEREUS_PROFILE_LANES at once (4, #1297)

# Reefs (after the profile internal-developer-platform, `reef create secrets` fails as "already exists",
# `reef apply secrets` reports unchanged or configured)
nereus reef list
nereus reef apply <reef> --from-file ./reefs/<reef>/

# Nereids
nereus nereid suggest --reef <reef>
nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef <reef> [--reef <reef> ...] [--image <image>] [--param <key>=<value> ...]

# Mandates
nereus mandate create <mandate> --reef <reef> --nereid <nereid> [--param <key>=<value> ...] [--match <key>=<value> ... | --default]

# The reefs' own commands: nereus <reef> <kind> <verb> <name>; `nereus <reef> <verb>` is the
# reef's default kind (ADR 0013), so `nereus secrets create` is `nereus secrets secret create`.
# create builds from flags, apply takes files or folders of .yaml
nereus secrets create <secret> --from-env <variable> [--from-env <variable> ...]
nereus secrets create <secret> --from-env <variable> --dry-run --output yaml > <file>
nereus secrets apply --from-file <file or folder>

# The release reef (ADR 0010, #445): a kind named after its reef takes the reef's own verbs,
# so `nereus release create` is `nereus release release create`
nereus release repository create|apply|list|get|delete <repository> [--url <url> --type http|oci|git] [--secret <secret>]
nereus release source create|apply|list|get|delete <source> [--repository <repository> --chart <chart> --version <version>]
nereus release target create|apply|list|get|delete <target> [--namespace <namespace>] [--environment <environment>]
nereus release create|apply|list|get|delete <release> [--source <source> --target <target>] [--values-file <file>] [--mandate <mandate>]
nereus release get <release> --watch

# The tenancy reef (ADR 0015, ideas in its deck until #573): parents before children,
# the output names each node by its full path (#647); a flag per string field of the
# kind's spec; apply is the group's, never a kind's; spec.parent never changes (#646)
nereus tenancy organization create|list|get|delete <organization>
nereus tenancy project create|list|get|delete <project> [--parent <kind>/<name>] [--repository <url>] [--cascade]
nereus tenancy apply --from-file tenancy/ [--dry-run]

# The catalog reef (ADR 0016, built by #902, check an idea until #903): workload is the default kind;
# apply is the group's, never a kind's; a template writes files before the catalog, so
# --template is not a flag of create (its render is the delivery deck's); check fails on a
# contradiction (✗) and only points at a gap (!)
nereus catalog workload create|list|get|delete <workload> [--owner <kind>/<name>] [--type <type>] [--audience programs|people|agents|none] [--repository <url>] [--ref <field>=<value>] [--path <path>]
nereus catalog package create|list|get|delete <package> [--owner <kind>/<name>] [--type <type>] [--registry <registry>] [--name <name>] [--audience <audience>]
nereus catalog workload-type create|list|get|delete <type> [--runs always|once] [--trigger event|request|schedule]
nereus catalog package-type create|list|get|delete <type> [--registry <registry>]
nereus catalog apply --from-file catalog/ [--dry-run]
nereus catalog check

# The delivery reef (ADR 0020, planned in its deck until #845): deploy never guesses the
# target; workload list is the catalog's, delivery list is what was deployed
nereus workload deploy <workload>@<environment>|<delivery> --image <reference> [--wait] [--timeout <seconds>] [--dry-run]
nereus workload list
nereus workload logs <workload>@<environment>|<delivery>|<workload> [--environment <environment>] [--follow]
nereus delivery create|list|get|delete <delivery>
nereus delivery apply --from-file <path> [--wait=true|false] [--timeout <seconds>] [--dry-run]
nereus template render <template> --path <folder> [--param <name>=<value>] [--dry-run]

# The registry reef (ADR 0021): the zot Nereid is #1012, Repository and publish are #1013
nereus registry create <registry> [--owner <kind>/<name>] [--mandate <mandate>] [--dry-run]
nereus registry list|get|delete <registry>
nereus registry apply --from-file <path> [--wait=true|false] [--timeout <seconds>] [--dry-run]
nereus registry repository publish <repository> --registry <registry> --image <image>:<tag>
nereus registry repository list|get|delete <repository>

# The rooms reef (ADR 0030, #1491): Room, its default kind, owned by an organization or a project; without a name the
# repository's, without --owner the owner of your team; a new room past the default Mandate's maxRooms (20) fails
nereus rooms create [<room>] [--owner <kind>/<name>] [--description <text>] [--max-age <duration>] [--max-bytes <size>] [--deletion-policy retain|delete] [--dry-run]
nereus rooms apply --from-file <path> [--dry-run]
nereus rooms list|get <room>
nereus rooms delete <room> --yes [--dry-run]
nereus rooms peer list|get <owner>.<agent>

# The platform's identity (ADR 0006, planned in the authentication deck): a GitHub App is a Mandate
# of the opt-in github Nereid (#1273), its key a plain secret; Token is #1274, the browser action #1275
nereus nereid apply github --reef authentication --reef scm
nereus mandate create github --reef authentication --nereid github --param appId=<id> --param privateKey=<secret> --param allow=<namespace>:<repository or *>:<permission>=<level>[,...] [--default]
nereus authentication token create <token> --repository <org>/<repository> [--permission <name>=<access>] [--mandate <mandate>] [--dry-run]
nereus authentication token list|get|delete <token>

# The scm reef (ADR 0024, built in #1281): a Connection names an organisation
# reached through the App its scm Mandate names (--param identity=<authentication mandate>, #1281); no vendor, no key, no verify
nereus scm connection create <connection> --org <org> [--mandate <mandate>] [--default] [--dry-run]
nereus scm connection list|get|delete <connection>

# The current owner (ADR 0016, with #574): --owner becomes optional; the flag wins
nereus config set owner <kind>/<name>

# How the reefs are doing
nereus status

# Whether this instance is healthy: pass or fail per check, exit code 1 when one fails (#799)
nereus doctor

# The CLI keeps itself up to date (#1782): upgrade now, or only report; a normal call starts a
# detached upgrade once per check_interval (auto_upgrade: background, notify or off)
nereus upgrade [--check|--dry-run]
nereus config set auto_upgrade background|notify|off
nereus config set check_interval 24h
  • Output: every command with --output (-o) takes table (the default), yaml, yamlc (coloured YAML), json and jsonc (coloured JSON); the coloured forms colour even in a pipe, since the person asked for them (#409). Every -o also has the long form --output (owner, 2026-10-31). Every get, list, describe and show takes it, and every --output has -o (owner, 2026-11-16, #1734): cli/tests/test_help.py walks the command tree and fails otherwise. A get or list of an API object prints the object without managedFields; a command that shows settings or a table of its own prints its rows keyed by their headers in camelCase (REQUIRED BY is requiredBy). A command may add a form of its own that writes an export: presentation get --output html (#1703) and session get --output agent (#1718, a YAML for an agent, with a ✓ … written line on stderr when stdout is not a terminal). An export made to be redirected writes its summary line on stderr, never stdout, so the file holds only the export (owner, 2026-11-18).
  • Order: status and every list come in alphabetical order; --sort-by <path>, as kubectl's, sorts by any field of the objects (.metadata.creationTimestamp; .createdAt on status), in every form of --output; rows without the field go last, a field no row has is refused (#808). sorted_by in output.py is the one place. Over secrets it reads what the command shows, never the encrypted values. A table whose order means something keeps it (plan steps, doctor, profile describe, settings).
  • Help: every command and group takes -h as well as --help, with the same output and the same precedence over --version and --examples (#1733); the root sets both in its context_settings, and every command inherits them.
  • Examples: every command and group takes --examples (#674): each example after a # <what it does> line, as tldr prints them; a group lists every command under it, each after a ## <path> line, and nereus --examples lists the whole CLI. With --output, they come as data for agents: command and description, plus path on a group (#675). In code, examples() takes (description, command) pairs, and cli/tests/test_help.py requires a description for each.
  • Help: flat, Click's plain text, no Rich markup or colours (TYPER_USE_RICH=0, set in cli/src/nereus/__init__.py, #704). nereus --help lists its commands in sections Platform, Session, Model and Reefs, each sorted by name, one line per command; a new top-level command sets short_help (at most 60 characters) and rich_help_panel (one of those four), and cli/tests/test_help.py requires both.
  • Flags: --param <key>=<value> for every parameter (never --set); --reef and --nereid everywhere (never --implements), never prepositions (--on-reef, --to-nereid); examples use long-form options, one per line.
  • Verbs: kubectl's, ADR 0013 (command conventions): create builds from flags and fails when the thing exists, apply creates or updates from files or folders of .yaml only (every former add), delete deletes, plus get and list; every noun takes all five, and every command that changes something takes --dry-run. add and remove are not verbs. Installing a reef or a Nereid by name (nereus nereid apply <nereid>) keeps today's form until #487 (the verb that installs a reef or a Nereid by name) decides it.

  • Output lines name the object by its full path, as Azure's resource ids do: the reef, then each kind in the plural and its name, parents before children, the platform's kinds under core, and end in created, configured, unchanged or deleted:

    secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth created (key SHA256:Xy3…)
release/releases/keycloak created
core/mandates/default unchanged (reef: secrets, nereid: openbao, default)

  • Delete waits, as kubectl's does (#526): an object whose Nereid keeps its cleanup finalizer (#525) stays until the Nereid removed what it made; meanwhile list and get show Terminating in the state column (computed by the CLI from metadata.deletionTimestamp, never written in status, ADR 0005; the --output forms carry the object as it is). delete waits until the object is gone, printing each step of status.steps as it changes (the time it changed, ✓ Done, … InProgress, · Pending, ✗ Failed, its name, its message), then the deleted line; a step Failed or Ready=False with reason: CleanupFailed ends it with exit 1 and Next steps: naming get. --wait=false (kubectl's spelling: --wait takes true or false) returns at once with <path> is Terminating: <nereid> removes what it made.; --timeout (seconds, as get --watch's) ends the wait with a failure naming the step in progress, the object left as it is. get --watch prints the steps too, and stops once a Terminating object is gone. The shared part lives in cli/src/nereus/reefkinds.py, for every reef's commands.

  • What a delete must respect lives behind the API (#874): the vcluster Nereid holds an Environment's finalizer while a Target names it and says why in the status, for any client; nereus environment delete checks first only to refuse early, and refuses when it cannot check.
  • Discovery (#839): a reef's commands come from a cache, as kubectl's discovery. nereus login fills it from GET /v1/discovery, open to any signed-in person (the kubeconfig without sign-in); a run naming a reef refreshes it past one hour or from another instance; an unknown first word rediscovers once, then fails naming nereus status. --help and completion never call.

  • Next steps: every output ends with a Next steps: label, a blank line before and after it, and the command indented two spaces:

    core/reefs/secrets created (secrets.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: secrets, secretbindings, vaults)

Next steps:

  nereus nereid apply --help

docs.title: Kinds
docs.text:
The platform's own kinds are Reef, Nereid and Mandate, in core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1, owned by the core reef (ADR 0002, ADR 0009); a reef's own kinds live in <reef>.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1. Today's code applies these kinds in these groups (#20, #402): the cloud reef ships only its Cloud kind, and its Nereid's binding is a Mandate.

Their fields:

Kind Field Holds Reef spec the contract: API group, version, commands Nereid spec.reefs the reefs it looks after (a list) Nereid spec.image the image it runs, pinned by digest Nereid spec.params its authentication and default target parameters Mandate spec.reef, spec.nereid the reef and the Nereid it binds Mandate spec.params the overrides of the Nereid's target parameters Mandate spec.default true for the reef's default Mandate

A reef's own objects key their entries by reef, never by Nereid: a Cloud access entry is {reef: secrets, ...}. Today's code uses reef: in those entries and spec.reefs (a list) on Nereid.

docs.title: Listing
docs.text:
$ nereus status
REEF     NEREID           VERSION  STATUS  AGE
core     nereus-api       0.1.0    Ready   38m
secrets  azure-key-vault  0.1.0    Ready   8m

$ nereus nereid list
NEREID           REEFS    IMAGE                                                              STATUS  AGE
azure-key-vault  secrets  ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/secrets-azure-key-vault-controller:0.1.0  Ready   8m

nereus status has one row per reef and Nereid pair; nereus nereid list one row per Nereid, its reefs comma-separated (ADR 0011). nereus nereid get <nereid> shows one Nereid in full, with the image's OCI labels org.opencontainers.image.title and org.opencontainers.image.description and its digest, which nereid list leaves out.

STATUS is computed by the CLI, not written by the Nereid (spec 0003, layer 2, #527): the Nereid's own Ready condition, unless its Controller has no pod serving (Unavailable, which wins) or it does not honour its reefs' kinds (NotConformant): a reef that exposes no kind has no Ready Nereid, unless it has none by design (authentication, portal and metrics, pinned in contracts.REEFS_WITHOUT_KINDS, #794), and a Nereid serves every kind its reef exposes, declared in its status.kinds as <plural>.<group>.

core is built in and always Ready; a reef with no Nereid is Waiting, unless it needs none by design: every CRD of the reef annotated core.getnereus.dev/nereid: "none" (the tenancy reef, whose objects the API keeps, ADR 0015; #651) makes its row Ready with - as its Nereid, and its reason says why.

nereus nereid get prints why on a Reason line, nereus status --output json|yaml as the reason field of each row, and a command to a NotConformant Nereid is refused with that reason.

docs.title: Secrets are encrypted on the client
docs.text:
A mandatory capability of the secrets reef contract: every secrets Nereid publishes a public key for each Mandate naming it, in the Mandate's status.publicKey, and decrypts inside its own boundary. The CLI encrypts each secret locally with envelope encryption: an AES-256-GCM data key encrypts the value, and the Mandate's RSA-OAEP-256 public key wraps the data key.

nereus secrets create uses the key of the Mandate it targets, the default one unless a Mandate is named. The CLI stays provider-agnostic; only the Nereid differs:

Where The private key Azure (--target azure) A non-exportable RSA key in Key Vault; the Nereid calls Key Vault to decrypt. Local k3d, no target A non-exportable RSA key of the OpenBao Transit engine (API: exportable defaults to false); the Nereid calls Transit to decrypt. Fallback Sealed Secrets style: the private key in a cluster Secret.

Log redaction stays, whatever the encryption.

Through the Nereus API (#1323), the CLI still seals each value on the machine: the API stores the envelopes as they come, never returns spec.data in an answer or an error, and logs the route and the person, never a body. It hands the CLI the Mandate's public key, which the CLI checks (fingerprint, size) as it did from the apiserver.

docs.title: Legacy commands
docs.text:
The aliases of nereus system that #409 kept for the legacy commands are gone (#410): only nereus system access list|approve stays, until its form is designed.

Legacy (platform ...) New form platform init [--yes] nereus init platform init --target azure nereus init --target azure (it also adds the secrets reef with Azure Key Vault, its default default Mandate, its RSA key and the vault default, ADR 0003) platform system interface, install, uninstall, implementation nereus reef ..., nereus nereid apply, delete, list, nereus mandate create ... --default; the aliases went in #410 platform controller list, platform controller install nereus nereid list, nereus nereid apply platform system access list, approve No new form yet (open, designed later) platform config installation set, show No new form yet (open, designed later) platform config slo set, show, reset No new form yet (open, designed later) platform release ..., platform helm repo ..., platform namespace ..., platform cloud ... The reef's own commands: nereus <reef> <verb> platform login, platform user ... Old form, no new form: users come through SSO (authentication reef); nereus user commands will be designed when Nereus needs them none nereus status, nereus doctor, nereus nereid suggest, nereus mandate create (new)

The commands of the room moved under the rooms reef (#2076, #2075). Each old name is hidden from the help and prints one line, <old> moved: run \`, exiting 2;nereus room pullstays a silent alias, since the hooks of sessions started before #2076 run it, andnereus mcp local add` rewrites those hooks. Old name New form nereus room follow nereus rooms follow nereus room pull (a hook's command) nereus rooms pull, the old name still runs nereus messaging session list nereus rooms peer list nereus messaging session create nereus rooms join (#2075)

docs.title: First implementation step
docs.text:
Before any command of this design is built, the code's binary platform became nereus and the MCP server's name platform-mcp became nereus-mcp (#396; the names live in cli/src/nereus/names.py and one build setting, docs/agent/rules.md), so the legacy commands now run as nereus system ..., nereus config .... The sequence after that:

  • The kinds Interface, Implementation and the per-reef classes (CloudClass) became Reef, Nereid and Mandate in core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (#402).
  • nereus init with no target came with the secrets reef, the openbao Nereid, the default vault Mandate and its public key (#404).
  • nereus nereid apply keycloak --reef authentication (then a legacy alias under system) added the authentication reef's local Nereid, the authorization server of the claude.ai connector (#407).
  • nereus reef create|apply|list|delete, nereus nereid apply|list|get|delete, nereus mandate create|apply|list and nereus status came, with nereus status --output json as the contract of the first MCP tool, status, served today by the Nereus API's /mcp (#409, ADR 0029).
  • nereus reef get, nereus nereid create, nereus mandate get and nereus mandate delete completed the five verbs, and the legacy aliases of nereus system went (#410).

docs.title: Decks
docs.text:
