  • A cloud request is refused, when you lack a right.
  • Grant access: what the reefs ask of the cloud.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • Spec 0005: the Nereid azure and the requester tags.

docs.title: Prepare a cluster for Nereus
docs.text: Make a cluster that offers what Nereus needs, by hand, for Install with Helm; nereus init --create-cluster does the same for you.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
What any cluster must offer, and how k3d and AKS meet it. AKS is there to compare and is not tested: no installation has run on it yet.

Need k3d AKS (not tested) Tools Docker 20.10.5+, k3d 5.0.0+, Helm 4.0.0+ az, Helm 4.0.0+ Host fs.inotify.max_user_instances=1024 the nodes are Azure's Entrance: Gateway API kinds, a way to the Gateway no Traefik; 127.0.0.1:8080 to the load balancer's port 80 a LoadBalancer Service with a public IP, DNS and TLS in front Images the local registry, or ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus ghcr.io, or a copy in an Azure Container Registry Registry trust: every node trusts the local registry's CA the CA's certificate mounted on every node not needed: the nodes pull from a container registry such as ACR or ghcr.io, with credentials The registry reef: a registry in the cluster its CA is the one of step 2, which every node trusts planned: the nodes would have to trust its CA API server: anonymous reads of the issuer's discovery only an AuthenticationConfiguration on the server --enable-oidc-issuer; the anonymous read is still to check

On a machine that already has a k3d cluster named nereus, such as one kept for daily work, pick another name and port: replace nereus in the commands of step 5 and Clean up, and 8080 in --port. | Storage: a default StorageClass | local-path | managed-csi | | Network: NetworkPolicy enforced | k3s enforces it | --network-policy azure, calico or cilium |

docs.title: Steps
docs.text: The steps make a k3d cluster; the registry CA of steps 2 and 3 is for its local registry. AKS follows after step 5.

docs.title: 1. Raise the host's inotify limit
docs.text:
With Ubuntu's default of 128, a second k3d cluster never starts. Raise it once per machine.

echo "fs.inotify.max_user_instances=1024" \
  | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-k3d-inotify.conf
sudo sysctl --system

docs.title: 2. Make the registry CA
docs.text:
A Registry answers only over TLS, with a certificate from one CA every node trusts. Its name constraints allow only localhost and names under svc.cluster.local, so trusting it trusts nothing else. Keep its files in a folder of your own, nereus/.

mkdir --parents nereus/registry
(umask 077 && openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out nereus/ca.key)
openssl req -new -x509 -sha256 -days 3650 \
  -key nereus/ca.key \
  -out nereus/registry/ca.crt \
  -subj "/CN=Nereus registry CA" \
  -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:true,pathlen:0" \
  -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" \
  -addext "nameConstraints=critical,permitted;DNS:localhost,permitted;DNS:svc.cluster.local,excluded;IP:0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0,excluded;IP:::/::"
chmod 0755 nereus nereus/registry
chmod 0644 nereus/registry/ca.crt

docs.title: 3. Trust it for every registry
docs.text:
nereus/registries.yaml adds the CA to the roots of every registry the nodes pull from.

configs:
  "*":
    tls:
      ca_file: /etc/nereus/registry/ca.crt

docs.title: 4. Open the issuer's discovery
docs.text:
zot reads the cluster issuer's discovery and keys with no token, to check a build's push token. k3s turns anonymous requests off; nereus/authentication-config.yaml lets them in on those two paths only.

apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: AuthenticationConfiguration
anonymous:
  enabled: true
  conditions:
    - path: /.well-known/openid-configuration
    - path: /openid/v1/jwks

docs.title: 5. Create the cluster
docs.text:
No load balancer, since k3d's is nginx, and the API on the loopback only (#2152); no Traefik, since the profile brings Istio's Gateway; the Gateway on port 8080 of the loopback; the CA on every node and the configuration on the server. Docker mounts absolute paths.

k3d cluster create nereus \
  --no-lb \
  --api-port "127.0.0.1:random" \
  --k3s-arg "--disable=traefik@server:*" \
  --port "127.0.0.1:8080:80@server:0:direct" \
  --registry-config nereus/registries.yaml \
  --volume "${PWD}/nereus/registry:/etc/nereus/registry@all" \
  --volume "${PWD}/nereus/authentication-config.yaml:/etc/rancher/nereus/authentication-config.yaml@server:*" \
  --k3s-arg "--kube-apiserver-arg=authentication-config=/etc/rancher/nereus/authentication-config.yaml@server:*" \
  --wait

Keep nereus/: the nodes mount it, the API server reads its file on every restart, and the chart nereus takes the CA from it.

On AKS, the same rows are flags of az aks create: --network-plugin azure --network-policy azure, --enable-oidc-issuer and --enable-workload-identity; a build pool is a node pool labelled and tainted build.getnereus.dev/pool=build.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text: kubectl get storageclass shows local-path as the default, and kubectl get nodes shows every node Ready. After the install, nereus doctor says when the issuer's discovery is closed.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text: Delete the cluster with k3d cluster delete nereus and its folder with rm -r nereus.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Install with Helm on this cluster.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • Runtime and profiles: what the profile installs on the cluster.

docs.title: Deploy main to the live cluster
docs.text: Upgrade the live cluster in place to the commit of main, from the published charts, and check it with the smoke test.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• live is today the kept cluster k3d-nereus (see Rebuild the kept cluster). The scenes use it too, so the script refuses it without --allow-kept-cluster, and the other sessions on the repository are asked first.
  • A clone of the repository: the script runs on your machine, by hand; no GitHub Action is involved, and the trigger on every push comes later (#914).
  • NEREUS_LIVE_CONTEXT=k3d-nereus exported, the kubeconfig context the script uses; kubectl --context k3d-nereus get nodes answers.

docs.title: 1. See the plan
docs.text:
A dry run prints every command, resolves the commit of main and touches nothing.

scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster --dry-run

docs.title: 2. Deploy and test
docs.text:
The script fetches origin/main, runs helm upgrade --install for nereus-reefs, then nereus, from oci://ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts, records the commit as the annotation deploy.getnereus.dev/commit on nereus-system, then runs the smoke test. The first run on a cluster names the installation, which never changes after that.

scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster --installation-name nereus

A failed upgrade ends the run before the commit is recorded. Each upgrade runs with --force-conflicts: on live, the chart decides over a field another manager changed.

docs.title: 3. Drop values the chart owns now
docs.text:
A release installed by hand or by nereus init may hold values such as an image pointing at the local registry. --reset-values drops them, so the chart's published images, by digest, apply; give the installation's name again.

scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster --reset-values --installation-name nereus

docs.title: 4. Verify main before it is published
docs.text:
scripts/deploy/line compares the new main with the last green commit, else the highest tag, on the paths a release is built from, and runs make scene-core on it in a kept worktree. A merge that changed none of those paths is green by inheritance.

scripts/deploy/line run
output
fetch: origin/main is dde5f73 (last verified none)
paths: changed since v0.1.8: api/ cli/ controllers/ Makefile
scene: make scene-core on dde5f73 in ../nereus-line
ok: scene-core passed in 13m05s
publish: off (would run: make release)
== line green: dde5f73

A failed scene marks the line red, keeps its log in ~/.local/state/nereus/line/<commit>.log and exits non-zero. run --publish runs make release only after a green scene; a file .deploy-paused in the main clone's root suspends every run.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
The smoke test only reads: every Deployment of nereus-system rolled out, the annotation equals the commit, the API answers /healthz, and nereus doctor passes. Run it alone any time.

scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster --smoke-only

scripts/deploy/line status shows the last verified commit and whether the line is paused.

scripts/deploy/line status
output
main     dde5f73  green  2026-11-15 05:25  scene-core 13m05s
paused   no   (<main clone>/.deploy-paused)

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Meet the time SLO for the scenes the line runs.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• scripts/deploy/live --help: the settings, all options or environment variables (NEREUS_CHART_REF, NEREUS_CHART_VERSION, NEREUS_LIVE_INGRESS_ADDRESS), so the repository holds no address or token.
  • The line is a stand-in: on the platform, k3d-nereus mirrors main and builds it (#159, #1613).

docs.title: Publish at a hostname
docs.text: Publish a reef's endpoint, here Triton, at a hostname of your own domain, while Nereus runs on your machine behind a Cloudflare tunnel.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A cluster from Prepare the cluster with the secrets reef: the Nereid cloudflare requires it, and makes the vault edge.
  • A domain, a Cloudflare account on the free plan, and a named tunnel's credentials from cloudflared tunnel create nereus, in ~/.cloudflared/<UUID>.json.

docs.title: 1. Apply the edge reef
docs.text:
nereus reef apply edge adds the kinds Zone, Domain and Route.

nereus reef apply edge
output
✓ core/reefs/edge 0.1.0 created

docs.title: 2. Apply the Nereid cloudflare
docs.text:
nereus nereid apply cloudflare runs the zone and the tunnel.

nereus nereid apply cloudflare --reef edge
output
✓ core/nereids/cloudflare created, Ready

docs.title: 3. Keep the tunnel's credentials and name the tunnel
docs.text:
Keep the credentials file as the secret edge/cloudflare-tunnel with nereus secrets create edge/cloudflare-tunnel --from-file credentials.json=<file> (Keep a secret). Then the Mandate names the tunnel and that secret.

nereus mandate create cloudflare \
  --reef edge \
  --nereid cloudflare \
  --param tunnel=nereus \
  --param credentialsSecret=edge/cloudflare-tunnel \
  --default
output
✓ core/mandates/cloudflare created (reef: edge, nereid: cloudflare, default)

docs.title: 4. Delegate the domain
docs.text:
nereus edge zone create makes the zone and prints its nameservers; point your registrar at them.

nereus edge zone create getnereus.dev --mandate cloudflare
output
✓ edge/zones/getnereus.dev created, waiting for its delegation
  nameservers: ada.ns.cloudflare.com, bob.ns.cloudflare.com
  point the registrar of getnereus.dev at them; the zone turns Active once Cloudflare sees it

When the domain is registered at GoDaddy, the Nereid godaddy points it there for you (#475): nereus nereid apply godaddy, its Mandate with GoDaddy's key and secret in the vault edge, then nereus edge domain apply.

nereus edge domain apply getnereus.dev --nameservers-from zone/getnereus.dev --wait

GoDaddy answers 403 to an account that may not use its production Domains API; the Domain then says RegistrarRefused, and the registrar is changed by hand.

docs.title: 5. Carry the hostname through the tunnel
docs.text:
nereus edge route create carries a hostname to the ingress gateway. Create the routes right after the Mandate: until one exists, the tunnel answers 404 for every hostname.

nereus edge route create triton --hostname triton.getnereus.dev
output
✓ edge/routes/triton created, Ready: https://triton.getnereus.dev

A route may also name the endpoint a reef publishes, never a cluster, a namespace, a Service or a port (#1951). nereus edge endpoint list shows every endpoint the Nereids publish, with the hostnames each one serves; none is published by default. The Nereid's own apply grants one, then the route names it:

nereus edge endpoint list
nereus nereid apply triton --reef rooms --publish mcp
nereus edge route create triton --hostname triton.getnereus.dev --endpoint rooms/mcp

The tunnel carries the hostname only when the endpoint is publishable, granted and served on that hostname; otherwise the route says why (NotPublished, NotServed, NoEndpoint, or Exposes when the hostname also serves an endpoint that may not leave the cluster: the tunnel carries the whole hostname). The kept cluster's routes move to endpoints with #2011.

Only a Nereid with an HTTPRoute of its own on the hostname counts for Exposes: what a Nereid says in its status alone never takes another Nereid's route off the air.

Any other HTTPRoute the entrance's Gateway admits on the hostname makes the route Exposes too, naming it as <namespace>/<name>: one with no Nereid label (the chart's nereus-api, one a Release made), one of another namespace, or one whose Nereid publishes no granted endpoint there. Give such a host its own hostname, or publish its endpoint.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus edge zone list shows the zone Active once the delegation arrives, and nereus edge route list shows every hostname the platform answers; then https://triton.getnereus.dev answers.

nereus edge route list
output
NAME     HOSTNAME               ENDPOINT  MANDATE     READY   URL
auth     auth.getnereus.dev     -         cloudflare  True    https://auth.getnereus.dev
portal   portal.getnereus.dev   -         cloudflare  True    https://portal.getnereus.dev
triton   triton.getnereus.dev   -         cloudflare  True    https://triton.getnereus.dev

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Rebuild the kept cluster, which publishes Triton, the realm and the portal this way.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• With a Cloudflare API token in a secret of the vault edge (--param apiTokenSecret=edge/cloudflare-token on the Mandate), the Nereid creates or adopts the tunnel itself, with no cloudflared tunnel create (#1961, deploy/edge/README.md).
  • ADR 0005: Nereids publish their endpoints and commands in status.

docs.title: Install with Helm
docs.text: Install Nereus and the profile internal-developer-platform on a cluster you made, with two helm upgrade --install lines and no nereus init.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The k3d cluster nereus of Prepare a cluster for Nereus, with its folder nereus/ kept: the nodes mount it, and the chart nereus takes the registry CA from it.
  • helm and kubectl pointed at that cluster. Both charts and every image are published on ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus, by digest, so nothing is built.

docs.title: 1. Install the kinds
docs.text:
The chart nereus-reefs holds every kind, kept on uninstall, so a plain helm upgrade updates them.

helm upgrade --install nereus-reefs \
  oci://ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus-reefs \
  --version 0.1.6 \
  --namespace nereus-system \
  --create-namespace \
  --wait
output
Release "nereus-reefs" does not exist. Installing it now.
Pulled: ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus-reefs:0.1.6
Digest: sha256:50389e42b8f2ed45423ca3c221607cc28aa1984c411c528912ec18daa5ac8246
NAME: nereus-reefs
NAMESPACE: nereus-system
STATUS: deployed
REVISION: 1
DESCRIPTION: Install complete

docs.title: 2. Install the Gateway API's kinds
docs.text:
The chart nereus renders the API's route only when the Gateway API's kinds exist, so apply them first, at the version nereus init uses.

kubectl apply --server-side --filename \
  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.7.0/standard-install.yaml

docs.title: 3. Install Nereus and the profile
docs.text:
The chart nereus brings the API and thetis, the installer Nereid, plus the Installation, the Profile and the registry CA as the Secret registry-ca. --take-ownership adopts the namespace of step 1.

helm upgrade --install nereus oci://ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus \
  --version 0.1.6 \
  --namespace nereus-system \
  --take-ownership \
  --set installation.name=nereus \
  --set profile=internal-developer-platform \
  --set ingress.address=http://localhost:8080 \
  --set-file registryCA.certificate=nereus/registry/ca.crt \
  --set-file registryCA.key=nereus/ca.key
output
Release "nereus" does not exist. Installing it now.
Pulled: ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus:0.1.6
Digest: sha256:2beceb8078d35e6ac4ebc90a0ba4cdd0bd873664794336fd22f5d953920e9a7f
NAME: nereus
NAMESPACE: nereus-system
STATUS: deployed
REVISION: 1
DESCRIPTION: Install complete

The profile is the file profiles/<profile>.yaml of the chart; a name with no file fails before anything is installed, listing the profiles there are.

docs.title: 4. Remove the CA key
docs.text: The key now lives in the Secret, kept on uninstall, and in Helm's release history in nereus-system. Delete the file with rm nereus/ca.key.

docs.title: 5. Wait for the profile
docs.text:
thetis installs each reef, Nereid and Mandate in the order of what each requires; the Profile is Ready when the last one is, in about 8 minutes.

kubectl get profiles.core.getnereus.dev nereus --watch
output
NAME     PROFILE                       READY   AGE
nereus   internal-developer-platform   True    8m30s

docs.title: 6. Log in
docs.text:
Helm writes no CLI config: set NEREUS_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 so every command finds the instance, then nereus login keeps that URL.

nereus login --use-device-code

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus reef list shows the same reefs nereus init --profile internal-developer-platform gives; nereus nereid list shows each Nereid Ready, from ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus.

nereus reef list
output
REEF            NEREIDS
authentication  keycloak
build           buildkit
catalog         catalog
database        cloudnative-pg
delivery        kubernetes
environment     vcluster
metrics         victoriametrics
portal          nereus-portal
registry        zot
release         flux
scm             forgejo
secrets         openbao
tenancy         -

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text: Delete the cluster with k3d cluster delete nereus and its folder with rm -r nereus.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Rebuild the kept cluster from a published version.
  • Keep a secret in the vault the profile made.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • Runtime and profiles: what a profile installs and in what order.

docs.title: Update the kept cluster without a rebuild
docs.text: Move one Nereid, or the Nereus API and its charts, of the kept cluster k3d-nereus to a new build, keeping the Installation and every reef, Nereid and secret.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The kept cluster of Rebuild the kept cluster, and a clone on main.
  • No scene of another session using the registry localhost:5111.

docs.title: 1. Build one Nereid's image
docs.text: Build it from main under the tag the cluster runs, then push it: make nereid-sdk, then docker build --build-arg API_GROUP=core.getnereus.dev --build-context nereid-sdk=lib/nereid/dist --tag localhost:5111/keycloak-controller:0.1.0 controllers/keycloak, then docker push that tag. make nereids NEREIDS=keycloak builds the same image but also rebuilds the API and thetis.

docs.title: 2. See what changes
docs.text:
nereus nereid apply --image with --dry-run compares the digest the Deployment pins with the new one.

nereus nereid apply keycloak \
  --image localhost:5111/keycloak-controller:0.1.0 \
  --dry-run
output
Would configure core/nereids/keycloak for reef authentication: image sha256:7daa642492a8 → sha256:3a50a7f56b45.
Nothing changed (--dry-run).

docs.title: 3. Apply it in place
docs.text:
The Deployment pins the new digest, and the Nereid's next pass applies what changed. Triton is a Nereid too, so it moves the same way.

nereus nereid apply keycloak \
  --image localhost:5111/keycloak-controller:0.1.0

docs.title: 4. Move the API and the charts
docs.text:
Run make cli, then make nereids, so the CLI and the images share a version. nereus init without --create-cluster upgrades the charts nereus-reefs and nereus in place; the API is ready a few seconds after the nereus line.

When the registry lacks an image at the CLI's version (make cli ran again after make nereids), init stops at its images step, before the nereus line, and changes nothing:

output
✗ images                    0.0s
  total                     0.0s  slo 8m, 0% green
✗ 2 images the release names are not in their registry: nereus-api, thetis
  nereus-api  localhost:5111/nereus-api:0.1.41.dev146
  thetis      localhost:5111/thetis-controller:0.1.41.dev146
  fix         make nereids

Run the fix line, then init again. A Pod that cannot pull its image anyway (ImagePullBackOff) stops the ready step at once, naming the Pod, its image and the same fix, instead of waiting for the step's timeout of 30 minutes.

nereus init \
  --target k3d \
  --name nereus \
  --profile internal-developer-platform \
  --yes

The output below is what test/scene-core-upgrade prints on its cluster, profile reference, after one Nereid was applied by hand: only that one stops, and the other six already run their new digests.

output
✓ kinds          1.2s  release nereus-reefs revision 2
✓ nereus         3.3s  release nereus revision 2, profile reference, images localhost:5111 at 0.1.41.dev129-nereus-scn-2031-9bab4b-next
✓ installation   0.3s  kept nereus-scn-2031-9bab4b
✗ ready         1m32s
  total         1m37s  slo 8m, 20% green
✗ the cluster's Nereids keep their images: thetis does not change an image that is already there
  reference-secrets  localhost:5111/reference-secrets-controller@sha256:0de294bd2444 → @sha256:780a0ec273e5
  fix                nereus nereid apply reference-secrets --reef secrets --image localhost:5111/reference-secrets-controller@sha256:780a0ec273e5ca09d10175bb3835eb75e899fbc34f2718c5a795bd8e79b71a93

thetis moves in place every Nereid whose image it installed itself: it records that image on the Nereid (the annotation core.getnereus.dev/profile-image), and while the Nereid still runs it, the new one replaces it. When nothing stops it, init's ready line counts them (7 Nereids ready, 6 moved by thetis).

A Nereid whose image was applied by hand, as in step 3, keeps it: thetis marks its step Blocked, reason ImageApplied, and the Profile's Ready condition says ImageApplied.

init stops as soon as it reads that, instead of waiting for its timeout, and names only those Nereids; the API, the charts and the Nereids it moved stay as they are. nereus doctor shows the same list in its profile row.

A Profile that names an image its registry lacks moves nothing either. thetis reads each image before it applies a Nereid: the step is Blocked, reason ImageMissing, with the image, and the steps after it go on, so a Nereid already there keeps its own. The Profile's Ready condition says ImageMissing; init stops at once and adds the fix:

✗ ready          2 Nereids name an image the registry lacks: database, secrets
  database  localhost:5111/database-controller:0.1.41.dev146
  secrets   localhost:5111/secrets-controller:0.1.41.dev146
  fix       make nereids

nereus doctor's profile row says the same, with the same fix, before any image a Nereid keeps.

A registry that does not answer leaves the step Waiting for the next pass.

A Nereid installed before thetis recorded its images has no annotation, so the first update after it lists every such Nereid once; their fix lines adopt them, and the next update moves them.

docs.title: 5. Move each Nereid applied by hand that should change
docs.text: Run each fix line init printed, as in steps 2 and 3. thetis's next pass finds every image as the Profile names it, records it, and the Profile turns Ready.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text: nereus nereid list shows each Nereid Ready with the image you applied, and nereus status shows every reef Ready.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Rebuild the kept cluster when an in-place update is not enough.
  • Get a reef's commands working again when a Nereid has no pod serving.

docs.title: Rebuild the kept cluster
docs.text:
Rebuild k3d-nereus, the kept cluster used as production, from nothing: the profile internal-developer-platform Ready, and Triton, the realm and the portal at their public hostnames.

The owner's job

An agent never deletes or recreates this cluster: the guard .claude/hooks/guard-kept-cluster refuses it. The rebuild loses OpenBao's secrets, Keycloak's database and the NATS streams of Triton's orders.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A clone on main, and no scene of another session using the registry localhost:5111.
  • ~/.config/nereus/google-keycloak.env, exporting GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET of the Google OAuth client.
  • The tunnel's credentials, ~/.cloudflared/<UUID>.json from cloudflared tunnel create nereus, mode 0400: the one piece that cannot be made again without Cloudflare's dashboard. On a new machine, copy ~/.cloudflared/ and ~/.config/nereus/.

docs.title: 1. Build the CLI and every Nereid from the checkout
docs.text: nereus init installs the images at the version of the nereus on the PATH, and make nereids tags them with the checkout's version, so build both from the same commit: make cli, then make nereids.

docs.title: 2. Delete and create the cluster
docs.text:
In the owner's terminal (in Claude Code, ! first): k3d cluster delete nereus, then nereus init. About 9 minutes; the tenancy tree comes with it.

nereus init \
  --target k3d \
  --create-cluster \
  --name nereus \
  --profile internal-developer-platform \
  --yes

docs.title: 3. Log in as the initial admin
docs.text:
The realm answers at http://auth.localhost:8080 from the start. nereus login --initial-admin reads the admin's password with your kubeconfig.

nereus login --initial-admin

docs.title: 4. Bring up the tunnel and trust it at the ingress gateway
docs.text:
Apply the edge reef and its Nereid cloudflare (Publish at a hostname), keep the credentials file as the secret edge/cloudflare-tunnel, then create the Mandate with --param tunnel=nereus --param credentialsSecret=edge/cloudflare-tunnel --default. Create the three routes at once: until a Route exists, the tunnel answers 404.

nereus edge route create triton --hostname triton.getnereus.dev

Repeat for auth and portal.

numTrustedProxies: 1 keeps cloudflared's X-Forwarded-Proto: https, so Keycloak's issuer stays https://. Write the Release istio-gateway with --values-file deploy/ingress/istio-gateway-values.yaml --dry-run --output yaml, nereus release apply it, then kubectl apply --filename deploy/ingress/gateway.yaml.

docs.title: 5. Put Google in the realm
docs.text:
Only once the tunnel answers. Source the env file, keep the pair as the secret google-oauth-keycloak, then apply the Mandate; mandate apply replaces every param, so all go together. Then nereus logout and nereus login at the public realm.

nereus mandate apply keycloak \
  --reef authentication \
  --nereid keycloak \
  --param publicUrl=https://auth.getnereus.dev \
  --param googleSecret=google-oauth-keycloak \
  --param googleUsers=owner@example.com \
  --param googleAdmins=owner@example.com

docs.title: 6. Set the portal's address and bring up Triton
docs.text:
nereus mandate apply nereus-portal with --param publicUrl=https://portal.getnereus.dev.

Then the Mandate messaging-nats is the messaging reef's default with no match (--default, no --match), so it holds the Rooms' Topics, which name no engine (ADR 0030).

A cluster that had --param agents=true there keeps the old streams of the account AGENTS on the claim, unread, and the Secret nats-triton of nereus-system: drop the parameter, run nereus nereid apply nats --reef messaging again, and delete the Secret by hand.

The rooms reef needs no parameter of it and no NATS account of its own (#2078): nereus reef apply rooms installs the rooms reef. Triton's issuer is the public realm of step 5, given with --set (#2157); without it Triton stops with --issuer is required.

nereus reef apply rooms
nereus nereid apply triton \
  --reef rooms \
  --set TRITON_ISSUER=https://auth.getnereus.dev/realms/nereus \
  --set TRITON_JWKS_URL=http://keycloak-server-http.nereus-system.svc:8180/realms/nereus/protocol/openid-connect/certs \
  --set TRITON_RESOURCE_URL=https://triton.getnereus.dev/mcp

POST https://triton.getnereus.dev/mcp with no token answers 401.

Every other login is gone with the old realm: the claude.ai connector Triton signs in again, and a token saved from the old realm no longer works.

docs.title: 7. Make yourself an administrator User
docs.text:
A new instance has no User or binding, so your every call passes through the nereus-admins emergency exit (ADR 0027, teams, roles and Users) and nereus doctor warns emergency-exit. nereus user create takes the e-mail of step 5; nereus authorization binding create gives it administrator (#2159).

nereus user create owner --email owner@example.com
nereus authorization binding create owner-admin --role administrator --user owner
nereus authorization can-i create core/users
output
✓ core/users/owner created
✓ authorization/bindings/owner-admin created
yes: authorization/bindings/owner-admin gives administrator to user/owner at the whole instance

From then on your calls take the normal check, and the doctor's count of emergency-exit passes stops growing; its warning goes when the API restarts. You stay in nereus-admins, so the exit is still there for an emergency.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus status shows every reef Ready; curl on https://triton.getnereus.dev/healthz and https://portal.getnereus.dev/ answers 200, and the realm master answers 404 from outside.

nereus status
output
REEF            NEREID           VERSION  STATUS  AGE
authentication  keycloak         0.1.0    Ready   7m
catalog         catalog          0.1.0    Ready   1m
core            nereus-api       0.1.0    Ready   9m
                thetis           0.1.0    Ready   9m
database        cloudnative-pg   0.1.0    Ready   7m
delivery        kubernetes       0.1.0    Ready   1m
environment     vcluster         0.1.0    Ready   1m
metrics         victoriametrics  0.1.0    Ready   3m
portal          nereus-portal    0.1.0    Ready   3m
registry        zot              0.1.0    Ready   1m
release         flux             0.1.0    Ready   7m
secrets         openbao          0.1.0    Ready   9m
tenancy         -                -        Ready   9m
Registry  localhost:5111

docs.text:

  • Deploy main to the live cluster.

docs.title: Meet the time SLO
docs.text: See and change the time objective nereus init is measured against: 8 minutes on k3d, 20 on a cloud, by default (spec 0004).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • A cluster from Prepare the cluster. The defaults live in the CLI; the cluster may override them in one ServiceLevelObjective object in nereus-system, whose name and shape are provisional.

docs.title: 1. See each value and where it came from
docs.text:
nereus config slo show prints the objective of each target (local, cloud), the shares of it where the clock changes colour (yellow, orange, red), and the tolerance. cloud is recorded, not checked yet.

nereus config slo show
output
SETTING    VALUE  SOURCE
local      8m     default
cloud      20m    default
yellow     50%    default
orange     75%    default
red        100%   default
tolerance  20%    default

docs.title: 2. Change some
docs.text:
nereus config slo set writes only what you give; the rest keep their defaults.

nereus config slo set --local 4m --tolerance 5
output
SETTING    VALUE  SOURCE
local      4m     cluster
cloud      20m    default
yellow     50%    default
orange     75%    default
red        100%   default
tolerance  5%     cluster

docs.title: 3. Read the bands on the next init
docs.text:
The next nereus init reads them once its kinds are applied: on a cluster it just created, the defaults hold. A step that crossed into a band says so on its line; red reports a miss, and init still finishes. With a tight objective (--local 1s --yellow 10 --orange 20 --red 30), its last lines read:

nereus init --yes
output
✓ prerequisites             0.0s  docker 29.9.1, k3d 5.9.0, helm 4.1.4
✓ registry localhost:5111   0.0s  reused
✓ cluster nereus-local      0.1s  reused
✓ kinds                     0.4s  release nereus-reefs revision 2  slo 47% red
✓ nereus                    1.1s  release nereus revision 2, profile core
✓ installation              0.3s  kept nereus-local
  total                     1.8s  slo 1s, 180% red

Past the objective, init warns with the slowest steps and the command that raises it. With --check-slo, which the scenes that install a profile pass, init fails past objective plus tolerance and names the three slowest steps.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text: nereus config slo show prints cluster as the source of each value you set. A cluster set up before #313 may hold the former key spec.targets.azure: the table then opens with a warning, and any nereus config slo set moves it to cloud.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
nereus config slo reset deletes the object, and every value is back to its default.

nereus config slo reset
output
✓ SLO reset: every value is back to its default

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Rebuild the kept cluster, whose init the objective measures.

docs.title: Prepare the undercloud
docs.text:
Create the installation's undercloud, <installation>-undercloud, a local cluster with the cloud reef whose public OIDC issuer a cloud trusts, here Azure.

Recorded against fakes

The outputs are what init prints in its tests, against a fake k3d, a fake Nereid, a fake az and recorded Azure answers. A real subscription is checked by hand (#266).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• What Prepare the cluster needs, plus the image of the Nereid azure in the local registry: init reads its login label before the cluster exists, and stops naming it when it is missing.
  • az login done, with rights to create a resource group, a storage account and a managed identity.

docs.title: 1. Name the cloud and the installation
docs.text:
The settings file names both; a cloud target needs the installation's name, since it names everything created in the cloud. --target azure --installation-name tailwind does the same without a file.

apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: InitConfig
spec:
  cloud: azure
---
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Installation
metadata:
  name: tailwind
spec:
  id: 0b7e4c1a-93d2-4f6e-8a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b
  alias: tailwind

docs.title: 2. See the plan
docs.text:
nereus init --dry-run computes the issuer's URL from the installation's id, creates the cluster with it, and prints the plan for Azure; nothing runs there. --show-requests adds why each resource exists, each request's URL and its tags.

nereus init --dry-run --yes
output
✓ undercloud tailwind-undercloud on k3d    0s
✓ installation tailwind, new               0s
✓ Reef cloud, Nereid azure    0s

Plan for Azure · northeurope · 9 requests · not run (--dry-run)
  1  create   resource group        tailwind-platform
  2  create   storage account       issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e
  3  create   container             oidc
  4  access   Storage Blob Data Contributor on issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e to you
  5  publish  issuer documents (3)
  6  create   managed identity      tailwind-cloud-provisioner
  7  create   federated credential  tailwind-undercloud-azure
  tagged with the installation and who asked
  --show-requests for the why, URLs and tags

Nothing ran in Azure. To run it:
$ nereus init --yes --approve-access

docs.title: 3. Approve and run it
docs.text:
Without --approve-access, init asks Approve 9 requests? [y/N], and a non-interactive run stops. Each line then shows its progress, ending with the proof that Azure trusts the undercloud: the Nereid azure exchanging its token.

nereus init --yes --approve-access

A request Azure refuses marks its line ✗ and says what an administrator has to run (Connect to the cloud).

docs.title: 4. Run it again
docs.text: The cluster, the installation and the reef are kept, and the plan is made again. When the published keys are the cluster's own, nothing is uploaded; when they changed, the issuer is marked Stale and the upload planned. A cluster presenting another issuer is recreated, but only one whose namespace says undercloud and whose Installation has this name and id.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text: The run ends with ✓ azure exchanged its token as tailwind-cloud-provisioner. Each run that sends requests writes a log, readable by you alone, in ~/.local/state/nereus/logs/: the plan, each request and its answer's status, never a token.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Connect to the cloud: the Nereid azure and what it may do.
  • Meet the time SLO: the cloud target counts against 20 minutes.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Undercloud and overcloud.
  • Spec 0005: the cloud reef and the issuer.

docs.title: Say what Nereus has
docs.text: Register what a repository says it runs and publishes, Workloads and Packages, from its files in catalog/, and check that it holds together: the files are the truth, the catalog reef holds a copy.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A cluster from Prepare the cluster with --profile internal-developer-platform: it brings the catalog reef with its Nereid catalog, which writes each entry's status and changes nothing an entry names.
  • The tenancy tree the entries name as owners.
  • A checkout with a catalog/ folder, such as Nereus's own.

docs.title: 1. Register the repository's catalog
docs.text:
nereus catalog apply takes the folder, types first, then the entries. An owner that does not exist, or a registry a type does not take, refuses the whole folder; a second run prints unchanged.

nereus catalog apply \
  --from-file catalog/
output
✓ catalog/workloadtypes/controller created
✓ catalog/workloadtypes/service created
✓ catalog/packagetypes/cli created
✓ catalog/packagetypes/image created
✓ catalog/workloads/flux created (owner: Project/nereids, type: controller)
✓ catalog/workloads/keycloak created (owner: Project/nereids, type: controller)
✓ catalog/workloads/openbao created (owner: Project/nereids, type: controller)
✓ catalog/workloads/triton created (owner: Project/triton, type: service)
✓ catalog/packages/nereus created (owner: Project/core, type: cli, registry: pypi)
✓ catalog/packages/openbao-image created (owner: Project/nereids, type: image, registry: oci)

Next steps:

  nereus catalog check

docs.title: 2. Write a new entry as a file
docs.text:
nereus catalog workload create with --dry-run --output yaml prints the file to commit in catalog/, then apply. --audience is required: none says nobody talks to it. Without --owner, the owner set by nereus config set owner is used.

nereus catalog workload create edge-cloudflare \
  --type controller \
  --audience none \
  --ref branch=main \
  --dry-run \
  --output yaml
output
apiVersion: catalog.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workload
metadata:
  name: edge-cloudflare
spec:
  owner:
    kind: Project
    name: nereids
  type: controller
  source:
    ref:
      branch: main

docs.title: 3. Check that it holds together
docs.text:
nereus catalog check fails with ✗ on a contradiction, such as an owner whose Project was deleted; a gap prints ! with its issue and passes. A lookup that did not run is a gap, never a pass.

nereus catalog check
output
✓ tenancy: 1 organization, 5 projects, every owner resolves
✓ types: every workload type and package type resolves, every registry allowed
! catalog/workloads/triton: audience people, agents, no edge reef (#470)
! catalog/workloads/triton: uses nats, no messaging reef (#576)
! catalog/packages/nereus: not found on pypi
0 contradictions, 3 gaps

make catalog-check runs it on the repository's files before a pull request, with a cluster that has the tenancy reef.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus catalog list shows each Workload with what the catalog Nereid found, - until its first pass.

nereus catalog list
output
WORKLOAD  OWNER            TYPE        AUDIENCE        STATUS
catalog   Project/nereids  controller  -               Ready
flux      Project/nereids  controller  -               NereidNotInstalled
keycloak  Project/nereids  controller  -               NereidNotInstalled
openbao   Project/nereids  controller  -               NereidNotInstalled
triton    Project/triton   service     agents, people  DeploymentNotFound

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Follow the golden path: a Workload deployed into an Environment of its own.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• The catalog reef: Workloads, Packages, their types, every status and command.
  • ADR 0016: the files in the repository are the truth, the cluster holds a copy.

docs.title: Follow the golden path
docs.text: Run your own image in an Environment of its own, a vcluster, from docker build to a Pod that answers, through a ready-made chart and with no product code.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A cluster from Prepare the cluster with --profile internal-developer-platform, and nereus login done: it brings the environment reef with the Nereid vcluster, the catalog, the delivery reef with the Nereid kubernetes, and the release reef with flux.
  • The workload type service from the repository's catalog, as in Say what Nereus has.
  • Your image pushed to the registry that nereus status names, such as docker build --tag localhost:5111/hello:0.1.0 test/golden-path, then docker push localhost:5111/hello:0.1.0. The same reference pushes and pulls, from your machine and from the nodes.

docs.title: 1. Get an Environment
docs.text:
nereus environment create makes a vcluster for an owner, deleted when it expires. It is small unless its Mandate says otherwise: 20 Pods, 512Mi per container. Its Pods reach one another and the Internet, never the platform's own Services.

nereus environment create dev \
  --owner project/nereus \
  --expires 2h
output
✓ environment/environments/dev created (mandate: vcluster, nereid: vcluster)

Next steps:

  nereus environment get dev --watch
  nereus environment kubeconfig dev

docs.title: 2. Say what runs
docs.text:
A Workload is the catalog's entry: who owns it, its type and who talks to it. nereus workload create is short for nereus catalog workload create.

nereus workload create hello \
  --owner project/nereids \
  --type service \
  --audience programs
output
✓ catalog/workloads/hello created (owner: Project/nereids, type: service)

Next steps:

  nereus catalog workload list

docs.title: 3. Deploy it
docs.text:
nereus workload deploy takes hello@dev, the Workload and the Environment: a bare hello is refused, since a deploy always says where it goes. The Nereid kubernetes resolves the tag to a digest, reads the port the image exposes, and releases a ready-made chart in the vcluster.

nereus workload deploy hello@dev \
  --image localhost:5111/hello:0.1.0
output
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev created

Next steps:

  nereus delivery get hello-dev

A tag moves only with a deploy: push the same tag with other content and deploy again for a new digest, the previous one kept. --wait waits on the deploy and prints the Nereid's reason when it cannot deliver.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus delivery get --watch follows the Delivery until its Pod is ready.

nereus delivery get hello-dev \
  --watch
output
NAME       WORKLOAD  ENVIRONMENT  DIGEST  NAMESPACE  READY
hello-dev  hello     dev          -       -          Unknown
hello-dev  hello     dev          sha256:fdeec3  hello-dev  False
hello-dev  hello     dev          sha256:fdeec3  hello-dev  True

Next steps:

  nereus workload logs hello-dev

nereus workload logs reads the Pods' output through the Nereus API, with no kubeconfig and no port-forward of yours; --follow stays until Ctrl+C.

nereus workload logs hello-dev
output
[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:53792: response:200

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
Deleted for good

Deleting the Environment deletes its vcluster and everything inside it.

Delete the Delivery first: an Environment that a Delivery still targets is refused. nereus delivery delete removes its Release, so Flux uninstalls the chart.

nereus delivery delete hello-dev \
  --timeout 300
output
2026-11-04T17:26:05Z  … release  Deleting release/releases/hello-dev: Flux uninstalls the chart.
2026-11-04T17:26:06Z  · target   Deleting release/targets/hello-dev.
2026-11-04T17:26:38Z  ✓ release  release/releases/hello-dev deleted.
2026-11-04T17:26:37Z  … target   Deleting release/targets/hello-dev.
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev deleted

Next steps:

  nereus workload list

nereus environment delete dev \
  --timeout 600
output
2026-11-04T17:26:47Z  … release    Deleting release/releases/env-dev: Flux uninstalls the vcluster chart.
2026-11-04T17:26:47Z  · namespace  Deleting the namespace env-vcluster-dev.
2026-11-04T17:27:15Z  ✓ release    release/releases/env-dev deleted.
2026-11-04T17:27:14Z  … namespace  Deleting the namespace env-vcluster-dev.
✓ environment/environments/dev deleted

Next steps:

  nereus environment list

  • Collect metrics: see how each Nereid is doing.

docs.text:

  • The delivery reef: Deliveries, the chart they release and why one fails.

docs.title: Use the MCP server
docs.text: Reach the tools of the installed reefs from Claude Code or claude.ai: the Nereus API serves /mcp itself, each tool run as you, through the installation's entrance as /v1 is.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An installation reachable at https://nereus.example.com, and nereus login done, from Turn on authentication.
  • To choose the tools the installation offers, a login in nereus-admins.

docs.title: 1. See the tools you may call
docs.text:
nereus mcp tool list shows each tool the installed reefs declare whose route you may call, the core's status first. A tool whose route is a POST shows off (write): it starts off until an admin enables it.

nereus mcp tool list
output
REEF           TOOL                STATE
core           status              on
presentations  presentations_list  on

docs.title: 2. Choose the tools the installation offers
docs.text:
An admin turns tools off or on with nereus mcp tool disable and enable, by name or every tool of a reef (<reef>_*). An exact name beats a pattern.

nereus mcp tool disable presentations_list
output
✓ tool presentations_list disabled for the instance

nereus mcp tool enable 'presentations_*'
output
✓ tools presentations_* enabled for the instance
! presentations_list stays off: disabled by its own name, which beats a pattern

The switch lives in the Installation's spec.mcp.tools; /mcp lists and calls only the tools on, and the list shows the others as off (instance). It is never changed through /mcp itself.

docs.title: 3. Add it to Claude Code
docs.text:
nereus mcp client add runs Claude Code's own claude mcp add, so it never writes the agent's settings or copies your token into them. --dry-run shows that command; --scope user, the default, adds the server to every project.

nereus mcp client add claude-code \
  --dry-run
output
would run: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user --client-id claude-code --callback-port 33418 nereus https://nereus.example.com/mcp

nereus mcp client add claude-code
output
✓ claude-code: MCP server nereus added (https://nereus.example.com/mcp, scope user, OAuth client claude-code)

Next steps:

  claude    # then /mcp, and log in to nereus

In Claude Code, /mcp opens the realm's login page in the browser.

docs.title: 4. Add it to claude.ai
docs.text:
In claude.ai, add a custom connector with the URL https://nereus.example.com/mcp and the OAuth Client ID claude. The client finds the issuer from the protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) and logs in with a token only /mcp accepts.

curl --silent https://nereus.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
output
{"resource":"https://nereus.example.com/mcp","authorization_servers":["https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus"],"scopes_supported":["openid","offline_access"],"bearer_methods_supported":["header"]}

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
After the login, the Claude Code session lists the same tools as nereus mcp tool list. /mcp is stateless: a reef installed or uninstalled shows on the client's next connection. nereus mcp client list shows the coding agents that have it.

nereus mcp client list
output
CLIENT       SERVER  URL                             SCOPE
claude-code  nereus  https://nereus.example.com/mcp  user

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
nereus mcp client remove claude-code
output
✓ claude-code: MCP server nereus removed

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Join the team's room: your coding agent among the team's agents.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • ADR 0029: each reef declares its tools in its Nereid's contract, and the Nereus API serves them.

docs.title: Send messages
docs.text:
Give a project a topic and a queue on NATS, each with a Secret that says where to reach it, made by the nats Nereid. The Mandate picks the Nereid, so the code asks for an engine, never for a server.

A topic carries each message to everyone who listens, on the subject topics.<name>. A queue keeps each message until one worker takes it, in the JetStream stream queue-<name> on queues.<name>. To put a coding agent in the team's room, see Join the team's room.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • A cluster from Prepare the cluster, with the tenancy tree its profile seeds: the owner of each topic and queue, here the project triton, must exist in it.

docs.title: 1. Apply the messaging reef
docs.text:
nereus reef apply brings the two kinds.

nereus reef apply messaging
output
✓ core/reefs/messaging 0.1.0 created (messaging.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: queues, topics)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef messaging

docs.title: 2. Apply the nats Nereid and its Mandate
docs.text:
nereus nereid apply nats runs NATS next to the Nereid in its Pod, with JetStream on the claim nats-data.

nereus nereid apply nats \
  --reef messaging
output
✓ core/nereids/nats created, Ready, pinned to sha256:<digest>: see 'nereus messaging --help'

Next steps:

  nereus mandate create messaging-nats --reef messaging --nereid nats --match engine=nats --param jetstream=true

The Mandate takes every request of engine nats; jetstream=true is what queues need. A second Mandate with the same match is refused.

nereus mandate create messaging-nats \
  --reef messaging \
  --nereid nats \
  --match engine=nats \
  --param jetstream=true
output
✓ core/mandates/messaging-nats created (reef: messaging, nereid: nats, match: engine=nats)

docs.title: 3. Create a topic
docs.text:
nereus messaging topic create names the owner and the engine. An owner missing from the tree is refused before anything is written.

nereus messaging topic create orders \
  --owner project/triton \
  --engine nats
output
✓ messaging/topics/orders created (mandate: messaging-nats, nereid: nats)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging topic get orders

docs.title: 4. Create a queue
docs.text:
nereus messaging queue create takes the same flags.

nereus messaging queue create builds \
  --owner project/triton \
  --engine nats
output
✓ messaging/queues/builds created (mandate: messaging-nats, nereid: nats)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging queue get builds

docs.title: 5. Create one from a file
docs.text:
A dry run writes the YAML that nereus messaging queue apply takes. --deletion-policy delete drops the stream and its messages with the queue; retain, the default, keeps them.

nereus messaging queue create scratch \
  --owner project/triton \
  --engine nats \
  --deletion-policy delete \
  --dry-run \
  --output yaml > scratch.yaml

nereus messaging queue apply \
  --from-file scratch.yaml
output
✓ messaging/queues/scratch created

Next steps:

  nereus messaging queue list

A topic works the same way, with nereus messaging topic apply.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text: nereus messaging topic list and nereus messaging queue list show each one Ready, with the Mandate and the Nereid that took it. nereus messaging queue get names the Secret that says where to reach it: builds-queue in nereus-system, with the keys host, port, uri, subject and stream.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
nereus messaging queue delete follows the queue's deletion policy.

nereus messaging queue delete builds
output
✓ messaging/queues/builds deleted (deletionPolicy: retain, its messages are kept)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging queue list

nereus messaging queue delete scratch
output
✓ messaging/queues/scratch deleted (deletionPolicy: delete)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging queue list

nereus messaging topic delete orders
output
✓ messaging/topics/orders deleted (deletionPolicy: retain, its messages are kept)

Next steps:

  nereus messaging topic list

docs.title: Next

docs.title: Collect metrics
docs.text: See how each Nereid is doing, its passes, failures and how long a pass takes, in the metrics the platform keeps with VictoriaMetrics.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A cluster from Prepare the cluster with --profile internal-developer-platform: it brings the metrics reef with the Nereid victoriametrics, which scrapes every Nereid in nereus-system and each node's CPU and memory per container.
  • kubectl reaching that cluster. The query API has no credentials yet, so only the scraper, the Nereus API and a port-forward reach it.

docs.title: 1. Open vmui
docs.text:
The Mandate victoriametrics publishes the in-cluster query address in status.query.url (nereus mandate get). From your machine, forward a port to it, then open http://localhost:8428/vmui. The --context names the cluster nereus init made.

kubectl port-forward service/vmsingle-nereus 8428:8428 \
  --context k3d-nereus \
  --namespace nereus-system

docs.title: 2. Count each Nereid's passes
docs.text:
The queries are MetricsQL, a superset of PromQL. Each Nereid built on nereid-sdk serves its metrics with the label nereid, taken from its Pod, so no Pod can pose as a Nereid. One series per Nereid: its reconcile passes since it started.

sum by (nereid) (nereus_nereid_reconcile_total)

docs.title: 3. See which failed, and why
docs.text:
A Nereid that never failed has no error series, so or adds a zero for it from the passes, and every Nereid shows up.

sum by (nereid) (nereus_nereid_reconcile_errors_total) or sum by (nereid) (nereus_nereid_reconcile_total) * 0

The errors carry a reason label, the cause of a failed pass: group by (nereid, reason) to see them.

docs.title: 4. See how long a pass takes
docs.text:
The duration is a histogram. The 95th percentile over the last five minutes, per Nereid:

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (nereid, le) (rate(nereus_nereid_reconcile_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
The same port answers the Prometheus query API, for scripts: the first query returns one series per Nereid. A target that fails shows as down, and nothing else stops.

curl --get \
  --data-urlencode 'query=sum by (nereid) (nereus_nereid_reconcile_total)' \
  http://localhost:8428/api/v1/query

docs.text:
