  • Runtime and profiles: why another Nereid of the metrics reef would publish the same status.query.url.

docs.title: Run a registry
docs.text: Run a zot registry of your own in the cluster, publish an image to it and run that image: TLS only, nothing anonymous, images kept on its own volume.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A cluster from Prepare the cluster with --profile internal-developer-platform: it brings the registry reef with the Nereid zot, the release reef that installs zot, and the secrets reef that keeps each registry's read credential.
  • nereus login done: publishing pushes through the Nereus API, for a person in nereus-admins.
  • The namespace builds, which nereus nereid apply buildkit --reef build makes: each repository's push identity lives there.
  • An image built locally with a tag, such as docker build --tag hello:v1 ..
  • A k3d cluster: on AKS the registry reef is planned, since the nodes pull only from registries whose certificate they trust, and they do not trust the CA of a registry in the cluster (Prepare a cluster for Nereus).

docs.title: 1. Create a registry
docs.text:
nereus registry create makes a namespace registry-<name> with zot and a 10 GiB volume. The first registry also makes the vault registries. --purge-unused is optional: it deletes each image no Delivery runs once older than the duration, keeping the newest of each repository.

nereus registry create main \
  --purge-unused 168h
output
secrets/vaults/registries created
registry/registries/main created (mandate: zot, nereid: zot; purge: images no Delivery runs, after 168h)

docs.title: 2. Publish an image
docs.text:
nereus registry repository publish creates the repository with a push identity of its own and pushes the local image through the Nereus API with your login; your docker configuration stays untouched. A tag is published once: the same tag again is refused.

nereus registry repository publish hello \
  --registry main \
  --image hello:v1
output
registry/registries/main/repositories/hello created
registry/registries/main/repositories/hello/tags/v1 published (sha256:97683bd68ee3e86c6560172b9f6e0b371a6bbcebf06041dbe7284355a7703797)

Next steps:

  nereus workload deploy hello@<environment> --image localhost:30763/hello:v1

docs.title: 3. Run it
docs.text:
nereus workload deploy runs the image in an Environment, here dev from Follow the golden path. Name the address the publish printed; the Pod runs the digest found behind the tag. A registry with an owner serves only a Workload and an Environment of that owner or under it in the tenancy tree.

nereus workload deploy hello@dev \
  --image localhost:30763/hello:v1 \
  --wait
output
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev configured
✓ delivery/deliveries/hello-dev ready (sha256:de1338)

Next steps:

  nereus workload logs hello-dev

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus registry get shows the registry ready, its pull address for the nodes and the credential that reads it.

nereus registry get main
output
NAME  NEREID  PURGE  PULL-ADDRESS     READY
main  zot     168h   localhost:30763  True

credential: secret registries/main-pull (vault registries)

localhost:30763 is a NodePort, for an image reference on this cluster's nodes. Reading it takes the credential above.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
Deleted for good

The registry's namespace and volume go with it, and every image on the volume.

A repository that a Delivery runs is refused, and so is a registry that still has repositories: delete the Deliveries first.

nereus registry repository delete hello
output
✗ registry/repositories/hello is still in use by delivery/deliveries/hello-dev. To delete it, run:
  # first, the Deliveries that run its images
  nereus delivery delete hello-dev
  nereus registry repository delete hello

nereus registry delete main
output
registry/registries/main deleted

Next steps:

  nereus registry list

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Follow the golden path: an Environment of your own, and a Workload deployed into it.
  • Run what a Build pushed: nereus workload deploy --build takes the Build's digest instead of a tag.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• The registry reef: registries, repositories, purge and every command.
  • Tenancy and access: who may read a registry with an owner.

docs.title: Release a chart
docs.text: Release a Helm chart into a namespace, with its values and its secrets, through the Nereid that its Mandate picks: Flux here, swappable for another tool.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A cluster from Prepare the cluster with --profile internal-developer-platform: it brings the release reef with the Nereid flux as its default, and the secrets reef.
  • A secret google-oauth from Keep a secret, in a vault that allows the target's namespace.
  • A file keycloak-values.yaml with the chart's values.

docs.title: 1. Point at the chart repository
docs.text:
A Repository says where charts come from: http for a Helm repository, oci for a registry.

nereus release repository create codecentric \
  --url https://codecentric.github.io/helm-charts \
  --type http
output
✓ release/repositories/codecentric created
NAME         TYPE  URL                                        READY
codecentric  http  https://codecentric.github.io/helm-charts  True

Next steps:

  nereus release source create <name> --repository codecentric --chart <chart> --version <version>

docs.title: 2. Pick the chart and its version
docs.text:
A Source is one chart at one version.

nereus release source create keycloak \
  --repository codecentric \
  --chart keycloakx \
  --version 7.0.1
output
✓ release/sources/keycloak created
NAME      REPOSITORY   CHART      VERSION  DIGEST  READY
keycloak  codecentric  keycloakx  7.0.1    -       True

Next steps:

  nereus release target create <name> --namespace <namespace>

docs.title: 3. Say where it goes
docs.text:
A Target is a namespace, made when missing. --environment picks an environment of the environment reef; without it, the target is in the cluster Nereus runs in.

nereus release target create dev-identity \
  --environment dev \
  --namespace identity
output
✓ release/targets/dev-identity created
NAME          ENVIRONMENT  NAMESPACE  READY
dev-identity  dev          identity   True

Next steps:

  nereus release create <name> --source <source> --target dev-identity

docs.title: 4. Release it with its values and secrets
docs.text:
nereus release create puts the source in the target. --secret makes a Kubernetes Secret with every key of a secret in the target's namespace; --secret-value <path>=<secret>/<key> puts one key into one values field. The CLI refuses a vault that does not allow the namespace before writing anything.

nereus release create keycloak \
  --source keycloak \
  --target dev-identity \
  --values-file keycloak-values.yaml \
  --mandate flux \
  --secret google-oauth \
  --secret-value nereus.googleClientId=google-oauth/GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
output
✓ release/releases/keycloak created (nereid: flux)
  binding secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth/secretbindings/identity/keycloak
  binding secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth/secretbindings/nereus-system/keycloak-values-google-oauth

Next steps:

  nereus release get keycloak --watch

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus release get --watch follows the release: the secret bindings first, then the chart, until it is Ready.

nereus release get keycloak \
  --watch
output
NAME      SOURCE    TARGET        VERSION  NEREID             STATUS
keycloak  keycloak  dev-identity  7.0.1    flux    Pending
2026-10-30T07:53:21Z  ✓ binding      2 Secrets ready: identity/keycloak, nereus-system/keycloak-values-google-oauth.
2026-10-30T07:53:21Z  ✓ helmrelease  Wrote the Flux HelmRelease keycloak.
keycloak  keycloak  dev-identity  7.0.1    flux    Progressing
keycloak  keycloak  dev-identity  7.0.1    flux    Ready

A release that fails shows Failed once Flux stops retrying; a refused namespace or a failed binding shows BindingFailed.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Run a registry to publish your own chart with nereus release source publish.
  • Follow the golden path: your own image, deployed through a ready-made chart into an Environment of its own.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• The release reef: repositories, sources, targets and releases, every command.
  • Runtime and profiles: why the Mandate, not the reef, picks Flux.

docs.title: Create a room for your team
docs.text: Give your team a room of its own on Triton, beside the repository's: a Room of the rooms reef, owned by your team's project, which Triton backs with a Topic of the messaging reef. A member of the team creates it with no admin, and every member's agent can join it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You are in the team's room already: Join the team's room (the CLI, nereus login, and your login in the group nereus-team).
  • The installation has the rooms reef and Triton (nereus reef list shows rooms).

docs.title: 1. Create the room
docs.text:
nereus rooms create makes the Room; without --owner, your team's owner. Triton applies its Topic, room-<room>, closed to every other client.

nereus rooms create ops \
  --owner project/payments \
  --description "Operations peers"
output
✓ rooms/rooms/ops created (owner: project/payments)

Next steps:

  nereus rooms get ops

Past the default Mandate's maxRooms, 20 by default, the command refuses and names what an admin runs to raise it.

docs.title: 2. Put your agent in it
docs.text:
nereus rooms join opens Claude Code with an agent in the room. From a session already open, its agent runs the same command from its Bash tool and joins one more room with no restart; nereus rooms leave takes it out of one room and keeps it in the others.

nereus rooms join ops

docs.title: 3. Tell the room without an agent
docs.text:
nereus rooms post posts as you, with no agent's session.

nereus rooms post "k3d-nereus is mine until 21:30" \
  --room ops
output
✓ rooms/rooms/ops note posted (id m-20261122-0128)

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus rooms get shows the Room, its Ready Peers and whether its Topic is ready; nereus rooms follow --room ops shows its messages.

nereus rooms get ops
output
NAME  OWNER             DESCRIPTION       PEERS  MESSAGES  READY
ops   project/payments  Operations peers  2      -         True

PEERS: ana.doto (Ready), bia.speo (Ready)

nereus rooms session list --room ops shows each room session, from the first peer in to the last one out, which Triton writes as a RoomSession. The messages stay on the Topic while its retention keeps them; there is no file of them yet.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text: nereus rooms delete ops --yes removes the Room and its Topic; with deletionPolicy: retain, the default, the engine keeps the messages. Only admins delete a room for now.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Join the team's room: the walkthrough for a new person of the team.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• The rooms reef: rooms, peers, room sessions and the conversation, every command.
  • Triton: the rooms reef's Nereid.

docs.title: Connect an organisation
docs.text: Connect an organisation of a source host to Nereus through the GitHub App an scm Mandate names: you write the organisation, and the github Nereid writes whether the App reaches it. A Connection holds no key and no token.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • The App's Mandate github, Ready, from Prove a GitHub App installed. For GitHub to deliver events, give that Mandate the App's webhook secret in --param webhookSecret=<secret>.

docs.title: 1. Apply the scm reef and the github Nereid
docs.text:
The scm reef is opt-in, outside the internal-developer-platform profile. One github Nereid serves both the authentication and the scm reef.

nereus reef apply scm
output
✓ core/reefs/scm created (scm.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: connections)

nereus nereid apply names both reefs.

nereus nereid apply github \
  --reef authentication \
  --reef scm
output
✓ core/nereids/github created, Ready, pinned to sha256:1e74cbc6a968: see 'nereus authentication --help'
  namespaces/nereus-system-github applied (the github Nereid's Role there, where vault default delivers the App keys)

Next steps:

  nereus mandate create github --reef authentication --nereid github --param appId=<id> --param privateKey=<secret> --param allow=<namespace>:<repository>:<permission>=<level> --default
  nereus mandate create github-scm --reef scm --nereid github --param identity=github --default

docs.title: 2. Bind the scm reef to the App
docs.text:
nereus mandate create binds the scm reef to the Nereid. Its name follows <nereid>-<reef>, and its param identity names the App's Mandate; a second App is a second scm Mandate.

nereus mandate create github-scm \
  --reef scm \
  --nereid github \
  --param identity=github \
  --default
output
✓ core/mandates/github-scm created (reef: scm, nereid: github, default)
  clusterrole/controller-github configured (nereid github writes the status of mandate github-scm)

Next steps:

  nereus mandate list

docs.title: 3. Connect the organisations
docs.text:
nereus scm connection create names one organisation. The first Connection is the reef's default; --mandate picks another scm Mandate.

nereus scm connection create example \
  --org example
output
✓ scm/connections/example created (mandate github-scm)

Next steps:

  nereus scm connection get example

Connect labs, meta and some the same way, with --org example-labs, example-meta and example-some. A second --default is refused: one in the reef.

nereus scm connection create other \
  --org example-other \
  --default
output
✗ scm/connections/example is the reef's default already: one in the reef. Nothing was changed.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus scm connection list shows what the App reaches on each organisation. There is no verify: the status is the check, from the first that fails: NotInstalled, NotAllRepositories, MissingPermissions (less than metadata and contents read), else Ready.

nereus scm connection list
output
CONNECTION  ORG           MANDATE     STATUS              DEFAULT
example     example       github-scm  Ready               yes
labs        example-labs  github-scm  NotInstalled        no
meta        example-meta  github-scm  MissingPermissions  no
some        example-some  github-scm  NotAllRepositories  no

nereus scm connection get says what to do about a status.

nereus scm connection get labs
output
Name:          labs
Org:           example-labs
Mandate:       github-scm
Nereid:        github
Default:       no
Status:        NotInstalled
Installation:  -
Repositories:  -
Permissions:   -
Message:       the App of mandate github is not installed on the organisation example-labs: install it at https://github.com/apps/example-nereus/installations/new

The App's webhook points at POST /scm/webhook on the github Nereid's Service, reached only inside the cluster for now: a delivery is accepted only when X-Hub-Signature-256 checks with the App's webhookSecret.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
nereus scm connection delete removes the Connection; the App stays installed on the organisation, and its Mandate in the authentication reef.

nereus scm connection delete labs
output
✓ scm/connections/labs deleted

Next steps:

  nereus scm connection list

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Mirror a repository of a connected organisation into the cluster.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• The scm reef: Connections and Mirrors, every command.
  • Reef, Nereid and Mandate: why a Mandate holds the App, never the Connection.

docs.title: Mirror a repository
docs.text: Copy a public Git repository into the cluster, where the forgejo Nereid keeps it in a Forgejo it runs, pulled again on an interval. A public source needs no Connection and no App.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The release reef with the flux Nereid, and the secrets reef with the openbao Nereid and the vault default: Forgejo comes from its upstream chart through the release reef, and its admin is sealed into the vault.
  • The profile internal-developer-platform brings the scm reef and the forgejo Nereid already: then go to step 2.

docs.title: 1. Apply the scm reef and the forgejo Nereid
docs.text:
nereus reef apply scm
output
✓ core/reefs/scm created (scm.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: connections)

nereus nereid apply installs the Nereid. It makes its own Mandate forgejo, asks the release reef for Forgejo (SQLite on a volume, no Ingress) and makes Forgejo's admin.

nereus nereid apply forgejo \
  --reef scm
output
✓ core/nereids/forgejo created, Ready: see 'nereus scm --help'
  core/mandates/forgejo created (reef: scm, nereid: forgejo)

Next steps:

  nereus scm mirror create <name> --from https://github.com/<owner>/<repository>

Forgejo copies from github.com only. The Nereid's setting MIRROR_ALLOWED_DOMAINS adds hosts, comma-separated (--set MIRROR_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=git.example.com).

docs.title: 2. Mirror a repository
docs.text:
nereus scm mirror create copies the repository at --from, pulled again every --interval. It goes through --mandate, else the reef's default Mandate; a Mandate whose Nereid serves no mirrors, such as github-scm, is refused.

nereus scm mirror create nereus \
  --from https://github.com/getnereus/nereus \
  --interval 10m
output
✓ scm/mirrors/nereus created (mandate forgejo)

Next steps:

  nereus scm mirror get nereus

A source is https://. A plain http:// host in the cluster needs both --allow-http here and the setting MIRROR_ALLOW_HTTP=true on the Nereid.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus scm mirror list shows the commit each copy holds: Syncing until the first pull, then Ready.

nereus scm mirror list
output
MIRROR   FROM                                       MANDATE  LAST SYNC             COMMIT   STATUS
nereus   https://github.com/getnereus/nereus        forgejo  2026-11-10T12:00:00Z  68d7a0d  Ready
outside  https://example.com/example/outside        forgejo  -                     -        SourceUnreachable

nereus scm mirror get adds the address the cluster clones from, and the default branch.

nereus scm mirror get nereus
output
Name:         nereus
From:         https://github.com/getnereus/nereus
Interval:     10m
Mandate:      forgejo
Nereid:       forgejo
Status:       Ready
Repository:   getnereus/nereus
Clone:        http://forgejo-http.nereus-system-forgejo.svc:3000/getnereus/nereus.git
Branch:       main
Commit:       68d7a0d6f1c2b3a4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80
Last sync:    2026-11-10T12:00:00Z
Message:      getnereus/nereus holds 68d7a0d6f1c2 of main, pulled every 10m.

Any other status names what to fix:

Status Meaning SourceUnreachable a host outside MIRROR_ALLOWED_DOMAINS, a repository that is not there, or a plain http:// source without MIRROR_ALLOW_HTTP Taken another Mirror, the oldest, holds the same <owner>/<repository>, or Forgejo holds one there copied from another source NoMandate no scm Mandate names the forgejo Nereid WaitingForForgejo Forgejo is not up yet; the message gives the reason the Mandate forgejo carries

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
nereus scm mirror delete removes the copy in Forgejo too, never the source.

nereus scm mirror delete nereus

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Connect an organisation to reach its private repositories through a GitHub App.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • The scm reef: Connections and Mirrors, every command.

docs.title: Use a secret in a namespace
docs.text: Give a namespace a Kubernetes Secret made from a secret of the installation, under the key names its app expects: a binding asks for it, and the vault says which namespaces may.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A secret google-oauth in the vault default, from Keep a secret.
  • The namespace identity, such as from kubectl create namespace identity.

docs.title: 1. Allow the namespace
docs.text:
A vault lists the namespaces that may bind its secrets in spec.allowedNamespaces. Write the vault as a file with nereus secrets vault get, add identity there, then apply the file.

nereus secrets vault get default \
  --output yaml > default.yaml

nereus secrets vault apply \
  --from-file default.yaml
output
✓ secrets/vaults/default configured

docs.title: 2. Bind the secret
docs.text:
nereus secrets binding create makes the Kubernetes Secret in the namespace from the secret's current version; each --key NAME=KEY renames a key, and without any, every key keeps its own name. A namespace the vault does not allow, or a key the secret lacks, is refused before anything is written.

nereus secrets binding create keycloak-google \
  --secret default/google-oauth \
  --namespace identity \
  --key client-id=GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID \
  --key client-secret=GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
output
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth/secretbindings/identity/keycloak-google created
Secret keycloak-google ready in namespace identity.

Next steps:

  nereus secrets binding get keycloak-google --namespace identity

A chart asks the same way, with a SecretBinding among its templates, as test/charts/binding-demo does; helm uninstall removes it and its Kubernetes Secret. A release asks with --secret.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus secrets binding list shows each binding with FOR, who asked: a release, a chart from its Helm labels, or the CLI user.

nereus secrets binding list
output
NAME             SECRET                NAMESPACE  FOR                 STATUS  AGE
keycloak-google  default/google-oauth  identity   system:admin        Ready   12s
binding-demo     default/google-oauth  tools      chart binding-demo  Ready   4s

A secret is not deleted while bindings use it: nereus secrets get lists them.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
nereus secrets binding delete deletes the Kubernetes Secret first, then the binding.

nereus secrets binding delete keycloak-google \
  --namespace identity
output
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth/secretbindings/identity/keycloak-google deleted

Next steps:

  nereus secrets binding list --namespace identity

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Release a chart that reads the secret through a binding.
  • Give a team a vault of its own with nereus secrets vault create --allow-namespace.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • The secrets reef: vaults, secrets and bindings, every command.

docs.title: Keep a secret
docs.text: Keep a secret in a vault of the installation: each value is encrypted on your machine before it leaves it, and no command prints it back.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A cluster from Prepare the cluster with --profile internal-developer-platform: it brings the secrets reef, the Nereid openbao and the vault default.
  • The values in environment variables or files, never on the command line, where the shell history keeps them.

docs.title: 1. Create a secret from environment variables
docs.text:
nereus secrets create encrypts each value with the key of the vault's Mandate, then stores it.

nereus secrets create google-oauth \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
output
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth created (key SHA256:GQ8TrJ9h6ZrNYHItBycWK+tXkURjowfJWcjEyabRIKI)
Stored encrypted; a Kubernetes Secret is made only when a binding asks for it (#532).

docs.title: 2. Take a key from a file
docs.text:
--from-file KEY=PATH takes the file's bytes, for a private key or a certificate.

nereus secrets create github-app \
  --from-file private-key=key.pem \
  --from-env APP_ID
output
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/github-app created (key SHA256:GQ8TrJ9h6ZrNYHItBycWK+tXkURjowfJWcjEyabRIKI)
Stored encrypted; a Kubernetes Secret is made only when a binding asks for it (#532).

docs.title: 3. Change it from a file
docs.text:
create refuses a secret that exists. Write the encrypted secret to a file, safe to keep, then nereus secrets apply it; each change is a new version.

nereus secrets create google-oauth \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID \
  --from-env GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET \
  --dry-run --output yaml > google-oauth.yaml
nereus secrets apply --from-file google-oauth.yaml
output
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth configured

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus secrets list shows the keys' names, never a value.

nereus secrets list
output
VAULT    NAME          KEYS                  STATUS  AGE
default  github-app    APP_ID, +1            Ready   9s
default  google-oauth  GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, +1  Ready   10s

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
Deleted for good

Deleting a secret destroys every version of it in OpenBao.

nereus secrets delete default/google-oauth
nereus secrets delete github-app
output
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/google-oauth deleted
✓ secrets/vaults/default/secrets/github-app deleted

docs.title: Join the team's room
docs.text: Put your coding agent in the team's room on Triton, where the agents of the team's people say what they claim, ask and release. There is no room to create and no invitation to send: an admin gives you access, then you join alone.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The CLI from Install the CLI and Claude Code, logged in with claude auth login. No cluster, kubeconfig or NATS.
  • Your e-mail with the admin of the installation, here alice@example.com.

docs.title: 1. The admin lets you in
docs.text:
The admin adds your e-mail to the keycloak Mandate's googleUsers: the list is the invitation. The keycloak Nereid makes your user, and on your first Google login you choose a username.

nereus mandate apply keycloak \
  --reef authentication \
  --nereid keycloak \
  --param googleTeam=alice@example.com,bob@example.com

googleTeam lists the e-mails of the team: the keycloak Nereid makes each one a user (no need to repeat it in googleUsers) and puts it in the group nereus-team; an e-mail dropped from the list leaves the group. A login outside the group reaches Triton but no tool. Nobody touches Keycloak's console.

docs.title: 2. Log in to the installation
docs.text:
nereus login opens a browser page. On a machine with no browser (a container, SSH), add --use-device-code: the terminal shows a page and a code to open on another device.

nereus login https://nereus.example.com

docs.title: 3. Work in a clone of the repository
docs.text:
Without a room named, the room is the name of the folder's git origin: a clone of nereus.git is in the room nereus. A room is a Room of the rooms reef; Triton serves only the Rooms that exist, and a refusal lists them. A team member makes another with nereus rooms create (Create a room for your team).

git clone https://github.com/getnereus/nereus.git

docs.title: 4. Start your agent in the room
docs.text:
nereus rooms join opens Claude Code in this terminal under a Nereid's name no agent holds on Triton, with the room's peer tools under your own login and a hook that reads the room's new messages at each prompt. --tmux names the tmux window after it; --name picks the agent's name.

nereus rooms join \
  --tmux
output
no name given: the agent is speo (a Nereid's name, free on Triton)
  peer: rooms/peers/alice.speo in nereus
starting speo with claude-code: in the room nereus on Triton

To join from a Claude Code session already open, its agent runs nereus rooms join from its Bash tool, with no restart; that needs nereus mcp local add once, which puts the room's tools and hooks in Claude Code's user scope.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus rooms follow shows the room yourself, without an agent: the last 10 minutes, then each new message until Ctrl-C, or with --once what the room holds.

nereus rooms follow \
  --room nereus \
  --since 15m \
  --once
output
21:02:11  alice/speo  claim    #1406 in ../nereus-1406-size, paths controllers/vcluster/
21:02:40  bob/doto    note     k3d-nereus is mine until 21:30
21:30:02  bob/doto    release  k3d-nereus

nereus rooms peer list shows your agent as a Peer under your username, and nereus rooms post says something to the room with no agent.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Follow the protocol the agents use in the room, [claim], [ask], [ok], [wait], [note] and [release], the same as between the sessions of one machine.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• The rooms reef: rooms, peers, room sessions and the conversation, every command.
  • Triton: the room, the peer messages and their limits.

docs.title: Follow your agent's quota
docs.text: Report the share of a coding agent's quota window you read, and see where it is heading: the forecast at the reset, its pace, today's goal and the week day by day.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A cluster from Prepare the cluster with --profile internal-developer-platform: it brings the usage reef with its Nereid reference-usage.
  • nereus login done: the readings go through the Nereus API.
  • The share used and the reset of the window, as your agent's status line shows them.

docs.title: 1. Report a reading
docs.text:
nereus usage report sends the share, read now. Within one window the higher share is kept: an idle session that reports an older, lower share changes nothing.

nereus usage report weekly \
  --used 75 \
  --resets-at 2026-11-16T01:00:00-03:00
output
✓ usage/windows/weekly reported (75% used, resets Mon 16/11 01:00)

Next steps:

  nereus usage get weekly

docs.title: 2. Read where it is heading
docs.text:
nereus usage get shows the forecast at the reset and its pace (push below 70%, steady up to 95%, slow above), today's goal, and the week: the days gone (~ when estimated), today and the plan for the days left.

nereus usage get weekly
output
WINDOW  USED  RESETS           FORECAST  PACE    TODAY  READ
weekly  75%   Mon 16/11 01:00  91%       steady  ≤75%   Sat 19:06

DAY        SHARE  TOTAL
Mon 09/11  +10%   10%
Tue 10/11  ~+11%  ~21%
Wed 11/11  +10%   31%
Thu 12/11  +10%   41%
Fri 13/11  +19%   60%
Sat 14/11  +15%   75%    today
Sun 15/11  +25%   100%   plan

docs.title: 3. Cut the days where you live
docs.text:
The days and the times are cut in the time zone of the reef's Mandate, UTC until you set one. nereus mandate apply replaces every param, so name them all.

nereus mandate apply reference-usage \
  --reef usage \
  --nereid reference-usage \
  --default \
  --param timeZone=America/Sao_Paulo

docs.title: 4. Report a reset
docs.text:
When the quota was reset and the share really went down, say so with --replace: the lower share wins, and the days gone stay. For an hour, a reading above it but not above the old peak is taken for a stale session's and ignored.

nereus usage report weekly \
  --used 91 \
  --resets-at 2026-11-16T01:00:00-03:00 \
  --replace
output
✓ usage/windows/weekly replaced 98% (91% used, resets Mon 16/11 01:00), forecast 110.7% slow

Next steps:

  nereus usage get weekly

docs.title: 5. Report from the status line
docs.text:
report keeps a local cache, one JSON file per window under ~/.local/state/nereus/usage/, and sends at most every 5 minutes, so a status line can run it on every reading and read the figures back with jq. Offline, the cache keeps the reading and get answers from it, marked local.

jq '.figures.forecast' ~/.local/state/nereus/usage/weekly.json

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus usage get weekly shows the share you reported, its forecast, and today never below zero after a reset.

nereus usage get weekly
output
WINDOW  USED  RESETS           FORECAST  PACE  TODAY  READ
weekly  91%   Mon 16/11 01:00  111%      slow  ≤92%   Sat 19:06

DAY        SHARE  TOTAL
Mon 09/11  ~+18%  ~18%
Tue 10/11  ~+18%  ~36%
Wed 11/11  ~+19%  ~55%
Thu 12/11  ~+18%  ~73%
Fri 13/11  +18%   91%
Sat 14/11  +0%    91%    today
Sun 15/11  +8%    100%   plan

docs.text: • The usage reef's commands, with apply, list and delete.

docs.title: ✗ plan: the Nereid refused the Instance: IssuerNotPublic
docs.text: nereus nereid apply azure stops at the plan, before any cloud request.

docs.title: You see
docs.text:
output
✓ image            0.0s  cloud-azure-controller:0.1.0 implements cloud, login az
✓ login            0.0s  az, account 00000000-…, organization from the login
✗ plan             0.0s  the Nereid refused the Instance: IssuerNotPublic
  what     the undercloud of installation tailwind presents Kubernetes' default issuer https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local, which Azure cannot reach
  cause    probably created by nereus init without --target azure (k3d is the default): the issuer is set when the cluster is created and never changes after
  check    kubectl get --raw /.well-known/openid-configuration
  fix      nereus init --target azure --installation-name tailwind
  Nothing ran in the cloud.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: The cluster presents Kubernetes' default issuer, which Azure cannot reach. The issuer is set when the cluster is created and never changes after.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Create the undercloud with a public issuer, as in Prepare the undercloud:

nereus init --target azure --installation-name tailwind

docs.title: Check
docs.text: kubectl get --raw /.well-known/openid-configuration shows an issuer under blob.core.windows.net, and the next nereus nereid apply azure prints its plan.

docs.title: ✗ names: storage account is taken in Azure
docs.text: nereus init --target azure stops at the names plan, before it creates anything in Azure.

docs.title: You see
docs.text:
output
✗ names                         0.1s  storage account issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e is taken in Azure
  total                         0.2s  slo 20m, 0% green
  Record it for issuer.storage, then prepare the undercloud again with it:
    nereus config installation set --naming-override issuer.storage=issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e2
    nereus init --target azure

docs.title: Why
docs.text: A storage account name is unique across Azure, and the issuer's is issuers<id16>. The likely owner is a deleted installation with the same id.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Record the suggested name with nereus config installation set, then prepare the undercloud again:

nereus config installation set \
  --naming-override issuer.storage=issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e2
nereus init --target azure

In a terminal without --yes, init asks instead, and a yes does the same:

output
? Use issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e2 for issuer.storage? (Y/n) y
✓ installation tailwind  naming.overrides.issuer.storage = issuers0b7e4c1a93d24f6e2

docs.title: Check
docs.text: The next init recreates the cluster with the new issuer and runs to the end: every line starts with ✓.

docs.title: ✗ nereid reference-release is Unavailable
docs.text: A command of a reef stops at once, sends nothing and exits non-zero, because its Nereid has no pod serving.

docs.title: You see
docs.text:
nereus release repo list
output
✗ nereid reference-release is Unavailable: its Controller has no pod serving.
  Its commands work again by themselves once the Controller is back: see 'nereus nereid list'.

nereus nereid list shows the Nereid's STATUS as Unavailable, computed by the CLI from its Deployment.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: The Nereid's Deployment has no ready pod: scaled to zero, or its pod crashing. A deleted pod is replaced by the Deployment, and the new one starts with an empty work directory.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text: Bring the Deployment back, here scaled up from zero: kubectl scale deployment reference-release --namespace nereus-system --replicas 1. For a crashing pod, read why first in See what happened.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
The same command works again by itself, with no retry flag:

nereus release repo add chaos-scaled https://charts.example.com
output
"chaos-scaled" has been added to your repositories

test/scene kills the pod and scales the Deployment to zero and back, then checks these lines.

docs.title: ✗ create managed identity refused: AuthorizationFailed
docs.text: An approved plan of nereus nereid apply azure stops at the first request the cloud refuses.

docs.title: You see
docs.text:
output
✓ 1  create  resource group        tailwind-platform              0s
✗ 2  create  managed identity      tailwind-cloud-provisioner     0s
  3  create  federated credential  tailwind-undercloud-azure
  tagged with the installation and who asked
  --show-requests for the why, URLs and tags

✗ create managed identity tailwind-cloud-provisioner refused: AuthorizationFailed: The client cannot create managed identities in tailwind-platform.
  ran: create resource group tailwind-platform
  not run: create managed identity tailwind-cloud-provisioner, create federated credential tailwind-undercloud-azure
An administrator can create the identity, and give you Managed Identity Contributor on it:
  az identity create --resource-group tailwind-platform --name tailwind-cloud-provisioner
  az role assignment create --assignee <your-object-id> --role "Managed Identity Contributor" --scope <identity-id>
Then run:
  nereus nereid apply azure --reef cloud --param identity=<client-id>
  log: ~/.local/state/nereus/logs/20261019T221500Z-install.log

docs.title: Why
docs.text: Your login lacks the right to create that resource (403). The later requests did not run.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Ask an administrator to run the two az lines printed, then name the identity they created:

nereus nereid apply azure --reef cloud --param identity=<client-id>

docs.title: Check
docs.text: The run ends with ✓ azure exchanged its token as tailwind-cloud-provisioner. The log named in the output holds each request and its answer's status.

docs.title: See what happened
docs.text: Find why a reef, a Nereid or an object is not Ready, starting from the CLI and going down to the object's events and the Nereid's log.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • A cluster from Prepare the cluster, and kubectl for the last two steps.

docs.title: 1. See which reef has a problem
docs.text:
nereus status gives one row per reef and its Nereid:

nereus status
output
REEF            NEREID      VERSION  STATUS  AGE
authentication  keycloak    0.1.0    Ready   2m
core            nereus-api  0.1.0    Ready   4m
                thetis      0.1.0    Ready   4m
release         flux        0.1.0    Ready   3m
secrets         openbao     0.1.0    Ready   4m
tenancy         -           -        Ready   4m

Registry  localhost:5111

docs.title: 2. Look at the Nereid
docs.text:
nereus nereid get shows its image, digest and Mandates; a Nereid that is not Ready also says why (Unavailable, NotConformant).

nereus nereid get keycloak
output
Name:         keycloak
Reefs:        authentication
Image:        localhost:5111/keycloak-controller:0.1.0
Digest:       sha256:0f4675ab231b4e6d4a439d0c7d8e5b07011f35802b38592851542cf56666be93
Title:        authentication-keycloak-controller
Description:  The keycloak Nereid of Nereus, for the authentication reef
Status:       Ready
Mandates:     keycloak (default)
Age:          2m

docs.title: 3. Read the object's events
docs.text: Each object's Ready condition says why in its message, and every change of a step is a Kubernetes Event on the object, kept when the Nereid restarts: kubectl describe shows them, under Events.

docs.title: 4. Read the Nereid's log
docs.text: A Nereid logs JSON Lines, one per reconcile pass and its reason: kubectl logs deployment/keycloak --namespace nereus-system.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
nereus doctor runs ten checks of the installation, pass or fail, and says the next step for one that fails:

nereus doctor

docs.title: Next
docs.text:

  • Pass the conformance tests: the status every object must carry.

docs.text: • Spec 0003: the Ready condition, the steps and their events.

docs.title: Deck
docs.text:
The project as presentations, each rendered from one outline by render-outline, in the reference style of the How I use AI deck (how-i-use-ia.yaml, #461): one slide at a time, phone first, bilingual (English and Portuguese), light and dark themes; big titles with one amber accent, spaced uppercase labels, plain lists revealed in turn with the previous item dimmed, the source at the bottom, and the references in a deck of their own. The rules for whoever writes a deck are in docs/agent/decks.md.

  • nereus.yaml: the idea, the model (reef, Nereid, Mandate), the first slice and where it is heading.
  • storytelling.yaml: the talk before the platform, the same problems for fifty years and the question for the AI era (#190). Every fact on screen has a source, and its notes end with Source: references/<topic>.md, one file per topic under references/, which the renderer turns into a link.
  • how-we-work.yaml: how the work happens in this repository, for people who build software with AI: what already existed and what the agent changes (#882).
  • release.yaml: the release reef step by step: its four kinds, the nine commands that run a Helm chart through the flux Nereid, the HelmRelease it writes underneath, and swapping the tool (make deck OUTLINE=release).
  • implementation-comparator.yaml: two Nereids of the same reef measured side by side by performance, satisfaction and cost, and the comparator Nereid that turns the comparison into a decision (Keycloak and Auth0 in the authentication reef); its code frames and diagrams, one per language where they differ, are in implementation-comparator/ (#1457).
  • more-than-an-idp.yaml: the pitch, Nereus as more than an IDP in fourteen slides: an IDP is one profile of a composable platform API, swapping the tool changes no command, the comparator as the example, agents as clients and peers, and how the work happens; it ends asking for a pilot of the comparator (#1487).
  • how-i-use-ia.yaml: how I use AI, one real night told in eight acts and an appendix: the reference style of the decks (#461), first built by hand and rendered from its outline since #1458; its diagrams and the files it shows, one per language, are in how-i-use-ia/.
  • idp/: the Internal Developer Platform series, ported from the first proof of concept (wasp-idp, #538), one deck per part (make deck OUTLINE=idp/problem); its sources are in idp/references/.

One page is built by hand, not rendered from an outline: doris-demo.html, the replay of a thread of notes, a page that browses data (docs/agent/decks.md), until the ideas reef's portal (#1108) takes it.

docs.title: See it
docs.text:
make deck

It renders nereus.html and opens it; make deck OUTLINE=storytelling renders and opens the talk. F11 for full screen.

Key Action ↓ Enter Space PgDn Next step: the next item, else the next terminal step, else the next diagram part, else the next slide ↑ Back one step: hides the last item shown, else restarts the slide; at the start of a slide, the previous slide ← PgUp / → Previous / next slide, skipping the steps Home The first slide of the deck D The reference deck, and back I The slide index, and closes it; in it, ↑ ↓ walk the entries and Enter goes to one N / L / R / C Notes / language / restart the slide / every item at full colour + / - Larger / smaller text, terminals included O Hosted by the Sessions tab, in full screen: the room's turn on offer, the slide's question or the rating (#1882) Esc Close the QR code, else the index, else the notes

The top bar has the deck's name, the theme (it follows the system until tapped, then swaps light and dark), the language (EN | PT, the chosen one highlighted) and the counter (R before it in the reference deck); a tap on the counter opens the slide index (#1450): one entry per slide of the deck on screen (its number, label and message, in the language on screen) under its act's title, the current one marked and in view; a tap on an entry goes to that slide, at its start, and a second tap on the counter, the close button or a click outside closes it. The bar at the bottom has home, previous, A−, A+, the notes, References (Back to the deck from there) and next. On a phone, a round navigation pad sits above it (▲ back one step, ▼ next step, ◀ ▶ slides, ↺ restart, ☀ every item at full colour), dims when idle and moves when dragged by its edge; a swipe to the left is the next step, to the right the previous slide. The notes open in a panel with their own A− and A+, and a click outside closes them; a QR code opens in an overlay with its link, and a click outside closes it. The deck remembers the slide, the language and the theme in the browser. A link to one slide: nereus.html#<name>, the name of the slide in the outline (#ref-<name> for a reference).

docs.title: Change it
docs.text:
1. Edit the outline, in both languages. One message per slide; what is said goes in notes, not on the screen.
  2. Show the repository's own files, never copies: code points to a file in the repository and diagram to an SVG with <g data-part="..."> groups (../assets/docs/landscape.svg).
  3. Render it again and look at it at phone and desktop width: make deck (with OUTLINE=storytelling for the talk). The .html is generated and versioned: it goes in the same commit as the outline, and is never edited by hand.
  4. make deck-test runs the renderer's tests, including the validation of both outlines and a fresh render compared with the committed decks.

docs.title: The portal mode
docs.text:
A committed deck is one self-contained HTML file, the offline export. The portal serves its pages under default-src 'self', which refuses an inline <style> and <script>, so render-outline --split writes the same deck as an HTML that links deck.css and deck.js, written next to it from the same CSS and SCRIPT (#1693). Nothing else differs: no style attribute, event-handler attribute or eval is left in either mode, and the script styles only through the CSSOM, which the policy allows.

uv run --with pyyaml --with segno python render-outline storytelling.yaml --output /tmp/deck/storytelling.html --split

make deck-test checks it in headless Chromium: two decks in the portal mode, served under the portal's own csp() (controllers/nereus-portal/portal.py) and walked through every slide and step, raise no CSP violation. The test uses Playwright's Chromium when it was downloaded, else the Chrome of the host.

docs.title: Steps and followers
docs.text:
A step is what one press reveals, counted with no animation (#1760): a slide at its start, then each item (.st, the cover's subtitle included), a terminal command's two presses (typed, then run), each further line of a stepwise output, and each part of a diagram's reveal. The renderer writes each slide's count as data-units, and render-outline <deck> --steps prints the deck's total; tests/test_steps.py walks every deck with the animations off and checks that each press is exactly one step.

The engine reports every move as a nereus-step event ({step, steps}) and goes to a step on nereus-goto ({step}): the next step animates as a press does, any other is reached at once. html[data-mode="follow"] is the follower's mode (the portal's /p/<code>, which loads the portal's copy of deck.css and deck.js): the controls that change the step are hidden and ignored, and A−/A+, the theme, the language and the animations (the M key or the pill, kept per device) stay. After a change of the engine, copy deck.css and deck.js from a --split render into controllers/nereus-portal/static/; make deck-test fails while they differ.

html[data-mode="drive"] is the speaker's mode (#1761): the presentations reef's Sessions tab frames the portal's /present.html, which gets the Session's page with the notes from the tab by postMessage and holds no token. Every control stays; the page that hosts the deck sets the first step, so the engine neither starts from nor writes the address's hash or the browser's remembered slide. Each nereus-step goes back to the tab, which posts it as the Session's step, and a nereus-clock event ({text, over}) puts the talk's time in the top bar. In full screen, while the room's pace thermometer is on, a nereus-pace event ({show, slow, fast, text, label}, #1922) puts its counts after the clock in the bottom bar, as the host writes them (▲ 1 ▼ 2: up too fast, down too slow), its sentence as the label.

docs.title: The outline
docs.text:
Its JSON Schema (#1700): one per outlineVersion, cli/src/nereus/schemas/presentations/outline/<version>.json. Version 1 is every field below but poll; version 2 is version 1 with a slide's poll (#1722), and a deck at 1 with a poll is refused with a message to raise outlineVersion to 2. A deck names its schema with $schema (a URL or a path, for an editor) and may name its version with outlineVersion (1 when absent); every deck of the repository validates against it (tests/test_outline_schema.py). nereus presentations schema get [<version>] prints it with no instance, the latest when no version is given, and the Nereus API serves it with no token on GET /v1/presentations/schemas/outline/<version>.json. What a schema cannot say (a pt for every text, links, files, fitting the screen) is the renderer's validation here and the Nereid's dry run (#1702).

At the top, deck (name, title, subtitle, and an optional accent: the words of the subtitle in amber on the cover), acts (name, title, an optional question that opens the act on its own slide unless opening: false) and references. Every text has its Portuguese version in a pt: block next to it, with the same field names; the validation refuses a missing one and an unknown field.

Slide field Required Meaning name yes Stable slug of the slide, used by dependsOn and in links act yes The act, from the acts list topic no Shown after the act in the label: "Act · topic" message yes The one idea of the slide, one sentence with no full stop, shown as the big title accent no The word or words of the message in amber, at most one per slide; with its pt.accent. It must be in the message and must not cut through other markup; a cover takes deck.accent instead heading or subtitle no The line under the message, revealed after it as its own step (at once with animations: none) cover no true: the deck's title at once, then its subtitle, in place of the message screen no Items of a plain list, revealed one at a time with the previous one dimmed (animations: none shows them at once); **Label:** text; a list that does not fit continues on the next slide; an item that starts with - is a sub-item of the one before, revealed on its own terminal no {cwd?, steps: [{comment?, run, options?, output?, stepwise?}]}: run is the command with no options, options the long options, one per line, output what it prints, streamed by itself, or with stepwise: true one line per step, a blank line going with the line after it (#1456): a line that starts with ✓ or ✗, or Next steps:, takes its colour whole; in any other, ✓ is green, ✗ red, a lone ~ amber, {nereid:auth0} (any concept) takes its colour and {dim:...} the comment grey, the only place {dim:...} is allowed (#1455) code no {file, lines?, focus?}: an editor frame on a repository file; focus dims the other lines diagram no An SVG with parts. show: parts at full colour; dim: parts faded; reveal: one new part per step, earlier ones dimmed unless accumulate: true. Its viewBox gives its height on a phone, so the items that fit beside it stay on its slide (#1458) pt.terminal, pt.code, pt.diagram no The Portuguese version of a frame whose text changes with the language, with the same parts; without it, both languages share the frame (#1457) details no Per part of the diagram, {title, tip, body}, also under pt: the tip shows under the mouse, a click, a tap or Enter opens the title and body in an overlay source no A "Source: ..." line at the bottom of the slide refs no The names of the slide's sources in references: links to their slides in the notes notes yes What the presenter says, not on the screen; the first sentence of each paragraph in bold dependsOn no Slides that must come before (the chain of the argument) status no A command's state in the CLI's specs (docs/specs/cli, #477): built, planned or idea, a tag after the label issue with planned The issue that builds the command, shown in the tag (planned #475) poll no, outlineVersion: 2 A question to the room (#1722), opened and closed by the speaker from the drive screen (#1917), named by the slide's name: {kind, question, choices?, scale?, seconds?, pt: {question, choices?}}. kind is choice (2 to 6 choices, lettered A to F, with as many pt.choices), scale (scale: {min, max}, integers from 0 to 10, min below max) or text (a few words from each phone, never shown on the projector); seconds is a reference time to answer, 5 to 300, 30 when absent: it closes nothing, the speaker closes the poll (and may reopen it, the answers in stay), and past it the drive screen counts the time over (+0:12) while the phones and the projector only say it is open. The slide shows the question and its options at once, no steps, with no screen, frame or cover; the message is optional, and with none the question is the slide's title. The poll's <div class='poll'> carries data-poll (the name), data-kind, data-seconds and data-choices or data-min and data-max, and an empty [data-poll-live] place (data-poll-clock, data-poll-count) and per option a data-poll-bar and data-poll-votes that a live session's screens fill. nereus presentations create --dry-run names the polls: 2 polls (level: scale 1-5, 30s; next: choice, 3 choices, 20s)

Inline markup on a slide: **bold**, _emphasis_ (italic, in amber in a title), `code`, [text](href) (a link; one to another deck's slide, ../specs/cli/reefs/edge.html#zone-create, must reach a slide of that deck, #477) and {reef:environment}, {nereid:vcluster}, {mandate:vcluster}, {secret:...} in the concept's colour; the roles of the work take theirs the same way: {order:...}, {pr:...}, {agent:...}, {raw:...}, {human:...}, {handoff:...} (#1458), and an SVG uses them as var(--cx-order) and so on.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
references holds one entry per source, and they make a deck of their own, opened with the References button or D: a slide lists them, each with its QR code, and each one gets its own slide with the source, About:, For this talk: and its link next to its QR code (generated at render time with segno, inline, no network). A tap on a QR code opens it large in an overlay, with its link. The notes of a slide link to its refs, each with its QR code.

Field Required Meaning name yes Stable slug, used by refs title yes The source's title url yes http(s): what the QR code opens author, year no Shown under the title about no The source in two or three sentences forUs no What matters in it for the talk, with the exact quote when there is one

The validation refuses an unknown refs entry, a reference with no title or a non-http(s) URL, a name defined twice, and a reference no slide cites.
