docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: The project's words and acronyms, one line each. A new term enters in the pull request that introduces it; a borrowed term links its source (#332).

docs.title: The project
docs.text: Term Meaning Nereus The project: a composable API platform, with an API and a CLI: reefs add the APIs, Nereids look after them, installed at runtime. An Internal Developer Platform is one profile of it. Organisation getnereus, domains getnereus.dev (development) and getnereus.app (production). After Nereus, the old man of the sea. Nereus API nereus-api, the platform's own HTTP API in the cluster (api/, #607): GET /v1/me answers who a token names, after checking it against the default authentication Mandate; GET /v1/status, what nereus status --output json prints (#739).

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
Words of ADR 0002 (Conceptual model) and ADR 0011 (reefs, Nereids and Mandates; nereus reef, nereus nereid, nereus mandate), used exactly.

Term Meaning reef A capability of the platform (auth, secrets, release), an API group. Added with nereus reef apply; a Reef object of core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1; its own kinds live in <reef>.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (ADR 0009). Legacy: Interface. Nereid What looks after a reef (keycloak, auth0, reference-release): a controller installed in the platform with nereus nereid apply; a Nereid object of core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1. Legacy: Implementation. Mandate Binds one reef to one Nereid and may make it the default; nereus mandate create, after Gateway API's GatewayClass. A Mandate object of core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (azure binds the cloud reef to the azure Nereid). Legacy: Class. Profile A named list of reefs, Nereids and Mandates applied on top of core (core, internal-developer-platform, reference, secrets); nereus init --profile, nereus profile apply (ADR 0014). thetis The installer Nereid: run by the chart nereus when a profile is set, it installs the profile's reefs, Nereids and Mandates in order. Instance One occurrence of a reef: a login for a team, a database for an app in an environment. Repository (release reef) Where a chart comes from: a Helm repository (http), an OCI registry (oci) or Git (git), with an optional secret of the secrets reef; a kind of release.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (ADR 0010). flux writes it as a Flux HelmRepository. Source (release reef) What is released: a chart of a Repository at a version (later Kustomize or plain manifests); a kind of release.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (ADR 0010). Target (release reef) Where a release goes: a namespace of an environment (environmentRef) or, with none, of the cluster Nereus runs in; a kind of release.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (ADR 0010). Connection (scm reef) One organisation of a source host, reached through the App its scm Mandate names (--param identity=<authentication mandate>); its status says whether the App is installed there, on every repository, with the permissions it needs (ADR 0024, #1281). nereus scm connection create. Registry (registry reef) A registry of images that runs in the cluster, a kind of registry.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (ADR 0021). Not the Nereid registry (#22), the public site listing Nereids. Release (release reef) A Source running in a Target, with its values, made by the Nereid of its Mandate; a kind of release.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1 (ADR 0010). flux writes it as a Flux HelmRelease. nereus release <verb> is nereus release release <verb>: a kind named after its reef takes the reef's verbs. Controller The mechanism: each Nereid runs as a Kubernetes controller that reconciles and writes status. Used in ADRs, code and repository names, not in commands. Tool What a Nereid works with: the helm binary, the Auth0 Management API. Vendor An attribute: whose thing it is (Auth0, AWS, local). Concept Former word for reef (then Interface), before ADR 0011. Default Mandate The one a reef's commands go to when several Nereids look after it (#72); formerly the active Implementation. Good Citizen The rules every Nereid must follow, checked by the platform (spec 0003). Conformance Whether a Nereid honours its reef's contract: labels at add, the contract call at start, a suite before the catalog (spec 0003).

docs.title: The platform
docs.text: Term Meaning nereus The CLI binary (formerly nereus). Control Plane The owner's name for the Nereus API as Nereids see it: what they talk to through events, subscribing to and sending to topics set when their Nereid is added (#254). Triton The switchboard operator of the agents (controllers/triton): lists who is connected, keeps the rooms where a team's agents talk as peers (a JetStream stream per room, #1417), and carries the owner's orders to an agent. After Triton, herald of the sea. Nereus API The one door every client goes through (CLI, portal, agent), installed by the chart nereus (ADR 0018, the Nereus API as the one door). Formerly Platform API. Progress lines What nereus init prints of its steps: one line each, with a mark, detail and time; drawn live on a terminal, the running one spinning (#88, #379). A cloud target sums them in three lines at the end, and its plan turns each numbered line into a ✓ and its time as it runs. Scene The end-to-end script of the current slice (test/scene), run on a throwaway k3d cluster, locally and in CI. Platform orchestrator The centrepiece of an IDP in internaldeveloperplatform.org's words: published contracts between developers and platform teams; compared in Platform orchestrators. Promise Kratix's contract: an API (a CRD) and the workflows that fulfil it, in one object. Recipe Pack Radius's implementation of its Resource Types, one Bicep or Terraform recipe per type, chosen by the Environment. Score A workload specification (score.yaml), a candidate for the app declaration the Nereus API composes. Session A live collaboration: people join with a code, contribute together, and every screen updates live (#217, #223). Slice A thin end-to-end piece that ends with something a person can run from the CLI; one spec each (docs/specs/). Undercloud, overcloud The local k3d cluster that seeds the platform, <installation>-undercloud (tailwind-undercloud) when nereus init --target <name> bootstraps a cloud (nereus otherwise), and the cloud cluster it moves into, AKS (#61, #263, spec 0005). Cluster role undercloud or overcloud: the label core.getnereus.dev/cluster-role of the nereus namespace, written by init and kept apart from the installation's identity so the pivot never carries it (#263). Pivot The move of the platform from the undercloud to the overcloud, as in Cluster API's clusterctl move (#61). Inception The platform building, running, measuring and telling its own construction (#24): its services run on itself, its metrics and agent records come through its own tools (#137), and it learns from how its owner suggests (#138). A lens: how could each practice become a native capability. Lean Inception The workshop (Paulo Caroli's method) that shaped the MVP (#79, docs/inception.md). One writer per field ADR 0005: the API (or the CLI) writes spec, the Nereid writes status, after Kubernetes' spec and status. Pinned version The version of a reef's kinds a CLI ships and nereus reef apply applies (cloud 0.1.0, in cli/src/nereus/interfaces/); apply --path or --image apply another (#264). Reef package An OCI artifact whose layers are a reef's CRDs as YAML (application/yaml), which nereus reef apply --image reads (#264). Pinned by digest An image recorded as <repository>@sha256:..., the digest of the manifest its labels were read from, not a tag that can be pushed again (#126, spec 0003 rule 3). cloud reef The connection to a cloud: an account, optionally the organization above it, and the identity the platform presents; azure is its first Nereid (spec 0005). Workload identity A pod trades the token its cluster signs for its service account at the cloud for a token of an identity, then calls the cloud as that identity; the platform projects that token into every Nereid that requires cloud (spec 0005, #310). Workload identity federation A cloud trusts tokens a cluster signs for one service account and trades them for its own, so the platform keeps no secret (spec 0005; Microsoft Entra). Discovery document /.well-known/openid-configuration: names the issuer and where its JWKS is. Bootstrap plan The plan the cloud Nereid makes when the undercloud's issuer is not published: the resource group, issuer storage and container, the person's grant on it, the issuer documents, then the first identity (spec 0005, #263). Names plan The read-only plan the cloud Nereid publishes before the bootstrap plan, checking every name at once; init runs it with no question, and a 404 is an answer, not a failure (spec 0005, #263). Service principal What roles are granted to in Entra ID; a managed identity has one, as an app registration does. App registration An application's definition in Entra ID; spec 0005 needs none for now. Access entry What a reef needs from the cloud, its identity and optionally a role on a scope, kept in the Cloud Instance's spec.access once a person approves it (spec 0005). Location Where an installation's resources are created, in the cloud's words (northeurope, eu-west-1): the Cloud Instance's spec.location, from --param location=<region> or the Tool's default (az config set defaults.location=<region>) (#319). Requester tags The tags every cloud resource the platform creates carries: installation, who asked, request id, Instance and the purpose the contract fixes; for attribution, never authorisation (spec 0005, #155). Installation One running platform, named once (tailwind): the name never changes, names its Installation object and is part of every name the platform creates; an id (random UUID v4) never changes either; an alias that listings show may. Undercloud and overcloud are one installation across the pivot (#154, #251). Installation alias What listings show of an installation, free text (Tailwind Prod) changed by nereus config installation set --alias; no resource name changes (spec 0006). Invitation A link and QR code that let one person into a Nereus, a kind of the authentication reef (nereus authentication invitation create, alias nereus invitation create); the link and the access expire separately (--invitation-expires, --access-expires), and accepting creates a core User (spec 0007). Naming override A name a person gives instead of a generated one that is taken (issuer.storage, state.storage, secrets.vault), kept in spec.naming.overrides of the installation and validated against the resource's rules (spec 0005, spec 0006). Plan The cloud requests a cloud Nereid publishes in its Instance's status.plans[] for the CLI to run with the person's login, each a method, an https URL and a JSON body, shown and approved first; untrusted input, checked against the request protocol's limits (cli/src/nereus/plans.py, spec 0005). Stalled The condition a Nereid sets True when it refuses an Instance as it is and plans nothing until its spec changes, with a reason, a message, the observedGeneration and, when known, the refusal's cause, check and fix (ADR 0012); nereus nereid apply stops on it and prints why, one line per field, after Kubernetes' kstatus (spec 0005, #318, #327). Request id r- and a lowercase ULID (r-01jaqb…), sortable by time: the CLI writes one for each access entry and on every object it writes (<API_GROUP>/request); the entry's plan carries it and spec.approved records it once the plan ran; listings show its first 6 characters after r- (spec 0005, #307). Naming function The one place that turns the naming table of spec 0005, the installation's name and id, and its overrides into full names (tailwind-platform, tailwind-cloud-provisioner, tailwind-undercloud-azure, issuers<id16>); automation receives the full name, never composes one (cli/src/nereus/naming.py, #307). Cloud resource identification The attributes every cloud resource the platform creates carries: installation id and name, requester id and name, request id; names only when a compliance policy allows (#155). Request protocol How a Nereid reaches a cloud before it has an identity: it publishes a plan, and once approved the CLI runs it on the person's machine with their own short-lived login, from a Tool entry fixed in the CLI (az first); the token never leaves the machine. Limits: https, the Tool's hosts (issuer storage only for the issuer's documents), no header but Content-Type, bodies up to 64 KiB, at most 50 requests, substitutions only from an earlier answer into a string value (#82, #264, spec 0005). Managed identity (user-assigned) An Azure identity created as a resource, with no secret to keep; one per reef and per installation, <installation>-<reef>-<role> (tailwind-secrets-reader), the same across the pivot (#82, spec 0005). Federated credential A trust on a cloud identity: tokens from one OIDC issuer, for one subject (a Kubernetes service account) and audience, are exchanged for the identity's access, with no secret stored (#82, #93). OIDC issuer The URL whose discovery document and JWKS let a cloud verify a cluster's service-account tokens; a k3d undercloud publishes its own on a public storage container, AKS has one built in (#82).

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
Words of ADR 0027 (teams, roles and Users).

Term Meaning User A person, one core User whatever the login; a login with no User has no permission. Team A group of people who work together; a Team of the teams reef. Joining it grants its access, leaving removes it. Member One person in a Team, pointing to their User; a Member of the teams reef. Position A free, lowercase name on a Member (tech-lead); a Binding that names it follows whoever holds it. Role A list of rules, <reef>:<kinds>:<verbs>; a Role of the authorization reef. Binding Gives a Role to a Team, a Position or, as the exception, one User, on one node of the tenancy tree; access flows down the tree.

docs.title: Ways of working
docs.text: Term Meaning Board, queue Project v2 #1 of getnereus: its order is the plan; scripts/board/queue reads and changes it. Claim queue claim <issue>: assigns the issue and sets In Progress in one step. Handoff comment The last step, the next step and the open decision, left on the issue before stopping. Walking skeleton Ship a thin end-to-end slice first, then widen it (Alistair Cockburn). Osmotic communication Everyone works in one room and overhears the others, so information flows unsent; Triton's room on NATS does the same for agents. Alistair Cockburn's term in Crystal Clear (the book). Dogfooding Eat your own dog food: the project builds itself with the platform, first user of each capability (vision.md). Conventional Commits The commit message format every commit follows: <type>(<scope>)!: <description> (conventionalcommits.org), checked by Commitizen through scripts/check-commit-message. Commitizen, cz The tool that checks the commit format and computes the version from the commits (cz.yaml, which reads the version from the tags v<x.y.z>, #186; bumps and releases in #55). Copier The open-source project template tool (copier.readthedocs.io, MIT) behind templates/nereid: scripts/nereid/new renders a new Nereid with it, and copier update brings a later change of the template as a diff (#752). Cycle time From claimed to closed (The Kanban Guide). Lead time From created to closed. Work item age How long an In Progress issue has been open (The Kanban Guide). #NoEstimates No sizing: forecasts from what was delivered (#95). Fitness function An automated check that a quality of the architecture holds, from Building Evolutionary Architectures (Ford, Parsons, Kua) (#50): init --check-slo in the scene fails CI when init misses its SLO by more than the tolerance (#141); the swap step fails it when swapping a Nereid changes a command (#124). Installation One platform with its own identity: a name and an id that never change and an alias that may, in the Installation object the first nereus init creates; undercloud and overcloud are one installation (spec 0006). SLO (service level objective) A target a quality must meet (Google SRE book); the first is the time nereus init may take: 8 minutes on k3d, 20 on a cloud, in the ServiceLevelObjective object with defaults in code (spec 0004, provisional). Band The colour of init's clock by the share of its time objective used: green, yellow from 50%, orange from 75%, red past 100% (spec 0004). Tolerance The share over the time objective (10%) past which the fitness function fails (spec 0004). proposed-by-agent Label of an issue an agent proposed, kept as its origin; waits for the owner's triage. triage/accepted The owner accepted a proposal (after Kubernetes' triage labels); a dropped one closes as not planned. When to do it is the board's order. Illusion of certainty An AI answer taken as settled when it is a guess; the AI should help teams learn faster, not create this illusion (Paulo Caroli, Times importam mais do que nunca, agent/ai-and-teams.md). Illusion of efficacy Speed and output without direction, mistaken for progress (Paulo Caroli, Times importam mais do que nunca, agent/ai-and-teams.md). First reasonable idea The trap of settling on the first idea that looks good enough; before a recommendation, the agent asks for alternatives, assumptions, unintended consequences, ignored signals and how it would fail (Paulo Caroli, Times importam mais do que nunca, agent/ai-and-teams.md). Learn faster together The edge of a team that uses AI: not more output, but faster shared learning (Paulo Caroli, Times importam mais do que nunca, agent/ai-and-teams.md).

docs.title: Acronyms
docs.text: Acronym Meaning ACR, ECR, GHCR Azure Container Registry, Amazon Elastic Container Registry, GitHub Container Registry. ADR Architecture Decision Record (docs/adr/, Nygard format). ARM Azure Resource Manager: the API every Azure resource and role assignment goes through. AKS Azure Kubernetes Service. C901 The cyclomatic-complexity rule of ruff (McCabe); the limit here is 10 per function. CEL Common Expression Language: the validation rules inside a CRD (self == oldSelf). CI Continuous integration: .github/workflows/ci.yaml on every pull request. CLI Command-line interface. CRD CustomResourceDefinition: a kind added to the Kubernetes API (cli/src/nereus/crds/). DCO Developer Certificate of Origin: a sign-off on each commit (#19). DORA DevOps Research and Assessment (dora.dev): its delivery metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore). IAM Identity and Access Management: who may do what in AWS and GCP. IDP Internal Developer Platform. JWKS JSON Web Key Set: the public keys an OIDC issuer publishes, so a token it signed can be verified. k3d, k3s k3s, a small Kubernetes distribution, run in Docker by k3d; the local cluster. MVP Minimum viable product: the waves in What it offers. OCI Open Container Initiative: the image format and the Distribution API the CLI reads labels through. OAM Open Application Model: the application model KubeVela is built on. OIDC OpenID Connect (ADR 0006, authentication). OLM Operator Lifecycle Manager (olm.operatorframework.io): a precedent for what an operator owns and requires. PKCE Proof Key for Code Exchange (RFC 7636): protects the OAuth flow of a public client such as the CLI. PR Pull request. RBAC Role-based access control: roles granted on a scope, in Kubernetes and in Azure. RGD ResourceGraphDefinition: kro's blueprint for a custom API, turned into a CRD. SIEM Security information and event management: where a security team searches logs. SSE Server-sent events: a server keeps an HTTP response open and pushes events down it, how every session screen updates live (#223). STRIDE Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege: the six threats a threat model asks about for each part (Microsoft, "STRIDE model"); the method proposed for #125. STS Security Token Service: where AWS and GCP trade a federated token for their own. WIP Work in progress. XRD CompositeResourceDefinition: Crossplane's contract, a precedent for reefs.

docs.title: What init does
docs.text: What nereus init does, step by step: the checks, the two Helm releases, the installation, the profile and the time. A first run is in Prepare the cluster.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
init checks Docker (20.10.5 or newer, daemon running), k3d (5.0.0 or newer) and Helm (4.0.0 or newer) first. An older or missing one stops it before anything changes, naming the version it needs and where to get it.

Then it creates or reuses the local registry and the k3d cluster, and points the kube context at it. One registry serves every cluster init creates.

docs.title: Two Helm releases
docs.text:
From there init is two helm upgrade --installs and a wait (#1055), each a release of the same name in nereus-system; helm list --namespace nereus-system shows both.

  • kinds: the chart nereus-reefs installs the Reef, Nereid, Mandate, ServiceLevelObjective and Installation kinds and the nereus-system namespace.
  • nereus: the chart nereus installs the Nereus API with the values from the settings.
  • installation: reads back the installation the chart created.

The kinds are templates, so every helm upgrade updates them; each is kept on helm uninstall nereus-reefs, with every object stored in it. Install with Helm installs the same charts without init.

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
The two charts also hold the profile core (#1052): the tenancy reef's kinds and admission policy, the Reef tenancy and Nereus's own tree, the Organization getnereus with its Project nereus and four Projects under it.

All of it is kept on helm uninstall, since a person's own Projects hang from the tree (Know whose each thing is). On core alone, nereus status lists core and tenancy, both Ready.

docs.title: The values file
docs.text:
init writes the values it passes to the chart nereus to ~/.config/nereus/values.yaml, with the two helm commands that make the same install by hand in its header. --dry-run prints them and changes nothing.

~/.config/nereus/values.yaml
image: localhost:5111/nereus-api:0.1.0-nereus-local
installation:
  name: nereus-local
  id: 1521c310-295d-49e9-a8ef-ed097f23fc46
  alias: nereus-local
profile: internal-developer-platform
thetis:
  image: localhost:5111/thetis-controller:0.1.0-nereus-local
  localRegistry: localhost:5111=k3d-nereus-registry.localhost:5000
nereids:
  registry: localhost:5111
  tag: 0.1.0-nereus-local
ingress:
  address: http://localhost:8080

docs.title: The images
docs.text:
The chart writes every Nereid's image into the Profile's spec from nereids, and thetis installs them as written (#1425). A checkout's init takes them from the local registry, where docker push localhost:5111/... puts them.

A CLI installed from a release installs the charts published at its own version, oci://ghcr.io/getnereus/nereus/charts/nereus-reefs and .../nereus, and the chart takes each image by digest from its images.lock (#1785).

NEREUS_NEREIDS_REGISTRY or NEREUS_NEREIDS_TAG wins over both: a cluster that cannot reach the local registry takes every image from the registry make promote NEREUS_PROMOTE_TARGET=registry.example.com/team/nereus copied them to (Publish on ghcr.io).

docs.title: Flux holds the releases
docs.text:
Once Flux HelmReleases in nereus-system hold the releases nereus-reefs and nereus, Flux upgrades the charts with the HelmRelease's values, and init leaves both alone:

output
✓ kinds                     0.1s  release nereus-reefs held by HelmRelease nereus-reefs
✓ nereus                    0.0s  release nereus held by HelmRelease nereus
✓ installation              0.0s  kept nereus-local
✓ ready                     0.0s  the profile is HelmRelease nereus's
✓ public key                0.0s  the profile is HelmRelease nereus's

docs.title: The profile
docs.text:
init runs no step of the profile itself. The value profile makes the chart run thetis, the installer Nereid, which installs the profile's reefs, Nereids and Mandates in order (The profiles).

The step ready waits until each Nereid is Ready and prints how many and the slowest; each Nereid's time goes to the SLO report as a step of its own (ready keycloak).

The step public key prints the fingerprint of the secrets reef's key.

docs.title: The time
docs.text:
Each step prints its time, and the total ends the run, even on failure (✗, then the error). On a terminal the lines are drawn live; elsewhere (CI, a script, a redirect, NO_COLOR) they print as each step ends (#379).

The total is measured against the target's SLO (spec 0004): green under 50%, yellow from 50%, orange from 75%, red past 100%. Missing it never stops init; --check-slo fails above it plus 10% (Meet the time SLO).

docs.title: Run it again
docs.text: nereus init --yes again reuses the registry and the cluster, upgrades both releases with the same values (revision 2), keeps the installation's identity, and finds every Nereid Ready at once, in seconds and 0% green.

docs.title: The installation
docs.text:
Every installation has a name, an id and an alias, held by one Installation object in nereus-system that the first nereus init creates (spec 0006).

See it with nereus config installation show.

docs.title: Name
docs.text:
The object's name; it never changes. It prefixes every name the platform creates outside itself, such as the Azure resource group <installation>-platform (spec 0005).

It defaults to the cluster name; --installation-name sets another on the first init. A name is lowercase letters, digits and -, starts with a letter, at most 63 characters.

A second init with another name keeps the installation, and its installation line says kept nereus-local, not acme-dev: the name of an installation never changes; another name is another installation.

docs.title: Id
docs.text:
A random UUID; it never changes. Cloud resources can carry it, so they trace back to this installation. The API refuses a change, even by hand:

kubectl patch installations nereus-local \
  --namespace nereus-system \
  --type merge \
  --patch '{"spec":{"id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"}}'
output
The Installation "nereus-local" is invalid: spec.id: Invalid value: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000": the id of an installation never changes

The settings file also holds the id, so a cluster recreated from it is the same installation. A cluster recreated without it is a new installation with a new id.

docs.title: Alias
docs.text: What listings show; free text, at most 63 characters, no control characters. It may change; the name and id stay, and the settings file follows: nereus config installation set --alias "Acme Prod".

docs.title: Address
docs.text:
spec.url is the address the API is published at: the chart's ingress.address, rewritten on every release, so it is not a setting. An instance with none (no Gateway, only port-forward) has no url.

nereus status --output json and GET /v1/status answer it as installation.url, null when absent. The portal's account sheet shows it with the nereus login <url> line.

docs.title: Naming overrides
docs.text: When a generated cloud name is taken, a naming override sets it: issuer.storage, state.storage or secrets.vault, each checked against its resource's rules, with nereus config installation set --naming-override issuer.storage=acmeissuers01. See A name is taken.

docs.title: With Helm
docs.text:
The object belongs to the Helm release nereus and is kept on helm uninstall.

The chart creates it from installation.name, which it requires, and keeps the id and alias the cluster holds, so a plain helm upgrade --install gives the same identity as init.

Another name on the same cluster is refused, since the name never changes:

output
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: execution error at (nereus/templates/installation.yaml:10:4): the installation of this cluster is nereus-local, not acme: the name of an installation never changes; another name is another installation

docs.title: One per namespace
docs.text: A namespace holds one installation; a second is an error naming both. The undercloud and the overcloud are one installation: the pivot moves the object (Undercloud and overcloud).

docs.title: Inside the metrics reef
docs.text: What the Nereid victoriametrics of the metrics reef installs to keep the platform's metrics in VictoriaMetrics (Apache-2.0) (#742). The queries are in Collect metrics.

docs.title: The operator
docs.text:
The Nereid asks the release reef for the VictoriaMetrics operator (chart victoria-metrics-operator 0.68.1, operator v0.75.0, pinned by digest), released by the flux Mandate into the namespace metrics-system.

The operator turns a few Kubernetes kinds into running VictoriaMetrics components, as CloudNativePG turns a Cluster into PostgreSQL.

docs.title: VMSingle
docs.text: One VictoriaMetrics server, vmsingle-nereus in nereus-system: it stores the samples on a 2Gi volume for 14 days and answers the Prometheus query API on port 8428. It also serves vmui, the web UI, at /vmui.

docs.title: VMAgent
docs.text:
The scraper, vmagent-nereus, reads the targets the Nereid's scrape objects name and writes the samples to the VMSingle with the Prometheus remote write protocol.

It reads only the scrape objects labelled with the Nereid's name, so another tool's objects never change what it collects.

docs.title: What it scrapes
docs.text:
The VMPodScrape nereids selects every pod labelled core.getnereus.dev/metrics: "true" in nereus-system, on its port http and path /metrics. Each Nereid built on nereid-sdk carries that label (#741), so no Nereid is ever named.

The label nereid of each series comes from the pod's app.kubernetes.io/name, never from what the pod serves, so no pod can pose as a Nereid.

The VMNodeScrape kubelet-cadvisor reads each node's kubelet at /metrics/cadvisor: CPU and memory per container. A target that fails shows as down, and nothing else stops.

The VMPodScrape kube-state-metrics reads kube-state-metrics (#2177), which the Nereid also asks the release reef for: chart 9.1.0, v2.20.0 pinned by digest, in metrics-system. The Nereid does not wait for it: it logs a Release not Ready.

It reads only the pods and Deployments of nereus-system, through a Role there: no ClusterRole, no Secret, no ConfigMap. It exposes five series: the containers' requests, last termination reason and restarts, and the Deployments' ready and desired replicas.

Its series keep their own namespace and pod (honorLabels: true): those of the pods they describe.

docs.title: The contract
docs.text: The Mandate victoriametrics publishes status.query.url, the in-cluster address of the query API, and its Ready condition; nereus mandate get victoriametrics shows both. It names no backend: another Nereid of the metrics reef would publish the same field.

docs.title: Who reaches it
docs.text:
The query API has no credentials yet. A NetworkPolicy, applied by nereus nereid apply and not by the Nereid, lets only the VMAgent and the Nereus API reach port 8428; a kubectl port-forward is not subject to it.

Deleting series takes a random key nobody is given (-deleteAuthKey, from the Secret victoriametrics-delete-key). An admission policy holds every object the Nereid writes to its name and its whole spec.

docs.title: The proof
docs.text: make scene-metrics installs the reef on a throwaway cluster and runs the three queries of Collect metrics, expecting one series per Nereid.

docs.title: The profiles
docs.text: The four built-in profiles, core, internal-developer-platform, reference and secrets, and what each installs. What a profile is: Runtime install and profiles.

docs.title: Choose one
docs.text:
nereus init --profile internal-developer-platform installs core, then the profile (ADR 0014, #420). An unknown profile is refused before anything changes:

output
'minimal' is not a profile: core, internal-developer-platform, reference, secrets

nereus profile list lists the four; core is the default. Profiles are built in; profile create is not built yet.

docs.title: core
docs.text: No --profile, or --profile core, installs core alone with the tenancy reef (ADR 0015, #646): no other reef, no Nereid.

docs.title: reference
docs.text:
--profile reference (#1421) installs the reference Nereid of each reef that has one, such as reference-secrets (#486), in place of the tools: the reefs' kinds answer end to end and no tool image is pulled. make scene-core runs it.

The authorization reef's, reference-authorization, is the gate Nereid of ADR 0031 there: a held object stays Pending until its Approval is decided (#2213).

docs.title: internal-developer-platform
docs.text:
Each Nereid comes after the Nereids of the reefs it requires. With this profile the instance offers sign-in, so nereus status, reef and nereid read through the Nereus API with your token.

  • Secrets: Nereid openbao, Mandate default and the vault default (Keep a secret).
  • Release: Nereid flux and Mandate flux (Release a chart).
  • Database: Nereid cloudnative-pg, which installs CloudNativePG through a Release, and Mandate cloudnative-pg.
  • Authentication: Nereid keycloak, its Database keycloak and Mandate keycloak (Turn on authentication).
  • The entrance: the Gateway API CRDs, Istio through the release reef and the Gateway istio-system/ingress (#951).
  • Portal: Nereid and Mandate nereus-portal, after the entrance (#896).
  • Metrics: Nereid and Mandate victoriametrics (Collect metrics).
  • Environment: Nereid and Mandate vcluster (#827).
  • Catalog and delivery: Nereids catalog and kubernetes (Follow the golden path).
  • Teams and authorization: the teams reef and Nereid openfga (Say who may do what).
  • Registry: Nereid zot (Run a registry).
  • Messaging: Nereid nats and Mandate messaging-nats (Send messages).
  • Build and scm: Nereids buildkit and forgejo.
  • Usage and presentations: Nereid reference-usage (the usage reef's reference Nereid, until it has a real one) and Nereid leagore, so the portal shows the Usage and Presentations tabs (#2018).

docs.title: The secrets reef's key
docs.text:
OpenBao runs next to the Nereid openbao, which creates a non-exportable rsa-4096 key and writes its public key in the Mandate's status; thetis checks it, and init prints its fingerprint.

The key lives on the volume openbao-data and OpenBao unseals itself, so a restarted Pod keeps it; only a lost volume makes a new key. The token and the unseal key are generated once, in Secrets, and never printed.

docs.title: The addresses on k3d
docs.text:
On k3d, init reads the ingress port from k3d and passes it as the chart's ingress.address (#1079). A new portal Mandate gets publicUrl=http://localhost:<port>, and the keycloak Mandate http://auth.localhost:<port> (#1933).

On another cluster init passes none, and the Mandates get no publicUrl; an existing Mandate is kept as it is. Set the portal's with --param publicUrl=https://portal.example.com on nereus mandate apply nereus-portal.

A host no route names answers 404 from Envoy, and the portal answers on localhost:

curl --include --header "Host: no-route.example.com" http://localhost:8080/
output
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
server: istio-envoy
content-length: 0

docs.title: buildkit and forgejo
docs.text:
The profile installs buildkit in portable mode, Pod Security privileged, so it builds on any cluster. Where a sandbox runtime is installed, apply it in sandbox mode with nereus nereid apply buildkit --set BUILD_RUNTIME_CLASS=gvisor (#1231).

forgejo mirrors a repository through the scm reef's default Mandate forgejo (Mirror a repository). Forgejo copies from github.com alone until nereus nereid apply forgejo --set MIRROR_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=git.example.com names other hosts.

docs.title: Apply a profile later
docs.text:
A profile also layers on core after init (#425): nereus profile apply internal-developer-platform runs the same steps thetis runs, from the laptop, one line each, created the first time and unchanged after.

--without buildkit leaves a Nereid out; on a cluster the charts installed, the Profile's spec.exclude does the same. --dry-run lists the steps and changes nothing. On a cluster init has not prepared, it stops and points to nereus init.

docs.title: Describe a profile
docs.text:
nereus profile describe internal-developer-platform shows its ingress and each Nereid with its reef, Mandate and who requires it, in order.

The order comes from each Nereid's image label core.getnereus.dev/requires (#1368). With no registry answering, describe prints the order from the offline list cli/src/nereus/requires.yaml, and its last line says so.

docs.title: The proof
docs.text: make scene-idp proves the profile (#1261): on a throwaway k3d cluster, every Nereid Ready, the portal answering, an app built by buildkit and deployed answering, and nothing left behind. It runs only on the owner's word (#1420).

docs.title: Reefs and Nereids
docs.text: The rules behind nereus reef and nereus nereid: what each command checks, writes and refuses. The model is in Reef, Nereid and Mandate; a first run is in Apply a reef and its Nereid.

docs.title: Apply a reef
docs.text:
nereus reef apply release applies the reef's kinds from the version this CLI pins; applying again reports unchanged when no resourceVersion moved, as kubectl apply does.

nereus reef create release fails on an existing reef, as kubectl create does, and shows the installed version: reef cloud already exists (0.1.0).

apply takes three sources: the pinned version, local YAML with --from-file (a file or a folder, alias --path), or a reef package with --image (an OCI artifact of YAML layers). --dry-run lists what it would create.

With --from-file, it reports configured when the files changed a kind and unchanged when the same files come again.

docs.title: What a reef may ship
docs.text:
A reef is a Reef object, and may ship kinds of its own: the cloud reef ships Cloud with the CLI, never with a Nereid (spec 0005).

Whatever the source, the CLI checks every document first: only CustomResourceDefinitions of the platform's group, never a platform kind (Reef, Nereid, Mandate, Installation, ServiceLevelObjective), nor one another reef owns.

A reef may also ship a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and binding, named <name>.<reef group>, matching only its own group, without parameters. The API then refuses for every client, as the tenancy reef refuses a Project that is its own parent (#646).

docs.title: A reef with no Nereid
docs.text:
The reef's command group exists, empty until a Nereid is applied:

nereus release --help
output
 Usage: nereus release [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

 Reef release: no Nereid applied.

 Apply one: nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef release --image <image>

nereus reef list shows - under NEREIDS. Without the reef, nereid apply is refused with Apply it first: nereus reef apply release.

docs.title: Apply a Nereid
docs.text:
nereus nereid apply reference-release reads the image's labels in the registry (manifest and config, no layer): name, reef, required reefs, version, repository.

It checks the reef exists, writes the Nereid object pinned to the digest, runs the image as its controller and waits until it reports Ready. The same image again reports core/nereids/reference-release unchanged.

  • A name argument wins over the label.
  • --reef <reef> names a reef the label lacks, or picks one when the label lists several; it repeats.
  • An image that declares no reef is refused: declares no reef (label core.getnereus.dev/reef).

docs.title: The digest
docs.text:
The tag is resolved once to a digest (pinned to, the first 12 hex characters), so pushing the tag again never changes what runs.

An image given by digest (--image <repository>@sha256:<64 hex>) is applied as is, once its manifest matches. The full reference is in spec.image.

docs.title: Update a Nereid in place
docs.text:
nereus nereid apply reference-release --image moves a Nereid to another image with no delete: rules, Deployment and record move together; the apply ends once the new pod runs (#386).

--dry-run shows the digest it would move to. The same image with outdated rules names what it wrote, ending clusterrole/controller-reference-release rules updated.

A new image that fails prints the nereus nereid apply line with the last image that worked, which the Nereid records until a new pod has run.

Another reef is refused: moving a Nereid between reefs is a delete and an apply.

docs.title: List and get
docs.text:
nereus nereid list shows each Nereid with its reefs, image and status; nereus nereid get adds the pinned digest, title, description and the Mandates naming it.

reef list|get, nereid list|get and nereus status read through the Nereus API with the token of nereus login, so they need no kubeconfig; only a member of nereus-admins reads them.

Logged out, they print Not logged in with the nereus login line. Until the instance offers sign-in (core alone), they read the cluster with the kubeconfig and print the same.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
nereus nereid delete reference-release removes the Nereid with its commands, Deployment, Service and identity, which belong to the Nereid object. The reef stays, and its group says no Nereid applied.

nereid delete refuses the last Nereid of a reef that applied Nereids require (Require a reef), unless --force.

nereus reef delete release removes the Reef object and keeps its kinds, so a Nereid's objects stay. It is refused while a Nereid of the reef is applied, and names the nereid delete to run first.

docs.title: The objects
docs.text:
A reef and a Nereid are Kubernetes objects, Reef and Nereid of core.getnereus.dev: kubectl get reefs and kubectl get nereids list them.

One writer per field (ADR 0005, one writer for each field of an object): the CLI writes the reef and the Nereid's spec.image, spec.reefs, spec.requires and spec.version; the controller writes only status.conditions and status.commands.

The CLI caches each reef's group and its Nereid's commands in ~/.cache/nereus/commands.json, as kubectl caches API discovery; reef and nereid commands refresh it.

docs.title: The settings file
docs.text:
The file ~/.config/nereus/init.yaml holds the settings of nereus init: written once with --generate-file, read by every plain nereus init.

A setting comes from its flag, else from the file, else from its default, in that order. An unknown key is an error.

docs.title: The file
docs.text:
Two YAML documents, written by nereus init --generate-file: an InitConfig, how to build the platform from this machine, and the Installation, as it goes to the cluster.

The first init writes the installation's id into the file, so a cluster recreated from it is the same installation.

cat ~/.config/nereus/init.yaml
output
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: InitConfig
spec:
  profile: core
  ingressPort: 8080
  undercloud:
    create: false
    name: nereus
---
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Installation
metadata:
  name: nereus
spec:
  alias: nereus

docs.title: InitConfig
docs.text:
Every key lives under spec of the InitConfig document.

Key Flag Default profile --profile core ingressPort --ingress-port 8080 cloud --target absent (k3d) undercloud.create --create-cluster false undercloud.name --name nereus

profile is what init installs after core: core (nothing more), internal-developer-platform or secrets (ADR 0014, the profiles). A cloud target takes no profile yet.

ingressPort is the host port of the cluster's ingress gateway, from 1 to 65535, mapped on the loopback only to port 80 of the load balancer of a cluster init creates.

cloud names the Nereid of the cloud reef whose cloud the cluster bootstraps. It is absent for a local k3d cluster, and it cannot be k3d.

undercloud.create creates the cluster, or reuses it when it exists. undercloud.name is the name of the cluster to create.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The second document names the installation, after the cluster unless --installation-name says otherwise (spec 0006).

Key Meaning Written by metadata.name The installation's name --installation-name spec.alias The installation's alias init, from the name spec.id The installation's UUID the first init spec.naming.overrides Names that differ from the default the author

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Initialise the platform reads this file; the Glossary holds the words.

docs.title: What is built
docs.text:
What runs on main today, area by area, each with a status chip and where it is decided. built

Planned work and ideas are on the roadmap; each reef's commands are in the reef pages.

A chip says how far a feature is: built is code on main, planned has an issue that builds it, idea is still being refined.

docs.title: The CLI and the model
docs.text: Feature What it gives Status nereus init Prepares a cluster and installs nothing else; settings kept in a file. ADR 0003 built Time limit for init A time SLO for nereus init, checked in CI. spec 0004 built Installation identity One Installation object per cluster, written by the first init. spec 0006 built Reefs at runtime nereus reef create | apply | list | delete. ADR 0010 built Nereids at runtime nereus nereid apply reads the image's labels from the registry. ADR 0003 built Required reefs A Nereid is refused when a reef it requires is missing. spec 0003 built Commands from a Nereid A reef's command group is built from data in the Nereid's status. ADR 0004 built The CLI design commands reef, nereid, mandate and the conventions. ADR 0013 built One writer per field The CLI writes spec, a Nereid writes only status. ADR 0005 built Profiles core and internal-developer-platform; nereus profile apply. ADR 0014 built nereus doctor Whether an instance is healthy, from GET /v1/doctor. #799 built Swap checked in CI Swapping a Nereid changes no command. #124 built Untrusted Nereid output What a Nereid publishes is untrusted input, with a test. #134 built Nereid recovery A Nereid that stops is reported and recovers by itself. #133 built

docs.title: The Nereus API and MCP
docs.text: Feature What it gives Status Nereus API nereus-api in the cluster; nereus whoami calls GET /v1/me. #607 built MCP tools from reefs A reef declares tools; the API serves them at /mcp. ADR 0029 built Chosen MCP tools nereus mcp tool enable | disable in the Installation. #1809 built /mcp in Claude Code nereus mcp client add claude-code. #1880 built nereus-mcp retired The instance's entrance serves /mcp. #1810 built

docs.title: Cloud and identity
docs.text: Feature What it gives Status Reef kinds shipped by a reef The cloud reef ships its kind Cloud and its Mandate. spec 0005 built Cloud plans A Nereid's plan is checked, approved and run with the person's login. #307 built Requester tags Every cloud resource says which installation created it and why. #155 built Undercloud nereus init --target <name> brings up the k3d undercloud. #263 built Cloud grants A Nereid that requires cloud is granted access by the person. #310 built

docs.title: Reefs
docs.text: Feature What it gives Status secrets Vault and Secret, encrypted on the client. #530 built release Repository, Source, Target and Release. ADR 0010 built environment An Environment per agent, with an expiry; the kept cluster nereus. ADR 0026 built catalog Workload, Package, WorkloadType and PackageType. ADR 0016 built database A PostgreSQL per Database. ADR 0017 built messaging Topics and queues on NATS. ADR 0019 built registry Registry, Repository, publish and purge, with the zot Nereid. ADR 0021 built build Builds of a Workload's source and Triggers on new commits. spec 0009 built scm A GitHub App Mandate, a Forgejo Mirror and a one-hour Token. ADR 0024 built metrics The victoriametrics Nereid. #742 built ideas The doris Nereid and Tide, its portal tab. #1106 built portal A PWA that says who you are. spec 0008 built usage A coding agent's quota window and its forecast. #1590 built teams Team and Member on the tenancy tree. #1646 built presentations A deck kept by the platform and a Session to follow. ADR 0028 built authorization Role and Binding, asked before every read and write. ADR 0027 built

docs.title: Building Nereids and the platform
docs.text: Feature What it gives Status nereid-sdk The Nereids' shared library, used by five Nereids. #754 built Nereid template scripts/nereid/new --reef <reef> --tool <tool>. #752 built Reference Nereids reference-build, reference-delivery, reference-registry. #1502 built Checks on every pull request Tests, deck tests, strict docs build, shellcheck. #49 built Deploy main to live scripts/deploy/live, and the line of main. #162 built

docs.title: The authentication reef
docs.text: Who the person is, and who the platform is towards the systems it acts on.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus login The browser opens, and the login comes back to the terminal
  • nereus login A machine with no browser logs in from another device
  • nereus login A new instance has one obvious way in: its initial admin
  • nereus login A new token without the browser, with the groups read again
  • nereus logout Logging out ends the session at the identity provider too
  • nereus whoami The Nereus API says who you are
  • nereus authentication app-register With no App yet, the Nereid creates it in the browser
  • nereus authentication token create catalog A Token lends one repository for an hour
  • nereus authentication token list list shows each Token, never its value

docs.title: login
docs.text:
Authorization code with PKCE, on a listener of 127.0.0.1.

nereus login
output
Opening https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/protocol/openid-connect/auth?... in the browser.
logged in as ana-silva (nereus-users), issuer https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus

Next steps:

  nereus whoami
  https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/account/account-security/signing-in   (set a password, optional)

docs.title: login-device
docs.text:
The device grant: open the page elsewhere and type the code.

nereus login \
  --use-device-code
output
Open https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/device and enter ABCD-EFGH (expires in 10 minutes).
logged in as ana-silva (nereus-users), issuer https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus

Next steps:

  nereus whoami
  https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/account/account-security/signing-in   (set a password, optional)

docs.title: login-initial-admin
docs.text:
The password goes to the clipboard, never to the terminal.

nereus login \
  --initial-admin
output
The initial admin's password is in your clipboard (user nereus). Paste it on the login page.
Opening https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/protocol/openid-connect/auth?... in the browser.
logged in as nereus (nereus-admins), issuer https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus

Next steps:

  nereus whoami
  https://auth.example.com/realms/nereus/account/account-security/signing-in   (set a password, optional)

docs.title: login-refresh
docs.text:
Renew the session, so a group joined since the last login shows.

nereus login \
  --refresh
output
token refreshed for ana-silva, valid until 14:05

docs.title: logout
docs.text:
Revoke the session, then delete the credentials.

nereus logout
output
logged out nereus@example.com: session revoked, ~/.config/nereus/credentials deleted

docs.title: whoami
docs.text:
GET /v1/me with the token of nereus login.

nereus whoami
output
ana-silva (nereus-admins, nereus-users)

docs.title: app-register
docs.text:
An action the github Nereid publishes under the reef.

nereus authentication app-register \
  --mandate team \
  --org example-team
output
→ opening the browser to create the GitHub App "nereus-prod"
✓ secrets/team-app-key stored by the Nereid (the key never reaches this machine)
✓ secrets/team-webhook-secret and secrets/team-oauth-client stored by the Nereid
✓ core/mandates/team configured (appId 900001, privateKey team-app-key, webhookSecret team-webhook-secret)

Next steps:

  Install it on the org: https://github.com/apps/nereus-prod/installations/new
  nereus mandate get team

docs.title: token-create
docs.text:
A token to read one repository, from the default Mandate.

nereus authentication token create catalog \
  --repository example/app \
  --permission contents=read
output
✓ authentication/tokens/catalog created (expires in 1h, mandate github)

Next steps:

  nereus authentication token get catalog

docs.title: token-list
docs.text:
Every Token.

nereus authentication token list
output
TOKEN    REPOSITORY   PERMISSIONS    MANDATE  EXPIRES  STATUS
catalog  example/app  contents=read  github   1h       Ready

docs.title: The authorization reef
docs.text: Every command of the first slice: Users, teams, roles and bindings, and who may do what.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus reef apply authorization The authorization reef brings roles and bindings
  • nereus profile apply internal-developer-platform openfga answers who may do what
  • nereus user create ana A person is one User, whatever the login
  • nereus user list Every User, and how many identities each has
  • nereus authorization role list One built-in role, four examples to edit
  • nereus authorization role get team-lead A role is a list of rules: reef, kinds, verbs
  • nereus authorization role create release-manager A new role takes the words the CLI already uses
  • nereus authorization role delete administrator The administrator role cannot be deleted
  • nereus authorization binding create payments-developers A binding gives a role to a team on a node
  • nereus authorization binding create payments-leads A position narrows the binding to the tech lead
  • nereus authorization binding list Every binding of a node, and who it reaches
  • nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments Ana asks, and the answer names the binding
  • nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments Bruno may not, and the answer says why
  • nereus can-i create build/builds The shortcut asks the same question
  • nereus authorization can-i drive presentations/sessions/platform-day Presenting is a right: a Session's speakers drive it
  • nereus authorization can-i assist presentations/sessions/platform-day The staff assists a Session, and never drives it
  • nereus environment create staging Bruno's environment is refused, politely
  • nereus environment create staging Ana's environment is created
  • nereus teams member delete ana planned #1307 Leaving the team removes the access
  • nereus environment list Without openfga, everything closes
  • nereus authorization gate create payments-environments A Gate says which requests wait, and for whom
  • nereus environment create staging planned #2119 The object exists at once, and stands Pending
  • nereus authorization approval list The approver sees what waits for a decision
  • nereus authorization approval approve staging-create-7f3a Approving lifts the hold, and the Nereid provisions
  • nereus authorization approval reject staging-create-7f3a Rejecting keeps the history, and provisions nothing
  • nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments planned #2124 No, but Bruno may ask

docs.title: reef-apply
docs.text:
The kinds of the reef.

nereus reef apply authorization
output
✓ core/reefs/authorization created (authorization.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: bindings, roles)

Next steps:

  nereus nereid apply openfga --reef authorization

docs.title: nereid-apply
docs.text:
The profile installs the Nereid and its default Mandate (an excerpt).

nereus profile apply internal-developer-platform
output
✓ networkpolicy openfga                      0.0s  networkpolicies/openfga applied (only nereus-api and vmagent-nereus reach openfga)
✓ nereid openfga                            1m19s  core/nereids/openfga created, Ready
✓ mandate openfga                            7.0s  core/mandates/openfga created (reef: authorization, nereid: openfga, default)

docs.title: user-create
docs.text:
The tech lead.

nereus user create ana \
  --email ana@example.com
output
✓ core/users/ana created

docs.title: user-list
docs.text:
The people of this instance.

nereus user list
output
NAME   EMAIL              IDENTITIES  AGE
ana    ana@example.com    1           2m
bruno  bruno@example.com  0           1m

docs.text:
The roles of this instance.

nereus authorization role list
output
NAME           RULES                    BUILT IN
administrator  *:*:*                    yes
developer      *:*:list,get and 3 more  -
requester      *:*:list,get and 1 more  -
team-lead      *:*:list,get and 5 more  -

docs.title: role-get
docs.text:
What a team lead may do.

nereus authorization role get team-lead
output
team-lead: 6 rules
REEF         KINDS         VERBS
*            *             list,get

docs.title: role-create
docs.text:
A role of this instance's own.

nereus authorization role create release-manager \
  --rule release:releases:create,apply,delete
output
✓ authorization/roles/release-manager created

Next steps:

  nereus authorization binding create <name> --role release-manager --team <team> --owner project/<project>

docs.title: role-delete
docs.text:
No one locks the instance out.

nereus authorization role delete administrator
output
✗ authorization/roles/administrator is built in: it cannot be changed or deleted. To see who holds it, run:
  nereus authorization binding list --role administrator
  Nothing was changed.

docs.title: binding-team
docs.text:
Everyone in the team is a developer of the Project.

nereus authorization binding create payments-developers \
  --role developer \
  --team payments \
  --owner project/payments
output
✓ authorization/bindings/payments-developers created

Next steps:

  nereus authorization binding list --owner project/payments

docs.title: binding-position
docs.text:
Only who holds the position.

nereus authorization binding create payments-leads \
  --role team-lead \
  --team payments \
  --position tech-lead \
  --owner project/payments
output
✓ authorization/bindings/payments-leads created

Next steps:

  nereus authorization binding list --owner project/payments

docs.title: binding-list
docs.text:
Who may do what on the Project.

nereus authorization binding list \
  --owner project/payments
output
NAME                 SUBJECT                  ROLE       OWNER
payments-developers  team/payments            developer  project/payments
payments-leads       team/payments/tech-lead  team-lead  project/payments

docs.title: can-i-yes
docs.text:
Signed in as ana: with no --user, the question is about the caller.

nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments \
  --owner project/payments
output
yes: authorization/bindings/payments-leads gives team-lead to team/payments/tech-lead at project/payments

docs.title: can-i-no
docs.text:
About someone else.

nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments \
  --owner project/payments \
  --user bruno
output
no: no binding gives bruno create on environment/environments at project/payments

Next steps:

  nereus authorization binding list --owner project/payments

docs.title: can-i-shortcut
docs.text:
Signed in as bruno: a developer creates builds.

nereus can-i create build/builds \
  --owner project/payments
output
yes: authorization/bindings/payments-developers gives developer to team/payments at project/payments

docs.title: can-i-drive
docs.text:
Ana is a speaker of platform-day.

nereus authorization can-i drive presentations/sessions/platform-day \
  --user ana
output
yes: ana is a speaker of platform-day

docs.title: can-i-assist
docs.text:
Carla is on the staff team of platform-day.

nereus authorization can-i assist presentations/sessions/platform-day \
  --user carla
output
yes: carla is on the staff of platform-day (team stage-2-staff)

docs.title: enforce-denied
docs.text:
Signed in as bruno.

nereus environment create staging \
  --owner project/payments
output
✗ environment/environments/staging: bruno may not create environment/environments at project/payments. To see who may, run:
  nereus authorization binding list --owner project/payments
  Nothing was changed.

docs.title: enforce-allowed
docs.text:
Signed in as ana, the tech lead.

nereus environment create staging \
  --owner project/payments
output
✓ environment/environments/staging created (mandate: vcluster, nereid: vcluster)

Next steps:

  nereus environment get staging --watch

docs.title: leave-team
docs.text:
Ana leaves the team.

nereus teams member delete ana \
  --team payments
output
✓ teams/teams/payments/members/ana deleted

docs.title: fail-closed
docs.text:
A read while the Nereid does not answer.

nereus environment list
output
✗ authorization does not answer (nereid: openfga): nothing is allowed until it is back. To see what is down, run:
  nereus doctor
  Nothing was changed.

docs.title: gate-create
docs.text:
Requests to create an Environment in payments wait for an approver.

nereus authorization gate create payments-environments \
  --reef environment \
  --kinds environments \
  --verbs create \
  --owner project/payments
output
✓ authorization/gates/payments-environments created

Next steps:

  nereus authorization gate list

docs.title: create-held
docs.text:
Bruno may ask, not create.

nereus environment create staging \
  --owner project/payments
output
✓ environment/environments/staging created, waiting for approval (authorization/approvals/staging-create-7f3a; approvers: team/payments/tech-lead)

Next steps:

  nereus environment get staging --watch

docs.title: approval-list
docs.text:
Every held request has one Approval.

nereus authorization approval list
output
NAME                 TARGET                            VERB    REQUESTED BY  PHASE    AGE
staging-create-7f3a  environment/environments/staging  create  bruno         Pending  2m

docs.title: approval-approve
docs.text:
Ana, of the tech lead team, decides.

nereus authorization approval approve staging-create-7f3a \
  --reason "sprint demo"
output
✓ authorization/approvals/staging-create-7f3a approved; environment/environments/staging released

docs.title: approval-reject
docs.text:
Or the approver says no, with the reason.

nereus authorization approval reject staging-create-7f3a \
  --reason "use the shared staging"
output
✓ authorization/approvals/staging-create-7f3a rejected; environment/environments/staging will not be provisioned

docs.title: can-i-may-ask
docs.text:
The answer to create is still no, and says who decides.

nereus authorization can-i create environment/environments \
  --owner project/payments \
  --user bruno
output
no, but may ask: authorization/gates/payments-environments holds create for team/payments/tech-lead's approval

docs.title: The build reef
docs.text: Every command that builds an image from a Workload's source inside the cluster.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus build create hello-1 create builds a Workload at the commit its Nereid read
  • nereus build get hello-1 get shows the digest the registry answered
  • nereus build list list shows every build, a line each
  • nereus build get app-1 A private repository is fetched with a token for that build alone
  • nereus build delete hello-1 delete removes the Build and its Job, never the image
  • nereus build trigger create triton trigger create builds a Workload on each new commit of its Mirror
  • nereus build trigger list trigger list shows the commit each one saw and its last Build
  • nereus build trigger get triton trigger get shows the Mirror it follows and the commit it saw
  • nereus build trigger delete triton trigger delete stops new Builds and leaves the ones it made

docs.title: build-create
docs.text:
Two Jobs in the namespace builds: fetch, then build and push.

nereus build create hello-1 \
  --workload hello

docs.title: The catalog reef
docs.text: Every command that says what Nereus has: what runs, what is published, and whether it holds together.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus catalog apply One apply registers the repository
  • nereus catalog workload create edge-cloudflare create writes an entry from flags
  • nereus catalog list list searches by type
  • nereus catalog delete openbao delete never touches what runs
  • nereus catalog package create nereus A Package says where it is published
  • nereus catalog workload-type list A type is a name plus answers

docs.title: The delivery reef
docs.text: Every command that takes a Workload to an Environment, and says what runs.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus reef apply delivery The reef, then the Nereid that delivers to Kubernetes
  • nereus workload deploy hello@dev One command takes a Workload to an Environment
  • nereus workload deploy hello deploy never guesses the target
  • nereus workload deploy hello@dev deploy runs what a Build pushed, by its digest
  • nereus workload deploy hello-dev Every deploy is a new request, even with the same tag
  • nereus workload deploy hello@dev --dry-run shows the Delivery, with the tag as typed
  • nereus workload deploy hello@dev --wait brings the Nereid's reason to the terminal
  • nereus workload list workload list says what the catalog has
  • nereus delivery list delivery list says what was deployed
  • nereus delivery get hello-dev delivery get says what runs and where
  • nereus workload logs hello-dev workload logs reads a Delivery by its name or its pair
  • nereus workload deploy hello@dev A Delivery in a file resolves once
  • nereus delivery delete hello-dev Deleting a Delivery takes the app out of the Environment
  • nereus template render python-service planned #851 A template writes files, and the catalog registers them

docs.title: The edge reef
docs.text: Every command of the edge reef: domains, zones and routes, in the order a person types them.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus reef apply edge One command applies the edge reef, with its kinds Route, Zone and Domain
  • nereus nereid apply cloudflare The cloudflare Nereid runs the tunnel its Mandate names
  • nereus nereid apply godaddy The godaddy Nereid talks to the registrar, through its Mandate
  • nereus edge zone create getnereus.dev A zone gives the domain the nameservers that will answer for it
  • nereus edge domain list The registrar shows its domains, with the credentials asked for now and never stored
  • nereus edge domain apply getnereus.dev Nereus takes the domain and sends it to the zone's nameservers
  • nereus edge domain list The list shows the domains Nereus looks after
  • nereus edge domain get getnereus.dev One domain shows every detail, its nameservers one per line
  • nereus edge route create triton A route makes a hostname reach the platform
  • nereus edge endpoint list The Nereids say what they serve, never where it runs
  • nereus edge route create triton A route publishes a reef's endpoint at a fixed address
  • nereus edge apply One file applies every Route and Zone, each checked before any is written
  • nereus edge route delete triton A delete waits until its Nereid takes away what it made, unless told not to

docs.title: The environment reef

docs.title: The registry reef
docs.text: Every command that runs an image registry in the cluster and publishes to it.

docs.title: Commands

  • nereus registry apply apply takes files, and waits for the Nereid
  • nereus registry delete main delete removes the registry and what its Nereid made

docs.title: The release reef
docs.text: Every command of the release reef: where a chart comes from, what it is, where it goes and the release itself.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus reef apply release One command applies the release reef, with its four kinds
  • nereus nereid apply reference-release The reference-release Nereid answers every kind with no tool, through the reference Mandate
  • nereus nereid apply flux The flux Nereid installs Flux and becomes the default through its Mandate
  • nereus release repository create codecentric A repository says where the charts come from
  • nereus release repository create codecentric Apply takes a file, and applying what already holds changes nothing
  • nereus release repository list The list shows every repository and whether it is ready
  • nereus release repository get codecentric One repository, by its name
  • nereus release repository delete codecentric A repository goes once no source names it
  • nereus release source create keycloak A source is one chart of a repository, at one version
  • nereus release source create keycloak A new version is one file away
  • nereus release source list The list shows every source with its chart and version
  • nereus release source get keycloak One source, by its name
  • nereus release repository create ghcr Publishing goes through the platform, with its credential, never yours
  • nereus release source delete keycloak A source in use is refused, with what to delete first
  • nereus release target create dev-identity A target is a namespace, of an environment or of the cluster Nereus runs in
  • nereus release target create dev-identity Applying the same target again changes nothing
  • nereus release target list The list shows every target with its environment and namespace
  • nereus release target get dev-identity One target, by its name
  • nereus release target delete dev-identity A target goes once no release names it
  • nereus release create keycloak-reference A release runs a source in a target, through the reef's default Mandate
  • nereus release create keycloak Values and a Mandate of your choice, with Flux installing the chart
  • nereus release create keycloak A release asks for its secrets by name, and its values never pass through Nereus
  • nereus release create keycloak-reference One folder holds the whole release, and the second apply changes nothing
  • nereus release list The list shows every release, its version and the Nereid behind it
  • nereus release get keycloak-reference One release, by its name
  • nereus release delete keycloak-reference Deleting a release uninstalls its chart
  • kubectl apply The Gateway API CRDs come first, applied by hand for now
  • nereus release repository create istio Istio's charts come from its own Helm repository
  • nereus release source create istio-base Three charts at one pinned version: base and istiod first
  • nereus release source create istio-gateway Three charts at one pinned version: then the gateway, into istio-system
  • nereus release create istio-base Each chart starts once the previous one is Ready: base first
  • nereus release create istiod Then istiod, the control plane
  • nereus release create istio-gateway Last, the ingress gateway, with no values of its own
  • kubectl apply A Gateway opens Envoy's listener, and with no route it answers 404

docs.title: The rooms reef
docs.text: Every command of the rooms reef: rooms, peers and the agents' sessions, on a Topic of the messaging reef.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus reef apply rooms One command applies the rooms reef and its kinds

  • nereus rooms create ops A room is created by name, and its Topic comes with it
  • nereus rooms list One room shows whose it is and the peers in it

  • nereus rooms peer get ana.doto One Peer says whose agent it is, and which rooms it is in

  • nereus rooms follow A person follows the room where the agents talk
  • nereus rooms pull doto A hook pulls each room's new messages into the session
  • nereus rooms post "k3d-nereus is mine until 21:30" A person posts to the room, as the agents do
  • nereus order create "run make checks" idea An order goes to one idle agent, and the list follows it

docs.title: The secrets reef
docs.text: Every command of the secrets reef: vaults, and the secrets in them, encrypted before they leave the machine.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• nereus init The profile brings the secrets reef ready to use, with its key and the vault default
  • nereus secrets create google-oauth A secret is encrypted on your machine, before it leaves it
  • nereus secrets create google-oauth Creating it again is refused, with how to change it
  • nereus secrets create github-app A key can come from a file, such as a private key
  • nereus secrets create google-oauth Apply takes a folder of secrets, and the second apply changes nothing
  • nereus secrets list The list shows every secret with its keys, never a value
  • nereus secrets get default/google-oauth One secret, by its vault and name
  • nereus secrets get google-oauth As YAML, the object shows the names of its keys instead of the envelopes
  • nereus secrets vault list The list shows every vault, its Nereid and how many secrets it holds
  • nereus secrets vault create team-a A vault for a team, with the namespaces allowed to bind its secrets
  • nereus secrets vault delete default A vault that holds secrets is refused, with what to delete first
  • nereus secrets delete default/google-oauth A secret goes by its full name, or by its name in the vault default
  • nereus secrets vault delete team-a An empty vault goes
  • nereus secrets binding create keycloak-google A binding makes a Kubernetes Secret from a secret, in a namespace the vault allows
  • nereus secrets binding create payments A namespace the vault does not allow, or a key the secret does not have, is refused before anything is written
  • cat test/charts/binding-demo/templates/secretbinding.yaml A chart asks for its secret with a SecretBinding among its templates
  • nereus secrets binding list Every binding, with who asked for it
  • nereus secrets get default/google-oauth A secret says where it is used, and is not deleted while it is
  • nereus secrets binding delete keycloak-google A binding goes, and its Kubernetes Secret with it

docs.title: The tenancy reef

docs.title: Commands

docs.title: Board tools
docs.text:
A snapshot of 2026-11-05: versions, activity and features change, so check them again before deciding.

GitHub Projects is poor on a phone. This page compares open source alternatives that can be self-hosted, focused on use on a phone, then on deploy and on integration with GitHub. It is material for the board reef (#137), where Vikunja may become a Nereid; nothing here is decided.

docs.title: How it was checked
docs.text:
Only Vikunja was tried: version 2.7.1 in a local container with SQLite and 12 sample tasks, in Chrome emulating a 390×844 phone. The other columns come from each project's documentation, source code and issues. A cell says "not checked" when none of these answered it.

What the trial left out: a real phone, dragging cards by touch, a task's detail page, and installing the PWA (its prompt appeared, the installation was not done).

not tried; no PWA mentioned No: the viewport meta tag is commented out in app/index.jade, and "Need responsive for mobile" (taiga-front #93) is open Phones and tablets are a Pro feature Not checked Kanban on a small screen Good in the trial: 300 px columns with scroll snap, the next column visible, no horizontal overflow of the page Not checked Poor, from the code and the issues Community has open bugs: "cards do not open on mobile" (#1282), a card modal too large (#190) Not checked Deploy One container with SQLite; it exits at start when its data directories are not writable Compose or an all-in-one container Compose with 9 services, two of them RabbitMQ Compose with 2 containers (app and Postgres) Not maintained Resources Light: about 70 MiB measured, nearly idle; a REST API and outgoing webhooks Links PRs to work packages; does not import issues The best: an importer for issues, comments and history, and a webhook None; a REST API and webhooks Not checked License AGPL-3.0 (app: MIT) GPL-3.0 MPL-2.0 (back), AGPL-3.0 (front) Fair Use License: source available, not open source Source: AGPL-3.0 or commercial; docs.title: Reading it
docs.text:
1. Vikunja is the only free and open source option with a board proven usable at phone width, and it is the lightest. Use its PWA rather than the app in alpha. Its gap is GitHub.
  2. OpenProject has no boards in its app and asks for 4 GB for a Kanban problem.
  3. Taiga has the best import and fails the main criterion. It fits only if migrating the issues weighs more than the phone.
  4. Planka leaves phones to its paid plan, and its license is not open source.
  5. Focalboard is the negative baseline: its own README says it is not maintained, which is enough to rule it out.

docs.title: The open idea
docs.text: Since Vikunja does not know GitHub, the integration may live in the platform: a process that copies issues from one to the other (#1029). scripts/board/queue (690 lines) calls GitHub directly and holds the WIP limit and claim, so replacing GitHub as the source of truth would mean rewriting it, while a copy would not.
