docs.text:
• Touches: api/authorization_routes.py (POST /v1/authorization/can-i), cli/src/nereus/commands/authorization.py, the top-level shortcut in cli/src/nereus/cli.py, the deck's slides to built.
  • Depends on: task 7.
  • Does: nereus authorization can-i <verb> <reef>/<kinds> [--owner <kind>/<name>] [--user <name>]: the deck's lines (yes: authorization/bindings/<binding> gives <role> to <subject> at <node>, or no: no binding gives <user> <verb> on <reef>/<kinds> at <node>); exit code 0 for yes and 1 for no. Asking with --user needs authorization:can-i:get at that node. The shortcut nereus can-i is the same command.
  • Done when: the deck's three can-i slides print what they show.
  • Proves it: the unit tests, and the step in the final scene.

docs.title: Task 9 (#1651): only who may bind assigns a position a binding names
docs.text:
• Touches: cli/src/nereus/teams_service.py, its tests.
  • Depends on: task 7.
  • Does: creating or changing a Member with a spec.position that some Binding names is allowed only to who may authorization:bindings:create at that binding's node (decision 8); the refusal names the binding and says who can do it.
  • Done when: a User with only teams:members:create,delete adds a member with no position, and is refused giving themselves tech-lead.
  • Proves it: the unit tests, and the step in the final scene.

docs.title: Task 10 (#1655): the profile, the walkthrough and the docs
docs.text:
• Touches: cli/src/nereus/charts/nereus/profiles/internal-developer-platform.yaml (the teams reef, the authorization reef with {name: openfga} and its default Mandate), ADR 0014's note that these "do not exist yet", a new docs/guides/access/authorization.md, docs/features.md (the rows that waited for #897, and the stand-ins table), mkdocs.yml, the decks' remaining statuses.
  • Depends on: tasks 4, 5, 6 and 7.
  • Does: the profile installs the two reefs and the Nereid; the walkthrough is the deck's story with real output; docs/features.md says what is built.
  • Done when: the profile lists the two reefs, the Nereid and the default Mandate, and its tests pass; a fresh instance of the profile ending with the authorization reef Ready is seen in task 11.
  • Proves it: the profile's unit tests (cli/tests/test_profiles.py), the docs build, and task 11's make scene. make scene-idp is not delegated to this journey: leave it, named in the PR, for the owner's word.

docs.title: Task 11 (#1652): the final scene, and the slice on k3d-nereus
docs.text:
• Touches: test/scene (a new step file it sources), a helper that creates two local people in the scene's Keycloak through its admin API (the Secret keycloak-admin), with a verified e-mail at example.com, and signs each in with test/oidc-flow.
  • Depends on: every task above.
  • Does: the scene below, on the throwaway cluster of make scene; then scripts/registry/release publish, scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster, the two reefs and the Nereid applied on k3d-nereus, and the proof of decision 22 there. On both clusters the first step is the administrator's own access: the signed-in administrator creates their own User (the e-mail nereus whoami shows) and a binding of administrator to it, through the emergency exit, once.
  • Done when: the scene passes, and on k3d-nereus nereus doctor ends with exit code 0 (a WARN of the emergency exit is expected after the first step) and nereus authorization can-i ... --user bruno answers no while --user ana answers yes.
  • Proves it: make scene, and the commands' output on k3d-nereus pasted in #1644.

docs.title: The final scene
docs.text:
On the scene's cluster, signed in as the scene's administrator unless a step says otherwise:

  1. nereus user create ana and bruno; a team payments owned by project/payments; ana a member with the position tech-lead, bruno a member with none.
  2. Bindings: developer to the team, team-lead to the position, both at project/payments.
  3. can-i create environment/environments --owner project/payments --user ana says yes and names the binding; --user bruno says no.
  4. As bruno: nereus environment list answers; nereus environment create is refused with its next steps and exit code 1; nothing was created.
  5. As ana: the same create --dry-run is accepted.
  6. As bruno: adding a member with no position is refused (bruno is not a team lead); as ana, it is accepted; as ana, giving herself or anyone the position tech-lead on a second team whose binding she may not create is refused (task 9).
  7. nereus teams member delete ana --team payments; can-i for ana now says no, and as ana the create --dry-run is refused (leaving the team removes the access).
  8. A person with a login and no User is refused everything but nereus whoami, which says so.
  9. The openfga Nereid scaled to zero: as bruno, a list is refused with the "down" message; as the administrator it answers, and nereus doctor shows the WARN of the emergency exit. Scaled back, bruno's list answers again.
  10. OpenFGA's database deleted and the Nereid restarted: after one pass, step 3's answers are the same (the objects are the source of truth).

docs.title: Carrying it out
docs.text:
Who: one Opus agent orchestrates and owns the journey (it comments "Owner session: " on #1644), with up to five subagents at a time and about eleven subagent runs in all. Opus for tasks 2 to 9 and 11; Sonnet for tasks 1 and 10. A Fable agent is called only for a design decision or a bug the plan does not cover (decision 21); its answer and the reason go in the progress log.

Waves:

Wave Tasks, in parallel Ends with A 3, 4, 5, 6, and one subagent for 1 then 2 (merge order: 3, 4, 5, then 6) milestone 1: the kinds and the Nereid on main; nothing is enforced, so nothing changes for anyone B 7, with 10's docs drafted beside it the API asks C 8, 9, 10 milestone 2: the slice is whole D 11, by the orchestrator milestone 3: the scene passes and k3d-nereus runs it

A release and a deploy to k3d-nereus happen at milestones 1, 2 and 3, never between.

Quota-safe order. Every task merges alone and leaves main green and usable: tasks 3 to 6 add kinds and a Nereid nothing uses yet; task 7 changes nothing while the reef has no Mandate; the profile gains the reef only in task 10. When the quota ends, a new session resumes from the state, never from memory: gh issue view 1644 (the sub-issues open and closed, and the comments), the progress log below, gh pr list, git worktree list. A task with a worktree and no merged PR is resumed in that worktree.

The rules every subagent gets (the same block in every brief, plus its task's section):

  • Read CLAUDE.md, docs/agent/rules.md and docs/agent/worktrees.md first. Work only in the task's worktree (scripts/worktree/new <type> <issue>-<slug>); the main clone is read and pulled only.
  • Its own scratch directory for commit messages and notes, never a shared one.
  • Tests first. Targeted tests while working; make checks once at the end; never two scenes at the same time on this machine (the orchestrator says when a subagent may run make scene-core; make scene and make scene-idp are run by the orchestrator).
  • Conventional Commits, one per topic, with git -C <worktree> add --all then git -C <worktree> commit --file <message file> as plain separate commands.
  • Public by design: no e-mail, personal or company name, internal domain, account id or token; examples use example.com.
  • Never speak. Never message another session. Never push or merge: the orchestrator does both.
  • Report in a few lines: the commits, each check run and its result, what was left out and why. Never file contents.

The orchestrator, per task: brief the subagent; when it reports, read the diff, rebase onto main, run what the task's "Proves it" names, open the PR saying what ran, merge by rebase, close the sub-issue, add its line to the progress log, remove the worktree. A check failing three times in a row on the same task stops that task: the log says what was tried, and the orchestrator goes on to a task that does not depend on it.

Limits, with no exception:

  • Nothing destructive on the host: no sudo, no docker system prune, no deleting of a k3d cluster other than the scenes' own throwaway ones, no rm outside a worktree or a scratch directory, nothing written to the owner's home but what make already writes.
  • No cloud resource: no cloud provider's CLI is run at all.
  • k3d-nereus is reached only through scripts/registry/release publish, scripts/deploy/live --allow-kept-cluster and the nereus CLI. It may go down and come up as often as needed. While another session is alive on the repository (claude-peers), an [ask] comes first (docs/agent/peers.md).
  • The release publishes to the project's own registry on ghcr.io. A new package (the openfga Nereid's image) is private until a click makes it public (#1338, docs/agent/publish.md). The owner pre-authorized that click for this journey (2026-11-15): the agent makes it in the owner's browser (the Chrome tools), for the packages this plan creates and for nothing else on that page, and records it in the progress log. When the browser is not reachable, install the Nereid on k3d-nereus from the local registry (docs/guides/operate/kept-cluster-update.md, "without publishing": the image at localhost:5111, then nereus nereid apply openfga --image ...), and leave the click as the one item waiting for the owner.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
Each with the better solution it leads to.

  • A second identity on the same User: ADR 0006's e-mail code through a notification reef; nereus user identity commands.
  • The instance's root User (#1306): created by nereus init, MFA required, its sign-ins audited; it replaces the nereus-admins emergency exit.
  • Agents as subjects: Member.spec.kind: agent, a token by OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) with the act claim, and a permission that is the intersection of the person's and the agent's scope; the audit trail records both.
  • Quotas: Kubernetes ResourceQuota object counts first, then a quota reef (Quota, Budget) on the same tenancy nodes; a Team is already a place a quota can attach.
  • Bindings projected into Kubernetes RBAC: the layer below the Nereus API of the pillar "No single control point" (ADR 0015: "the API projects them into the namespaces where a Project runs"), so kubectl is refused too.
  • The Position kind (#1307): skills, level and places; the position's name on a Member becomes a reference to it.
  • Groups mirrored to or from an identity provider: a Nereid writes Keycloak groups from the teams (#1306: an output, never the source).
  • No escalation on bindings: today whoever may create bindings at a node may grant any role there; later, only what they hold themselves, as Kubernetes RBAC's escalate and bind.
  • The model test in make checks: make authorization-model-test needs Docker, which make checks does not use today.
  • nereus environment kubeconfig still reads the kubeconfig (#1638); serving a virtual cluster's credentials through the API is its own decision.

docs.title: 0012. The presentations reef, first slice: drive and follow (J1)
docs.text: The walking skeleton of the presentations reef (ADR 0028, journey #1688): a phone drives a Session's step, another phone and a projector follow it. Crude on purpose: one deck as a blob (a package since #1701), only the talk time, any token with the reef drives (until #1726 made presenting a right of the authorization reef), one API replica.

docs.title: The commands
docs.text:
$ nereus presentations presentation create storytelling --from talks/storytelling.yaml
✓ presentations/presentations/storytelling created, revision 1 (sha256:3f9c2a71)

$ nereus presentations session create platform-day --presentation storytelling --talk 30m
✓ presentations/sessions/platform-day created (revision sha256:3f9c2a71)
  follow: https://nereus.example.com/p/K7Q4

$ nereus presentations session get platform-day
NAME           PRESENTATION   STEP   FOLLOWERS   FOLLOW
platform-day   storytelling   0/24   0           https://nereus.example.com/p/K7Q4

With the room's pace thermometer on from the start (#1723), session get adds its gauge, the taps of the last minute:

$ nereus presentations session create warm-room --presentation storytelling --talk 30m --thermometer
✓ presentations/sessions/warm-room created (revision sha256:3b9880a3)
  follow: https://nereus.example.com/p/M2X9

$ nereus presentations session get warm-room
NAME       PRESENTATION  STEP  FOLLOWERS  FOLLOW
warm-room  storytelling  0/3   0          https://nereus.example.com/p/M2X9

THERMOMETER  TOO SLOW  TOO FAST
on           3         11

$ nereus presentations session get warm-room --output agent > warm-room.yaml
✓ presentations/sessions/warm-room exported (3 slides, 4 questions, 3 feedback answers)
  pace: slide intro 0 slow 1 fast; slide demo 2 slow 14 fast (peak 14:21)

presentation is the reef's default kind (nereus presentations create is the same as nereus presentations presentation create). Each kind has create, get, list and delete, with --dry-run and --examples (ADR 0013).

docs.title: Who does what
docs.text:
phone / projector / follower
        │  POST step (token)        GET follow stream (no token, by short code)
        ▼
  Nereus API ── finds the reef's Nereid through its Mandate (never by name) ──┐
        │  HTTP, inside the cluster only (NetworkPolicy: the API alone)       │
        ▼                                                                     │
  the reef's Nereid: leagore (#1695); its store is PostgreSQL, or memory in scene-core
        │  every PostgreSQL connection: revisions, the Session's row, LISTEN
        ▼
  PostgreSQL, a Database of the database reef (engine postgres)
  • The API holds no database connection (🟠 decision of #1688, settled with a Fable review): it writes spec, and calls the Nereid for everything else. The rule "The API never names a Nereid" keeps the store and its driver behind the Nereid, as the ideas reef does with doris (api/ideas_notes.py).
  • The Nereid writes status (ADR 0005) and holds the one LISTEN connection; each API replica holds one internal stream to it and fans out to its own followers.
  • The short code is given synchronously by the Nereid inside the create request, so session create prints the follow link at once; its reconciler gives the same code to a Session created any other way.

docs.title: The kinds
docs.text:
Presentation (presentations, default kind):

  • spec: description (optional), source (optional, where the YAML came from, informative).
  • status: revision (sha256:<hex>), revisions (the count), slides (the slides of the revision; not steps, a name every Nereid's status takes for its own steps), conditions (Ready), observedGeneration.

Session (sessions):

  • spec: presentation (its name, required), talk (a duration such as 30m, required but for a rehearsal), rehearsal (#1710: true gives no code, so no public link; fixed at create).
  • status: revision (the digest it shows, fixed at create), code (four characters; none for a rehearsal), step, slides, times (#1710: [{name, seconds}], each slide's time on screen, in the deck's order), ended (#1710), conditions (Ready), observedGeneration.

docs.title: The Nereid's HTTP contract
docs.text:
On the controller port of the Nereid's Service, inside the cluster only. JSON in and out, except the deck. leagore serves it over one store interface with two stores: memory (unit tests and make scene-core, which installs no real tool) and PostgreSQL (make scene-presentations and k3d-nereus); one contract test suite runs against both. No reference Nereid: leagore is Nereus's own code, as doris is for the ideas reef (🟠 decision of #1688).

Method and path Body Answer PUT /presentations/{name}/revisions the deck's package (application/x-tar, #1701), at most 1 MB 200 {"revision": "sha256:…", "revisions": 1, "steps": 24}; patches the Presentation's status POST /presentations/{name}/checks the deck's package, a dry run (#1702) 200 {"errors": [...], "warnings": [...], "steps": 24}: every reason the deck engine refuses it (steps null then) and what may not fit the screen; stores nothing GET /presentations/{name}/deck 200 the latest revision as one self-contained page (text/html: style, script and diagrams inline), the speaker's notes included: the offline export (#1703); 404 unknown PUT /presentations/{name}/link {"expires": "2026-12-16T12:00:00Z" | null} 200 {"presentation", "link", "expires"}: the public link (#1704), made on the first put and kept after, the expiry set; 404 with no deck; 400 an expiry that is not an ISO UTC time GET /presentations/{name}/link, DELETE … 200 the link, 204 removed, 404 none GET /links 200 {"links": [...]}, by presentation GET /links/{link}/deck 200 the latest revision as a follower's page (--split, no notes); 410 {"error", "expires"} once expired; 404 unknown GET /revisions/{digest} 200 the package (a J1 revision: its YAML, application/yaml), or 404 PUT /sessions/{name} {"presentation": "storytelling"} 200 the Session's state (below); idempotent; gives the code, fixes the revision, patches status GET /sessions/{name} 200 the state with slides, the slide name, title and message of every step (#1759), and pace, the times of the last ended rehearsal of the same revision or null (#1711), or 404 GET /codes/{code} 200 the state, or 404 POST /sessions/{name}/step {"step": 3} 200 the state with the next sequence, the time since the previous step added to the slide that was on screen (#1710); 400 outside 0..steps-1; 409 once ended POST /sessions/{name}/end 200 the state with ended (#1710): the open slide's time closed; ending again answers the same POST /sessions/{name}/sharing {"on": true} 200 the state with sharing (#1859), the projector showing the follow QR code on any slide while it is on; the next sequence on a change only; 400 anything but a boolean; 404 unknown POST /sessions/{name}/thermometer {"on": true} 200 the state with thermometer and gauge (#1723): while it is on the followers tap Too slow or Too fast; the next sequence on a change only; 400 anything but a boolean; 404 unknown GET /sessions/{name}/thermometer 200 {on, slow, fast}, the taps that count now: each device's latest tap of the last 60 s (#1723); 404 unknown POST /sessions/{name}/open {"part": "questions"} 200 the state with questions_open or rating_open set once (#1876), the next sequence the first time only; 400 a part other than questions or rating; 404 unknown; 409 the questions of an ended Session. The step that reaches the deck's last step also opens the questions of a Session with a questions' time; a step back keeps them, End closes them POST /sessions/{name}/polls/{poll}/open 200 the state with the slide's poll opened (#1722), or reopened once closed (#1917, the answers in stay): poll {name, kind, opened, closes, closed, answers, result}, the next sequence; closes is only the reference (opened plus seconds) and closes nothing; 404 a Session or a poll its revision does not have; 409 a poll open now or an ended Session. An answer's count reaches the followers within a second POST /sessions/{name}/polls/{poll}/close 200 the state with the poll closed by the speaker (#1917), closed its time and result filled, the next sequence; 404 a Session or a poll unknown; 409 a poll not open (never opened, or closed). The end of the Session closes every open poll POST /codes/{code}/polls/{poll}/answers {"device", "answer"} 201 a new answer, 200 one that replaced the device's earlier one, {at, created}; 400 no device's id or none of the poll's options (a choice's index from 0, a scale's value, a text of 1 to 280 characters, trimmed); 404 a code or a poll unknown; 409 before it opens, while it is closed, or at its cap POST /codes/{code}/pace {"device", "vote": "slow"\|"fast"} 200 {vote, at, fades} (#1723): a device's tap, which replaces its earlier one and restarts its minute; kept per (Session, device, step), so the export has the pace by slide; 400 no device's id or another vote; 404 unknown code; 409 while the thermometer is off, once ended or at 20000 taps GET /sessions/{name}/polls 200 {"polls": [...]}: every poll of the deck in its order, with its question, options and seconds, its count, its result once closed and a text poll's texts once closed (the only place, with the export, that holds them) GET /sessions/{name}/questions 200 {"questions": [...]} in arrival order, each with the full device id and the step on screen when it was asked (#1716, #1718; null for a question kept before); 404 unknown GET /sessions/{name}/feedback 200 {count, average, comments: [{text, at}]}, the comments in arrival order (a replaced answer keeps its place), no device (#1717); 404 unknown GET /sessions/{name}/export 200 {session, slides: [{name, title, text, notes, seconds?}], questions: [{slide, text, at}], feedback}: the Session for an agent (#1718), each slide of its revision once in the deck's order (its English text and notes), each question under the slide on screen when it was asked, no device and no code; 404 unknown POST /codes/{code}/questions {"device": "<uuid>", "text": "..."} 201 the question {id, device, text, at, step} (#1716), checked against the Session in the same step as it is written; 400 a device that is no UUID or a text empty or over 280 characters after the trim; 404 unknown code; 409 once ended or at 500 questions POST /codes/{code}/feedback {"device": "<uuid>", "rating": 1-5, "comment": "..."} 201 a new answer, 200 one that replaced the device's earlier one, {id, rating, comment, at, created} (#1717), upserted per (Session, device) in the same step as the Session is checked; 400 a device that is no UUID, a rating that is no whole 1 to 5 or a comment over 280 characters after the trim (empty is none); 404 unknown code; 409 before the end or at 2000 devices DELETE /sessions/{name} 204; the code is free again GET /events text/event-stream: one event: step per change, data the state; a : hb comment every 15 s

The state of a Session:

{"session": "platform-day", "presentation": "storytelling", "revision": "sha256:3f9c…",
 "code": "K7Q4", "step": 3, "steps": 24, "sequence": 7,
 "slide": {"title": "Why a platform", "message": "…"}}

slide is what a follower draws: the current slide's title and its message, read from the deck by the Nereid, never the deck's code. Since #1709 and #1710 the state also has talk, questions, started, moved (when the current slide came up), ended, rehearsal and times, since #1859 sharing, since #1723 thermometer and gauge ({slow, fast}, the taps of the last minute; the followers get thermometer only, never the counts), and since #1876 questions_open and rating_open (when the speaker opened the room's questions and rating, null before: the turns follow the speaker, never the talk's clock); GET /codes/{code} and the events leave times out, and the API sends a follower only the public fields.

  • The digest is sha256: and the hex of the package's bytes as sent (a J1 revision: of its YAML).
  • The package (#1701, cli/src/nereus/deck_package.py) is a deterministic tar (USTAR, entries sorted, no times or owners) of the deck's YAML, every file it names (diagrams, code frames, relative links, the references/*.md it cites; a link to another deck's .html carries that deck's YAML and diagrams) and a package.json manifest at the root: {packageVersion: 1, outlineVersion, deck, files: [{path, sha256, size, origin}]}, where origin is the file's path in its Git repository and its last commit, never a path of the machine. Its root is the closest folder that holds them all, so the YAML travels as written. The Nereid checks every member against the manifest (regular files, relative paths, no ..), unpacks it in an empty folder, refuses a name that leaves it or a file it does not carry, and renders there. A J1 revision, the YAML alone, still parses, and is refused when it names a file.
  • The steps are the deck's slides, in order.
  • The offline export (#1703): the deck engine's own render without --split, one page with its style, script and diagrams inline and the speaker's notes, that opens from file:// with the network off; the portal's CSP does not apply to it. A link to a reference file stays relative, as in the repository's own HTML.
  • The public link (#1704): 26 characters of the code's alphabet (31^26, about 2^128: no rate limit is needed against guessing, though the follow routes' still applies), one per Presentation. It opens the latest revision, as a follower sees it (no notes), until expires; then 410, and a new one is link delete and link create again. Deleting the Presentation deletes its link.
  • A dry run (#1702): the CLI checks the outline's JSON Schema (#1700) before it sends anything, one ✗ line per error with its slide's name; then the Nereid checks what the schema cannot (links, references, the files the package carries, what the engine renders) and gives every reason. A message over 60 characters (docs/agent/decks.md, rule 3) is a warning, !, never a refusal: 242 messages of 25 decks of the repository break it.
  • The code has four characters of 23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ (no 0/O, 1/I/L), unique among the live Sessions.

docs.title: The Nereus API
docs.text:
Route Token What it does POST /v1/presentations/presentations the reef creates the Presentation, then puts the deck in its Nereid; {"name", "package" | "folder" | "deck", "description"?, "source"?}: package is the tar in base64 (1 MB counted on the tar), folder the files of a folder picked in the portal (#1705), {"deck": its YAML's path, "files": {path: base64}}, 4 MB at most, which the API packs as the CLI does, refusing a name that leaves the folder, deck the YAML as text from a CLI before #1701, which becomes a package of that YAML alone. ?dryRun=true has the Nereid check the package (POST /presentations/{name}/checks) and writes nothing: 200 with steps and warnings, or 400 Invalid with errors, every reason. A deck the Nereid refuses at create is the same 400, and the object is deleted again GET /v1/presentations/presentations[/{name}], DELETE …/{name} the reef list, get, delete GET /v1/presentations/presentations/{name}/deck the reef, asked as an apply (the notes are in it) the offline export (#1703): nereus presentations presentation get <name> --output html writes it as <name>.html; served as an attachment, sandboxed, with the follow page's headers POST /v1/presentations/presentations/{name}/link, DELETE … the reef, an apply the public link (#1704): {"expires": "30d"} (hours, days or weeks from now, h/d/w, at most 9999) or no body for one that never expires; answers {name, link, path: "/d/<link>", expires}; 409 AlreadyExists when the Presentation has one; ?dryRun=true writes nothing GET /v1/presentations/presentations/{name}/link, GET /v1/presentations/links the reef get (404 with the fix link create), list GET /v1/presentations/links/{link}/deck none the shared deck: the page leagore renders for a follower, with the follow page's sandboxed headers; 410 Expired once expired, 404 not found for any other link; limited per client as the follow routes POST /v1/presentations/sessions the reef creates the Session, then PUT /sessions/{name} on the Nereid; answers the state and follow: /p/<code> GET /v1/presentations/sessions[/{name}], DELETE …/{name} the reef list, get (with the live step, the followers, the slides of every step, #1759, and the last rehearsal's pace, #1711), delete POST /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/step the reef drives: {"step": n}, answers the new state; 400 outside the slides, 404 unknown (#1696), 409 Refused once ended (#1710) POST /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/end the reef the speaker's End (#1710): answers the state with ended POST /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/sharing the reef drives: {"on": bool}, the drive screen's "Show on the projector" in its Share sheet (#1859); answers the state with sharing, which the followers get, so the projector shows the follow QR code on any slide; 400 Invalid anything but a boolean POST /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/thermometer the reef drives: {"on": bool}, the switch Pace thermometer in the drive screen's Share sheet (#1723), or session create --thermometer from the start; answers the state with thermometer and gauge; 400 Invalid anything but a boolean GET /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/thermometer the reef drives: the gauge {on, slow, fast} (#1723), never cached; the drive screen reads it every 1.5 s while the thermometer is on and shows Too slow and Too fast with their counts; the projector shows nothing POST /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/open the reef drives: {"part": "questions" \| "rating"}, the Questions sheet's "Open questions" and the last step's "Ask the room to rate" (#1876); answers the state, which the followers get; 400 Invalid another part, 409 Refused the questions once ended POST /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/polls/{poll}/open, POST /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/polls/{poll}/close, GET /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/polls the reef drives: the drive screen's "Open question" on a poll slide (#1722), never by itself, its "Close question" and "Reopen question" (#1917), and the speaker's view of the polls with the texts; 404 NotFound a poll the deck has not, 409 Refused an open poll opened again, a poll not open closed, or an ended Session GET /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/questions the reef drives: the audience's questions in arrival order, each device by its six-character label only (#1716); the drive screen reads it every 5 s into its Questions sheet GET /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/feedback the reef drives: the audience's feedback once the rating opened or the Session ended (#1717, #1876), {count, average, comments}, the average to one decimal (null with no answer), no device; the drive screen shows it in its Questions sheet and nereus presentations session get under the Session GET /v1/presentations/sessions/{name}/export the reef drives (the notes are in it): the Session for an agent (#1718), {session: {name, presentation, revision, rehearsal, talkSeconds, questionsSeconds, started, ended}, slides: [{name, title, text, notes, seconds?, questions: [{text, at}]}], questionsWithoutSlide?, feedback, pace}, pace the thermometer's taps by slide, [{slide, slow, fast, peak}] with peak the last tap of the slide's busiest minute (null with no tap), and the session's thermometer (#1723), only the contract's fields of the Nereid's answer, so no device id nor label; nereus presentations session get <name> --output agent prints it as YAML GET /v1/presentations/follow/{code} none the SSE stream by short code (#1696): state first, then step events, id the sequence; retry: 2000 first, an event: hb every 15 s with no event (a named event, since EventSource hides comments from the page's watchdog), Last-Event-ID replays from the last 64 events or sends state; the payload is only code, step, steps, sequence, slide; rate limited per client (429 with Retry-After, also for unknown codes), a cap of followers per process (503, NEREUS_PRESENTATIONS_FOLLOWERS_CAP, default 2000); 404 not found for an unknown code; each device's anonymous id (#1714: a random UUID the follow page keeps in localStorage, no login) comes in the nereus_device cookie, set on /v1/presentations/follow/ only and never in the URL, and the followers are counted by distinct device; a log holds at most its six-character prefix POST /v1/presentations/follow/{code}/questions none a follower's question (#1716), shown by the follow page at the questions' turn only, from questions_open until the end (#1876): {"device", "text"}, the text trimmed; 400 Invalid empty or over 280 characters or a malformed device id, 413 a body over 4 KB, 404 an unknown code, 409 Refused before the questions open or once ended; rate limited per client, then per device (429 with Retry-After); a log holds the code and the device's six-character label, never the text POST /v1/presentations/follow/{code}/feedback none a follower's rating once the speaker asked the room to rate or the Session has ended (#1717, #1876), shown by the follow page from then on: {"device", "rating", "comment"}; 201 created, then 200 configured when the device answers again (its answer replaced); 400 Invalid, 413, 404 as a question; 409 Refused before either; rate limited per client, then per device, in buckets apart from the questions'; a log holds the code and the device's six-character label, never the comment POST /v1/presentations/follow/{code}/polls/{poll}/answers none a follower's answer to an open poll (#1722): {"device", "answer"}; 201 created, then 200 configured; 400 Invalid none of the options; 404 an unknown code or poll; 409 Refused before it opens or after it closes; rate limited per client (polls, loose for a room behind one address), then per device (poll); the followers' state carries the count and, once closed, the result, never a text POST /v1/presentations/follow/{code}/pace none a follower's tap (#1723): {"device", "vote": "slow"\|"fast"}; 200 configured {vote, at, fades}, the follow page marks its own button until fades; 400 Invalid another vote or a malformed device id; 404 an unknown code; 409 Refused while the thermometer is off or once ended; rate limited per client (taps, loose for a room behind one address), then per device (tap)

The follow link the CLI prints joins the installation's address with /p/<code>, the portal's public page (#1697). The public link (#1704) joins it with /d/<link>: the portal's shared.html, where anyone with the link moves through the deck on their own, with every control of the engine.

docs.title: The portal's screens (#1697)
docs.text:
Phone first: each screen is designed for 390 × 844, then checked at 1920 × 1080. All of them run under the portal's CSP, unchanged: no inline script or style, no innerHTML.

Screen Where Token What it does Follow GET /p/<code> on the portal (follow.html, follow.js, follow.css); the code is four characters of 23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ, any other path under /p/ is 404 none EventSource on /v1/presentations/follow/<code> (same origin, never through the portal's forward); draws "step n of N", the slide's title and message, only the last event of a burst; a quiet "reconnecting" mark; opens the stream again after 35 s with no event (an EventSource does not show the : hb comments, so only events reset the watchdog) Projector GET /p/<code>?projector none the same page in a large, full-screen layout, with a full-screen button (Fullscreen API, from a click) and, on the title slide and at the turn to the questions, the QR code of /p/<code> with the short code in large type (#1715); the deck rendered in the portal mode comes with its own sub-issue Drive the Sessions tab: leagore's contract publishes nereus-presentations-drive (ui/drive.js, asset drive.css) on uiPort 8083 the person's lists GET /v1/presentations/sessions, opens one (GET …/sessions/{name}), big Previous and Next: the screen moves at once and the step is posted to …/sessions/{name}/step in the background, in order, a refused one putting the screen back (#1759), the time spent against the Session's talk (a local timer from the first Next; J3 #1707 does it properly), the links /p/<code> and /p/<code>?projector Decks the Decks tab (#1705): leagore's contract publishes nereus-presentations-decks (ui/decks.js, asset decks.css) on the same uiPort the person's lists GET /v1/presentations/presentations; imports a deck from a file (a package .tar, or a YAML alone) or, where the browser has one, a folder (the chosen deck and the files it seems to name); Check posts ?dryRun=true and shows the steps and warnings or every reason the Nereid gives; Create, open only after a clean check, posts the same body

leagore's uiPort serves nothing but ui/: its Service has a second port and its NetworkPolicy opens it to the portal's pods alone, never the controller's port (decks and Sessions), as doris's.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• A01 Broken Access Control: every write needs a token with the reef, and driving a Session the right drive of the authorization reef, held by its speakers (#1726); the follow route is read-only and answers only the state of one Session, by its code; an unknown code says only "not found".
  • A04 Insecure Design: the Nereid's Service admits only the API's pods; the code space (31⁴, about 923 thousand) is enumerable, so the follow route is rate limited per client and reveals no deck.
  • A05 Security Misconfiguration: the portal keeps its CSP with no exception (#1693).
  • No personal data: a follower is anonymous; logs carry the Session's name and code only.

docs.title: Stand-ins
docs.text:
• Any token with the reef drives (J6, #1725): retired by #1726, where only a Session's speakers, or a binding that gives drive on presentations/sessions, drive it.
  • One API replica.
  • leagore's memory store, for unit tests and scene-core only.
  • Until #1695, the API's tests stand a fake Nereid in for leagore.

docs.title: 0013. The Nereids' screens in the portal: the home in a list or a grid, and each Nereid live
docs.text:
Status: Proposed (2026-11-23)

From the owner's session of 2026-11-23, part of journey #1816 (the Nereids' metrics: the standard controller names in the SDK, RED on the phone, ECharts on the desktop). The owner shaped it on a clickable prototype on the phone, kept next to this file: 0013-nereids-screens/prototype.html (invented data, simulated live updates). Raw data in the session's Pontos log; the idea of one metrics layer in the SDK comes from the voice session #pontos/raw/2026-11-17/1731-voice-nereid-sdk-controller-metrics.md.

docs.title: Intent
docs.text:
The portal's home (#740, the status: one row per reef and Nereid) answers "is anything out of the expected?" well, but each row says little next to what the platform knows. The owner wants:

  • the home to show more Nereids at once, and more about each, without losing the "problems first" reading;
  • a tap on a Nereid to open its own screen, with its metrics live, to understand how it is doing now.

The screens follow Material Design 3, as the portal does since #1838.

docs.title: Decisions (owner, 2026-11-23)
docs.text:
• Both home views, with a toggle. The list and the grid each show the Nereids in their own way; the owner keeps both. The switch is an icon-only M3 segmented button (list | grid), on the row of the filter chips, at its right end; the choice is kept in the browser.
  • The filter chips (All, Attention, Ready) apply to both views. They carry no counts: the summary card already says them, and the row fits 340 px only without them.
  • The detail screen shows the four RED signals live, and the Nereid's pods: CPU and memory over time, pods ready over desired, restarts, requests and limits, the last restart's reason, and each pod.
  • Pod data comes from the observability side, never from the Nereus API reading pods. In the owner's words, reading pods would make the API do what belongs to observability. A second opinion (Fable) agreed: in Nereus the object is the Nereid (ADR 0002), the pod is an operation detail.
  • kube-state-metrics enters the metrics reef, in a later slice, limited to pods and deployments (no Secrets). Approved by the owner, after the cAdvisor slice.
  • Out: the domain events and the audit trail of the "observable and auditable Nereids" idea (#pontos/raw/2026-11-19/0236-voice-idea-journey-observable-auditable-nereids.md); no journey covers it yet, and it is not this one.

docs.title: Approaches considered
docs.text:
Home layout.

  • List (today's rows plus a RED line and a sparkline): keeps the reading of today, about 7 Nereids on a phone screen, the reason of a problem in the row.
  • Grid (two columns of M3 cards, one big number and a sparkline each, the attention cards outlined in their colour): about 12 Nereids on screen, the reason left to the detail.
  • Both, with a toggle: chosen by the owner; each answers a different glance.

Where the pods' data comes from.

  • A. The Nereus API reads the pods from the Kubernetes API: no new component, current values only; gives the API new pod-read RBAC (a pod's spec exposes env) and a Nereid-to-pod mapping, and lastState vanishes when a pod is replaced. Refused by the owner.
  • B. kube-state-metrics in the metrics reef, everything through MetricsQL: one more component and a ClusterRole, history for the restart counter, the community's dashboards; the last terminated reason is only a gauge that also vanishes with its pod.
  • C. cAdvisor first, then a minimal kube-state-metrics: chosen. VictoriaMetrics already scrapes each kubelet's /metrics/cadvisor (kubelet-cadvisor in controllers/victoriametrics/victoriametrics.py), which already gives CPU, memory, the limits (container_spec_memory_limit_bytes, container_spec_cpu_quota), restarts with history (changes(container_start_time_seconds)) and OOM kills (container_oom_events_total). kube-state-metrics adds only the requests, ready over desired and the non-OOM restart reasons.

  • While the screen is visible, it refreshes on its own; the "Live" mark and the time of the last update sit in the bottom bar, never at the top centre (docs/agent/decks.md, screens on a phone).

docs.title: The slices
docs.text:
Each slice is one sub-issue of #1816, shipped and shown before the next.

  1. The home's signals, in both views (#744, adjusted): the signals field of each row of GET /v1/status (its contract in #744), the list's RED line and sparkline, the grid view, the chips and the toggle. RED from nereus_nereid_* today; the queries move to controller_runtime_* when #1814 lands.
  2. The detail screen, RED plus cAdvisor (#2176): a new route of the Nereus API for one Nereid's series over a range, the screen, the pods' CPU, memory, limits, restarts and OOM kills from cAdvisor. Done when, in the scene, a Nereid given a low memory limit is OOM-killed and the screen shows the restart and the OOM.
  3. kube-state-metrics in the metrics reef (#2177, done): only --resources=pods,deployments, scraped by the VMAgent; the screen gains the requests, ready over desired and the last restart's reason.

Slice 3's decisions (owner, 2026-11-24): the victoriametrics Nereid releases the upstream chart kube-state-metrics 9.1.0 (v2.20.0, pinned by digest) through the release reef, as it releases the operator, into the operator's namespace metrics-system (a second Target naming it: each Release installs with createNamespace). It reads only nereus-system, through a namespace-scoped Role there (rbac.useClusterRole: false: no ClusterRole, no Secrets, no ConfigMaps), and exposes only the five series the detail route reads (metricAllowlist). Its VMPodScrape keeps the series' own labels (honorLabels: true), so a pod series' namespace and pod join the Nereid's pods as cAdvisor's do. The restarts (per pod now, and their increase over 24h) and the last reason come from kube-state-metrics, cAdvisor's count and OOM kills only where it has no series; ready over desired is the Nereid's Deployment's, named after it. The Mandate's Ready and query.url depend on VictoriaMetrics alone: a kube-state-metrics Release that is not Ready is only logged, and its fields are null in the detail. The admission policy that pins a Nereid's objects now holds several objects of one kind (the operator's and kube-state-metrics's Release) with one rule.

The reefs' icons on the rows and cards are #1773's (each reef has its own icon); until then every row keeps the default icon. The desktop's richer charts are #1815's. Its slice 1 is built: from 1280 px the detail's six cards (the four RED signals, CPU and memory) draw Apache ECharts line charts with axes, a tooltip and an animated change of range, in a grid of three columns; ECharts 6.1.0's official simple build is vendored in the portal and loaded only on a desktop, as a script of the portal's own origin (the CSP is unchanged); below 1280 px, or when it fails to load, the cards keep the SVG charts. The desktop home is its slice 2.

Slice 2 of #1815 is built: from 1280 px the home is a list-detail split, the Nereids' list on the left (420 px, the selected row marked) and slice 1's detail on the right; a row swaps the right pane without leaving the home, and the URL still names the chosen Nereid (#/nereids/<reef>/<nereid>/<range>), so back, forward and a shared link open the split with it selected; with none chosen the pane shows the first Nereid needing attention, else the first row, which the URL does not name; below 1280 px the home and the detail's whole screen are as before.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• The portal reads the series only through the Nereus API (ADR 0018, the API is the one door; ADR 0025, metrics enter only through it); the browser never reaches VictoriaMetrics.
  • One request per signal for all Nereids at once on the home (by (nereid)), never one per row (#744).
  • The series of a Nereid are told by the nereid label the VMPodScrape sets from the pod's app.kubernetes.io/name (never from the series itself). cAdvisor's series carry namespace and pod, not nereid: the API joins them on namespace, pod with a series of the Nereid's own scrape, once, in a function both slices use.
  • Screens on a phone follow docs/agent/decks.md: both languages measured at 340, 360, 390 and 412 px, the controls of a row shrink, nothing live at the top centre.
  • The localStorage read is guarded: a browser that blocks it opens the list view and keeps no choice (the prototype showed a blank page in a sandboxed preview until it was guarded).

docs.title: Calls made while writing (the session's, not the owner's)
docs.text:
From the builder check of this file; the owner may overturn any of them.

  • The join holds over the whole range: a Nereid's pods are replaced (a rollout, an OOM kill), so the join of cAdvisor to the Nereid runs inside the range query (group_left on namespace, pod against the Nereid's own scrape series over the same range), never as an instant lookup that would drop the older pods. The VMPodScrape keeps namespace and pod on every series it scrapes.
  • What slice 2 shows per pod with cAdvisor only: the node from the kubelet's series, the age from container_start_time_seconds, restarts from its changes, and as the last reason only OOMKilled (from container_oom_events_total); any other reason waits for slice 3. The queue depth needs workqueue_depth, so its card says what is missing until #1814 lands.
  • A Nereid is named by its reef and its Nereid, as the rows of GET /v1/status are; the detail route takes both. A row with no Nereid (a reef with only kinds) shows in both views with its state and no numbers, and opens no detail.
  • No scoping by person: the status of the instance's Nereids is the instance's, the same for everyone who may read GET /v1/status today; the queries take no tenant label.
  • 7d fits: the VMSingle keeps 14 days.
  • Missing values are per field: when the metrics Mandate answers but one query fails, only that field is null and its card says so; signals: null stays for "no metrics reef or it does not answer".

docs.title: Not in this design
docs.text:
• A "Reconcile now" action: a write, which needs its own right; its own issue when wanted.
  • A link out to vmui: exposing vmui is the owner's decision in #1816's envelope, and #1815's.
  • Recent events on the detail screen: they would mean reading Kubernetes Events, the same concern as reading pods; they wait for the domain events idea above.
  • Baselines and their colours (#746).

docs.title: Left to the builder
docs.text:
• The exact MetricsQL queries and the step per range (🟠 in #1816's envelope: reported in a batch).
  • The detail route's path and payload, following the API's conventions.
  • The refresh interval of the detail screen, no faster than the metrics reef's scrape interval, 30s, set as the VMAgent's scrapeInterval (controllers/victoriametrics) and read by the API from NEREUS_METRICS_SCRAPE_INTERVAL (seconds, default 30), which must match it (#2187).
  • The M3 tokens of the new components (segmented button, cards, meters), from the portal's app.css.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text: Delete the Nereid, then the cluster and its local registry, so the machine is as it was before init.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Delete the Nereid: nereus nereid delete

nereus nereid delete reference-release
output
✓ core/nereids/reference-release deleted

Delete the cluster, with everything init installed in it:

k3d cluster delete nereus

Delete the local registry init created next to it:

k3d registry delete k3d-nereus-registry.localhost

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• The release command group goes with the Nereid, and its Deployment, Service and identity with it; the reef stays until the cluster goes.
  • No cluster and no registry left.
  • The settings stay in ~/.config/nereus/: a next nereus init --yes creates a cluster that is the same installation, with the same id. Delete that folder to start from nothing.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Learn the words behind what you ran: Reef, Nereid and Mandate.

docs.title: Apply a reef and its Nereid
docs.text: Add the release reef, the reference Nereid that serves it, and the Mandate that makes that Nereid the reef's answer.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Apply the reef, from the version this CLI pins: nereus reef apply release

nereus reef apply release
output
✓ core/reefs/release 0.1.0 created (release.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1: releases, repositories, sources, targets)

Next steps:

  nereus release --help
  nereus nereid apply <nereid> --reef release

Apply the reference Nereid, which answers every command of the reef with no tool behind it: nereus nereid apply

nereus nereid apply reference-release

The CLI reads the reef from the image's label, pins the image to its digest and waits until the Nereid reports Ready; its next step names the Mandate below.

Bind the reef to it, as the reef's default: nereus mandate create

nereus mandate create reference --reef release --nereid reference-release --default

It prints core/mandates/reference created (reef: release, nereid: reference-release, default).

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• The reef release, with its four kinds, and a release command group in the CLI: nereus release --help lists the commands its Nereid published.
  • The Nereid reference-release, running in the cluster as the reef's controller.
  • The Mandate reference, which sends every request of the reef to that Nereid (Reef, Nereid and Mandate).

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Run its commands.

docs.title: Prepare the cluster
docs.text: Create a local k3d cluster and install core on it, from the settings you wrote.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
init needs Docker 20.10.5 or newer with its daemon running, k3d 5.0.0 or newer and Helm 4.0.0 or newer; it checks them first and stops before changing anything when one is missing, naming the version it needs.

Prepare the cluster without being asked to confirm: nereus init

nereus init --yes

It prints the settings table, then one line per step with its time: the prerequisites, the local registry, the cluster, the kinds, the Nereus API and the installation. It ends with cluster ready in context k3d-nereus and names nereus status as the next step.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A k3d cluster nereus, its local registry on localhost:5111, and your kube context pointing at it.
  • Core: the kinds of the model, the Nereus API and the tenancy reef; no Nereid yet.
  • The installation's identity: its name and a random id, which the first init also writes into the settings file, so a cluster recreated from it is the same installation.
  • ~/.config/nereus/values.yaml: the values init passed to Helm, to run the same install by hand.
  • The total time, measured against the SLO: 8 minutes on k3d.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Look around the new installation.

docs.title: Install the CLI
docs.text: Install nereus, the CLI of the platform, on Linux (x86_64 or aarch64); the installer fetches uv when it is missing.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Install the latest release:

curl -fsSL https://getnereus.github.io/install/install.sh | sh

Check that it answers:

nereus --help
output
Usage: nereus [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  nereus: a composable API platform: reefs add the APIs, Nereids look after
  them, installed at runtime.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• nereus, and nrs, the same program under a short name for typing.
  • A CLI that upgrades itself in the background; NEREUS_AUTO_UPGRADE=off turns that off.
  • No cluster yet: the CLI prepares one in the next steps.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Write the settings of your first installation.

docs.title: Look around
docs.text: See what the new installation holds before you add anything: its reefs and the Nereids that look after them.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
See how each reef is doing, one row per reef and Nereid: nereus status

nereus status

On core alone there are two rows, core and tenancy, both Ready.

List the reefs: nereus reef list

nereus reef list

tenancy is the only one, with - under NEREIDS: the Nereus API keeps its objects itself, so no Nereid serves it.

List the Nereids: nereus nereid list

nereus nereid list

There are none yet; the line it prints points to nereus nereid apply --help.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A map of the installation: a reef is a capability with its own API group, a Nereid is the controller that looks after it (Reef, Nereid and Mandate).
  • These commands read the cluster with your kubeconfig, since core alone offers no sign-in; once an installation has the authentication reef, they read through the Nereus API and ask for nereus login first.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Apply a reef and its Nereid.

docs.title: Run its commands
docs.text: Use the release group the reference Nereid published: add a Helm repository and list it.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
See the group's commands; the CLI built them from what the Nereid published, with no code downloaded:

nereus release --help

It lists one group per kind of the reef: repository, source and target, next to the releases themselves.

Add a Helm repository: nereus release repository create

nereus release repository create codecentric \
  --url https://codecentric.github.io/helm-charts \
  --type http
output
✓ release/repositories/codecentric created
NAME         TYPE  URL                                        READY
codecentric  http  https://codecentric.github.io/helm-charts  True

Next steps:

  nereus release source create <name> --repository codecentric --chart <chart> --version <version>

List the repositories: nereus release repository list

nereus release repository list
output
NAME         TYPE  URL                                        READY
codecentric  http  https://codecentric.github.io/helm-charts  True

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A Repository object in the cluster, Ready: the reference Nereid answered it with no tool behind it.
  • The group is named after the reef, not the Nereid: another Nereid of release would serve the same commands (Reef, Nereid and Mandate).

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Clean up when you are done.

docs.title: Write the settings
docs.text: Choose the settings of your first installation and keep them in a file, before any cluster exists.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
See what nereus init would use, and where each value comes from; --dry-run creates nothing:

nereus init --dry-run --create-cluster
output
SETTING            VALUE   SOURCE
target             k3d     default
create_cluster     true    flag
name               nereus  default
ingress_port       8080    default
installation_name  nereus  cluster name
profile            core    default

The table comes first; the two helm upgrade --install lines after it make the same install by hand.

Write the same settings to a file with nereus init --generate-file; it prints the table again and the path it wrote:

nereus init --generate-file --create-cluster

Read the file:

cat ~/.config/nereus/init.yaml
output
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: InitConfig
spec:
  profile: core
  ingressPort: 8080
  undercloud:
    create: true
    name: nereus
---
apiVersion: core.getnereus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Installation
metadata:
  name: nereus
spec:
  alias: nereus

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Two documents: the InitConfig, how this machine builds the platform, and the Installation, whose name never changes (spec 0006).
  • The profile core: core and the tenancy reef, nothing more until you add it (Runtime and profiles).
  • A plain nereus init reads this file; a flag wins over it, and an unknown key is an error.
  • Nothing created yet: no cluster, no registry.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Prepare the cluster from these settings.
